Chr. 1608. nomine Ecclesiae & Scholae Tigurinae scriptas ad Petrum Titum, Ecclesiae Benthaniensis in Silesia Ministrum.
units.tr: Markus Beumler, of Zurich, born in the year of Christ 1555 at Volkensschwil in the county of Kyburg, first minister of the Word at Alzey in the Palatinate, afterwards archdeacon of the cathedral church at Zurich, and at last public professor of both Greek and theology, until he died in the year of Christ 1611. He wrote philosophical and philological works, namely: (1) An analysis of Cicero's Cato Maior, or dialogue on old age, and of Laelius, or on friendship, adapted to the method of Peter Ramus, Speyer 1583; a commentary on Pro Sexto Roscio, Speyer 1595; Plutarch's On the Education of Children, with commentary, Basel 1593 and Arnheim 1606; a Latin grammar, Zurich 1595; analyses of Demosthenes' three Olynthiac orations, Zurich and Frankfurt 1585; Rhetoric of Style, two books, Zurich 1598, much commended by theologians in the practice of the Church, or the art of preaching. (B) Theological works: (1) The Roman Antichrist, or a defence of the disputation of Dr. Georg Sohn (whom German theologians have always greatly esteemed) against the cavils of a certain John of Aquaportia, a priest, Herborn 1599; (2) An outline of theology, methodically and scholastically drawn up and divided into three books, Zurich 1607, which his pupil Dr. Breitinger afterwards reviewed, and illustrated with clear commentaries, John Rudolph Stuck, of whom later; (3) Various disputations: two, one on the person of Christ, the other on the phrases of Scripture when it speaks of Christ, Zurich 1596; b. on the book of nature and of Scripture, from Psalm 19, Zurich 1597; c. three disputations on the authority of the Scriptures, 1. their authority, 2. their clarity, 1605, 3. their perfection, opposed to the sophisms of the Papists, Zurich 1600; (4) a summary of the Helvetic Confession prepared for disputation, Zurich 1606; (5) whether Paul, in Romans 7:7 to the end, speaks of himself as a converted man; (6) on the nature, properties and effects of Scripture; (7) on God the Creator and Preserver; (8) on the knowledge of fallen and restored man; (9) on sin against the Holy Spirit; (10) on the prophetic office of Christ; (11) on the Catholic Church; (12) whether the Church, which embraces and professes the pure prophetic and apostolic doctrine but lacks visible and personal succession, continued from the times of the apostles, is the true Church. An oral disputation with Jakob Andreae at Tübingen on the communication of idioms, 1582, is found in Hospinian's History of the Sacraments, part 2, p. 370 etc. (4) A brief and necessary Apology, in which first are set out the reasons why the hand and tongue of Jakob Andreae are, like Ishmael's, against everyone; then his false accusations against Grynaeus, Markus Beumler and Zwingli, invented by him, are refuted, Zurich 1585; (5) On two questions, namely the sacramental union and the true communion of the body and blood of Christ, against the Synusiasts, and a subtle refutation of the Consensus, two treatises, 1584; b. the true faith of the sons of God, or on the origin, properties and effects of true faith, 1595, in German; (7) An analysis of Jakob Andreae's disputation on the religious adoration of the flesh of Christ, Zurich 1584; (8) Against Jakob Heilbrunner: a true and solid antididagma against the false assertion about the teaching of the Calvinists and Zwinglians, which he published in the year of Christ 1590, Zurich 1593; a solid refutation of the lengthy and false narrative of Jakob Heilbrunner, spread abroad in 1595, on the errors of Calvin and Zwingli, Zurich 1598. His own judgement in manuscript on casuistical questions, written in the year of Christ 1608 in the name of the Church and School of Zurich for Peter Titus, minister of the church at Benthen in Silesia, may also be added.

units.la: Bibliander Theodorus, Episcopi cellä Helvetius, Vir fæcundissimi ingenii, & Theologiæ exegeticæ communis in Helvetia parens, Theologiæ Professor meritissimus, ab an. Chr. 1532. ad 1560. 8. Febr. quo ob præclara merita, rude donatus, lampadem ad tempus vicariam tradidit D. Iosiæ Simlero. Obiit 1564. d. 24 Septembr. quo, sæviente peste, Geneva amisit Calvinum, Marpurgum, Hyperium Tigurum, præterea Christophorum Froschoverum, & Samuelem Pellicanum. Vitoduri inortuus est Ambrosius Blaarerus. Scripta ejus sunt. 1. Theologica Exegetica, in universum penè Veteris Testamenti contextum, quæ Bullingeri, Pellicani &c. aliorumque manu conscriptis & in Bibliotheca Carolina, & in privatis etiam asservantur. Ego habeo in Paraleipomena, Esram, Nehemiam, Estheram & Danielem Conradi Pellicani manu excepta; ejusdem, & alterius, in plure V. T. libros. Huc pertinent Oratio ad enarrationem Esaiæ de sermone Prophetico Tig 1532. Nahum Propheta, Latinè ab eo redditus, adjecta exegesi, Tiguri. 1534. Expositio vaticinii de restitutione Israelis, de instauranda urbe Hierusalem & Templo, terràque dividenda rursus inter tribus, quod ultimis octo capitibus Ezechielis legatur. Inserta Commentariis Pellicani. Evangelica Historia, quam scripsit B. Marcus &c. una cum vita Iohannis Marci Evangelistæ, collecta ex probationibus authoribus; Bas. 1551. Addidit Protevangelium Iacobi, quod tamen scriptum alii, operæ pretium reddidisse non putarunt. Christianissimus, copiosè ex Evangelio S. Marci, Epistolis Catholicis S. Petri, & Prophetarum fonte, Mose Sermo divinæ Majestatis voce pronunciatus in monte Sinai, & ipsius digito inscriptus tabulis lapideis de hominis officio, fine & vera beatudine. Specimen author exhibere voluit instaurandi veterem & sincerissimam Theologiam. 2. Philologica Linguarum. Institutionum Grammaticarum de Ling. Heb. lib. 1. Tig. 1535. De optimo genere Grammaticorum Hebraicorum lib. 1. Bas. 1542. Commentariorum de S. Sancta Lingua Hebraica, hoc est, principe atque parente omnium Linguarum Lib. 24. ἀνέκδοτοι, manu ejus scripti in Carolina custodiuntur Bibliotheca. De numeris, ponderibus, & mensuris divinæ Scripturæ lib. 4. De ratione communi omnium Linguarum & literarum Commentarium, cui annexa compendiaria explicatio doctrinæ recte beatèque vivendi, & religionis omnium gentium atque populorum, Tig. 1548. Neque Iudææ tantùm cancellis includi voluit, Bibliander, ipsam penetravit Arabiam, cujus linguæ beneficio, approbantibus Theologis Tigurinis maximè & Bernensibus, prodiit Emendatio textus Alkorani cum exemplaribus Latinis & Arabicis, addita præfatione editionis illius Apologetica, Basil. 1543. Separatim etiam Præfatio prodiit à Iohanne Fabricio Dantiscano 1638. 3. Historica. Chronologica Temporum à condito Mundo usque, ad ultimam ipsius ætatem supputatio partitioque exactior, accommodata universæ quidem Historiæ, præcipuè libris Prophetarum & Apostolorum. Purgatio scriptorum Oecolampudii & Zuinglii, quâ & acta eorum obiter defenduntur contra Calumniatores, Operibus Zuinglii præfixa est, De ratione temporum Christianis rebus & cognoscendis & explicandis accommodata, lib. 1. una cum alio libro demonstrationum Chronologicarum. Basil. 1551. De fatis Monarchiæ Romanæ, somnium vaticinum Esræ Prophetæ, non conjectatione privata, sed demonstratione Theologica, Historica, & Mathematica. Amplior consideratio decreti Synodalis Tridentini. Basil 1551. Oratio ad illustrissimos Germaniæ Principes & Optimates liberarum atque Imperialium Civitatum, de restituenda pace in Germanico Imperio, caeterisque politiis, deque conservandis sacris & civilibus hominum bonorum coetibus, quos turbare studet Antichristus; & quid opis ad eas res conferant literæ divinæ & humanæ. Ib. 1553. 4. Theologica. Topica tam Didactica, quàm Elenctica, Casuistica, Consilia &c. Consultatio ad Socios nominis Christiani, qua ratione posset ac debeat repelli potentia Turcarum à Christianis. Basil. 1542. Relatio fidelis ad omnium ordinum Reipublicæ Christianæ Principes viros, populumque Christianum, quod à solo verbo, Filioque Dei petenda sit exacta cognitio temporum præsentium & futurorum, & rerum Antichristi, optimaque moderatio Reipublicæ & totius vitæ Christianæ. Basil. 1545. Compendium doctrinæ Christianæ ex Augustino collectum Bas. 1550. Item, quomodo oporteat legere sacras literas, præscriptiones Propheticas, Apostolicas, Theologicas, Imperatorias & Pontificias. Christiana & Catholica doctrina, fides, opera, Ecclesia D. Petri Apostoli, Basil. 1551. Concilium SS. Domini nostri Iesu Christi, Angelorum, Apostolorum, Prophetarum, Regum, Episcoporum & Doctorum excellentium in Ecclesia Dei Catholica in quo demonstratur, quomodo possit ac debeat pereunti populo Christiano succurri per legitimam Ecclesiæ Reformationem. Salomonis sapientissimi Regis sermo de sapientia vera & Christiana institutione. Bas. 1552. Ejusdem de legitima vindicatione christianismi veri & sempiterni libri, Antisophistici, contra sophisticen, hoc est, fucatam & imaginariam & deceptricem sapientiam, Ib. 1553. Ad Iulium III. & cæteros Ecclesiæ Romanæ Præsides, consideratio de Iudæorum & Christianorum defectione à Christo, & Ecclesia, & fide Catholica; itemque de Iudæorum & Christianorum conversione ad Christum Iesum & Ecclesiam Dei sanctam, ac fidem Catholicam Basil. 1553. De summa Trinitate & fide Catholica liber Ib. De mysterio salutiferæ passionis, & mortis Iesu Messiæ expositionis Historicæ libri. 3. Primo exponitur Pascha Ecclesiæ Israëlitæ; secundo Cœna Domini nostri I. Ch. sacro-sancta. Tertio, Missa Ecclesiæ Romanæ meritoria, Ib. 1555. christianismus sempiternus, verus, certus & immutabilis, in quo solo possunt homines beari, ex Act. 2. Epistolæ de Objecto meriti Christi ad Myconium prolixæ MS. alio loco erit usus.
units.tr: Theodor Bibliander, a Swiss born in a bishop's cell, a man of very fertile genius and the common parent of exegetical theology in Helvetia, a most deserving professor of theology. He held the chair from 1532 until 8 February 1560, when, in recognition of his outstanding services, he was granted his discharge and handed the lamp, for the time being, to Mr Josias Simler. He died on 24 September 1564. In that year, while the plague was raging, Geneva lost Calvin, Marburg lost Hyperius, Zurich lost Christoph Froschauer and Samuel Pellicanus. Ambrosius Blaarer died at Konstanz. His writings are: 1. Exegetical theology, covering almost the whole text of the Old Testament. These manuscripts, written by Bullinger, Pellicanus and others, are kept both in the Carolinum library and in private collections. I have, in his Paraleipomena, Ezra, Nehemiah, Esther and Daniel, copied by the hand of Conrad Pellicanus, and other books of the Old Testament in his and another's hand. To this belong: an Oration on the prophetic style, for the exposition of Isaiah, Zurich 1532; the prophet Nahum, translated by him into Latin with an added exegesis, Zurich 1534; an Exposition of the prophecy concerning the restoration of Israel, on rebuilding the city of Jerusalem and the Temple, and on dividing the land again among the tribes, which is read in the last eight chapters of Ezekiel; inserted in the commentaries of Pellicanus. A Gospel history, which he wrote concerning St Mark etc., together with the life of John Mark the Evangelist, gathered from approved authors; Basel 1551. He added the Protevangelium of James, though others, who wrote it, did not think they had done a worthwhile service. Most Christian, drawn at length from the Gospel of St Mark, the Catholic Epistles of St Peter, and the fountain of the prophets; the Sermon of the divine Majesty, pronounced with a voice on Mount Sinai, and inscribed by his finger on the stone tablets, concerning man's duty, end and true blessedness. The author wished this to be a specimen of restoring the old and most sincere theology. 2. Philological works on languages. Grammatical Institutes concerning the Hebrew language, book 1, Zurich 1535. On the best kind of Hebrew grammarians, book 1, Basel 1542. Commentaries on the most holy Hebrew language, that is, the prince and parent of all languages, 24 books, unpublished [ἀνέκδοτοι]; they are kept in manuscript in the Carolinum library. On the numbers, weights and measures of divine Scripture, 4 books. A Commentary on the common nature of all languages and letters, to which is annexed a compendious explanation of the doctrine of living rightly and blessedly, and of the religion of all nations and peoples, Zurich 1548. Nor did Bibliander wish to be confined within the bounds of Judaea alone; he penetrated even Arabia, and by the help of its language, with the approval chiefly of the Zurich and Bern theologians, there appeared the Emendation of the text of the Koran, with Latin and Arabic copies, with an apologetic preface to that edition added, Basel 1543. A preface was also issued separately by Johannes Fabricius of Danzig in 1638. 3. Historical works. A chronological reckoning and more exact division of the times from the creation of the world to its last age, adapted to the whole of history, and especially to the books of the Prophets and Apostles. The Purgation of the writings of Oecolampadius and Zwingli, in which their acts are also incidentally defended against slanderers, is prefixed to the works of Zwingli. On the reckoning of times, suited to knowing and explaining Christian affairs, book 1, together with another book of chronological demonstrations, Basel 1551. On the fates of the Roman Monarchy, the prophetic dream of the prophet Ezra, shown not by private conjecture but by theological, historical and mathematical demonstration. A fuller consideration of the decree of the Council of Trent. Basel 1551. An Oration to the most illustrious princes and nobles of Germany and of the free and imperial cities, on restoring peace in the German Empire and in other states, and on preserving the sacred and civil assemblies of good men, which Antichrist strives to disturb; and what help divine and human letters bring to these matters. Ibid. 1553. 4. Theological topics, both didactic and elenctic, casuistical, counsels, etc. A consultation for the companions of the Christian name, by what means and how the power of the Turks can and should be repelled by Christians, Basel 1542. A faithful report to the princes and leading men of all orders of the Christian commonwealth, and to the Christian people, that exact knowledge of present and future times, and of the affairs of Antichrist, and the best management of the commonwealth and of the whole Christian life, is to be sought from the Word alone and the Son of God. Basel 1545. A compendium of Christian doctrine gathered from Augustine, Basel 1550. Likewise, how one ought to read the sacred letters, the prescriptions of the Prophets, Apostles, Theologians, Emperors and Popes. Christian and Catholic doctrine, faith, works, the Church of St Peter the Apostle, Basel 1551. The Council of our Lord Jesus Christ, of the Angels, Apostles, Prophets, Kings, Bishops and distinguished Teachers in the Catholic Church of God, in which it is shown how the perishing Christian people can and should be helped by a lawful reformation of the Church. The sermon of Solomon, the wisest king, on true wisdom and Christian instruction. Basel 1552. The same author's books On the lawful vindication of the true and everlasting Christianity, anti-sophistic, against sophistry, that is, a painted, imaginary and deceptive wisdom, Ibid. 1553. To Julius III and the other leaders of the Roman Church, a consideration of the defection of Jews and Christians from Christ, and from the Church and the Catholic faith; and likewise of the conversion of Jews and Christians to Christ Jesus and to the holy Church of God and the Catholic faith, Basel 1553. On the supreme Trinity and the Catholic faith, one book, Ibid. On the mystery of the saving passion and death of Jesus the Messiah, historical exposition, 3 books. First, the Passover of the Israelite Church is explained; second, the most holy Supper of our Lord Jesus Christ; third, the meritorious Mass of the Roman Church, Ibid. 1555. Everlasting Christianity, true, certain and unchangeable, in which alone men can be blessed, from Acts 2. Letters concerning the object of the merit of Christ, lengthy, to Myconius, in manuscript; it will be used in another place.

units.la: Beschenstein Iohannes, alias Boesenstein, de quo Geßner, Edit. 1. Biblioth.
units.tr: Johannes Beschenstein, otherwise Boesenstein, concerning whom see Gesner, first edition, Bibliotheca.

units.la: Huc Tigurum, me adhuc puero, Hebraicè docendi gratiâ venit. maticam scripsit Hebraicam 1524. quam habeo.
units.tr: I came here to Zurich, while I was still a boy, for the sake of learning Hebrew. He wrote a Hebrew grammar in 1524, which I possess.

units.la: Boßhart, Laurentius, Canonicus Montis sancti, prope Vitodurum. Eiusdem grammaticum tribuitur fragmentum de Helvetiæ Cantonibus primarijs, quod ad patriæ nonnihil confert Historiæ notitiam.
units.tr: Laurentius Boßhart, canon of Mount St Peter near Winterthur. To him is also attributed a short piece on the chief cantons of Helvetia, which contributes somewhat to knowledge of the history of the homeland.

units.la: Breitingerus, Iohannes Iacobus, Tigurinus, natus 1575. denatus 1645. ad usque ætatis 70. completo. Pastor primùm & primus Zumiconensis; postea Classis in Schola instaurata parallela quartæ præceptor. Inde Collegii Humanitatis Professor Rhetoro Logicus. Minister Ecclesiæ Petrinus, & tandem Templi Majoris Antistes. 1613.
units.tr: Johann Jakob Breitinger, of Zurich, born 1575, died 1645, having completed seventy years of age. First and foremost minister of Zumikon; afterwards teacher of the class parallel to the fourth in the restored school. Then professor of rhetoric and logic in the College of Humanity. Minister of St Peter's church, and finally head of the Great Minster, 1613.

units.la: Multa scripsit facundissimus & solidissimus Theologus: sed pauca edidit. Vulgata sunt 1. Conciones in Orationem Dominicam 2. De die Censorio, rogatu amicorum, conciones in lucem edidit. 3. Tractatus de peccato in sp. S. 4. De Sabbatho. 5. De durations sectarum: an secta seculum excedat? 6. De comœdiis. 7. Arbor Affinitatis, & consanguinitatis, Reipublicæ Tig. praxi potissimum accommodata. 8. πανηγυρικὰ ad Nobilissimam Domum Effingerorum Wildeckenlem. 9. Sermo de Ecclesiarum antiquarum sensu & consensu. 10. Concio in 1.Cor. 10.v.8. & Ioh.c.6. de Cœna Domini. Φάος ἡελίοιο sive splendor solis Orthodoxus, Phosphoro Pontificio oppositus. Edidit etiam Versionem N.T. fontibus proximam. 1628. Cætera sunt ἀνέκδοτα, eáque plurima 1. Conciones in Veteris Testamenti Prophetas, Esajam, & Danielem. In N.T. absolvit omnes, Apocalypsi excepta, quæ illi, ut Gualthero fuit fatalis. Gualtherus enim non attigit: Breitingerus ad finem non perduxit. Quamvis totum jam idea satis comprehendisse videatur opus, quod probant ejus Nuthemata Apocalyptica, scitu observatúque dignissima, quisquis cum fructu cupit & ædificatione Apocalypsin pro cathedra interpretari, quæ ad manum adhuc sunt.
units.tr: This most eloquent and most solid theologian wrote much, but published little. The following were published: 1. Sermons on the Lord's Prayer. 2. On the Day of Judgment: at the request of friends, he published sermons. 3. A treatise on sin against the Holy Spirit. 4. On the Sabbath. 5. On the duration of sects: whether a sect outlasts a century? 6. On comedies. 7. The tree of affinity and consanguinity, adapted chiefly to the practice of the Zurich commonwealth. 8. Panegyrics to the most noble house of the Effingers of Wildegg. 9. A sermon on the sense and consensus of the ancient Churches. 10. A sermon on 1 Corinthians 10:8 and John 6, on the Lord's Supper. Light of the sun [Φάος ἡελίοιο], or the Orthodox splendour, set against the Papist Phosphorus. He also published a version of the New Testament closest to the sources, 1628. The rest are unpublished [ἀνέκδοτα], and very many of them: 1. Sermons on the Prophets of the Old Testament, Isaiah and Daniel. He completed all of the New Testament, except the Apocalypse, which was fatal to him, as it had been to Gualther. For Gualther did not touch it; Breitinger did not bring it to an end. Although the work already seems to have been grasped entire in idea, as his Apocalyptic Nuthemata prove, most worth knowing and observing, for whoever wishes to expound the Apocalypse from the chair with profit and edification, which are still at hand.

units.la: 2. Synopsin Theologicam, vel συνοπτικῶν sanorum sermonum, quam, (Beumleri, quem summa observantia coluit, nec diffiteri erubuit, ad spartam tum in Schola, tum in templo exornandam Beumlerum sibi cotis instar fuisse) συνοπτικῶν secutus, annis 1639. & 40. publicis Lectionibus tradidit, editionemque ejus meritissimo Theologo D. Stuckio, paulo ante obitum, demandavit.
units.tr: 2. Synopsis Theologica, or the συνοπτικῶν [synoptikōn] of sound sermons, which he drew up following the συνοπτικῶν of Beumler, whom he cultivated with the greatest respect and was not ashamed to acknowledge, as a whetstone for sharpening his own skill, both in the School and in the pulpit, to be sharpened by Beumler; he delivered it in public lectures in the years 1639 and 1640, and entrusted its edition to the most deserving theologian D. Stuckius, shortly before his death.

units.la: 3. Sermones Synodales & materiarum varietate, & Methodo tractandi tanto artifice dignissimi. 4. Acta & Decreta Synodi Dordracenæ ab ipso diligentissimè observata, ejusque authoritate & jussu nitidè conscripta. 5. Axiomata quædam Practica Auditoribus publicis communicata. 6. Accurata studiorum Methodus, ad Ioh. Iacobum Wolfium, Patritium, Professorem etiam postea Tigurinum. 7. Iudicia ejus, Propositiones, Consilia publica, privata, in Archivo Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ extant. Brentvvaldius Henricus, studiis in Helvetia feliciter tractatis Academicis, Imbracensisque Præpositus, Historias Helveticas diligenter collegit, quibus se adjutum scripsit Gener ejus, D. Iohannes Stumpfius. Vid. Præfat. in Concil. Constant. ab ipso editam.
units.tr: 3. Synodal Sermons, most worthy of so skilled an artist both for the variety of their matter and for their method of treatment. 4. The Acts and Decrees of the Synod of Dort, most diligently observed by him and written out neatly by his authority and command. 5. Certain practical Axioms, communicated to his public hearers. 6. An accurate Method of study, addressed to Johann Jakob Wolf, a patrician, who later also became a Professor at Zurich. 7. His judgements, proposals and public and private counsels are extant in the Archive of the Church of Zurich. Henry Brennwald, who pursued his academic studies successfully in Switzerland and was provost of Embrach, diligently gathered the Swiss histories; his son-in-law, D. Johann Stumpf, wrote that he was helped by them. See the Preface to the Council of Constance, which he himself edited.

units.la: Bullingerus Henricus, Bremogartensis Helvetius, Capellæ primùm Præceptor, postea 1531. Zuinglii successor tam in Antistitio, quàm Scholarchatû, illius ad an. Chr. 1575. 17. Septemb. æt. 71. hujus 1534. Scripta edidit plurima, quæ cum notis nonnullis Chronicis & Criticis ipse tandem in decem digessit Tomos, quem ordinem & nos, autographum secuturi, proponemus, additis tamen occasionibus ab ipso authore diligenter consignatis, & minori charactere à nobis observatis, aliorum etiam hinc inde judiciis. Primis octo Tomis Didactica exhibet, nono & decimo Polemica. Tomo I. continentur 1. Catechismus pro adulterioribus scriptus de his potissimum capitibus: de Principiis religionis Christianæ, Sacra Scriptura, de Deo vivo, vero & æterno, de fœdere Dei, & vero Dei cultu, de Lege Dei & Decalogo mandatorum Domini; de fide Christiana & symbolo Apostolico; de invocatione Dei & oratione Domini; de Sacramentis Ecclesiæ Christi, 1559. (ita etiam corrigi debet in Edit. Gesner. ult.) ad Ludi literarii Tigurini Magistros. Jussu ab Ecclesia Tigurina Ministris in publica consolatione, scripsi, hanc Catechesin ad usum Scholarium.
units.tr: Heinrich Bullinger, a Swiss from Bremgarten, first a teacher at the Chapel, then in 1531 successor to Zwingli both in the office of antistes and as head of the school, until the year of Christ 1575, on 17 September, at the age of 71; he was born in 1504. He published very many writings, which, together with some chronological and critical notes, he himself at last arranged into ten volumes. We too, following the autograph, will set out this order, adding however the occasions carefully noted by the author himself, and, in smaller type marked by us, the judgements of others here and there. The first eight volumes contain his Didactic works; the ninth and tenth, his Polemical works. Volume I contains: 1. The Catechism, written for young people, chiefly on these heads: on the principles of the Christian religion, Holy Scripture, on the living, true and eternal God, on the covenant of God and the true worship of God, on the Law of God and the Decalogue of the Lord's commandments; on the Christian faith and the Apostles' Creed; on the invocation of God and the Lord's Prayer; on the Sacraments of the Church of Christ, 1559 (so it must also be corrected in the last Gesner edition), written for the Masters of the Zurich Grammar School. Written by order of the Church of Zurich for its Ministers in public consolation, I wrote this Catechism for the use of scholars.

units.la: 2. Compendium religionis Christianæ, X. libris comprehensum, quo continetur simplex & brevis summa fidei nostræ ex verbo Dei petita, in qua perspicuè traditur, quid omnibus ac singulis Christi fidelibus cognitu necessarium sit, quid ab illis credendum, faciendum &c. 1556. ad Vilhelmum Landgravium Hassiæ. Author edidit Germanicè: Simlerus Latinè transtulit, & alius Gallicè. Hac summa volui totum religionis negotium commendare & inculcare fidelibus absque disputatione & contentione simpliciter; adeoque Epitomen quinque Decadum mearum contexere. 3. Sermonum Decades quinque, de potissimis religionis Christianæ Capitibus, in tres Tomos digestæ, variis dicatæ, & diversis editæ temporibus. Sunt autem in Gallicam quoque Linguam conversæ, & impressæ, translatæ item Germanicè per Iohannem Hallerum Bernæ. Quo consilio Decades sermonum scripserim, expono in Dedicatoria Epistola, primis duabus Decadibus præfixa. Decanus Fratribus in agro Tigurino eas dedicavi. 1549. Decadem 3. & 4. dedicavi Eduardo VI. Regi Angliæ, 1550. Quintam verò Henrico Grayo, Marchioni Dorcestriæ 1551. Tom. II. confessio & Expositio simplex, Orthodoxæ fidei & dogmatum Catholicorum, sinceræ religionis Christianæ concorditer ab Ecclesiæ Ministris, qui sunt in Helvetia Tigurì, Bernæ (de Basileensium consensu, videatur Celeb. D. Gernlerus disput. 2. in Confess. Helvet.) Schafhusii, Sangalli, Curiæ Rhetorum, & apud Confœderatos, Mylhusii item & Biennæ. Quibus adjunxerunt se & Genevensis Ecclesiæ Ministri 1566. Latinè & Germanicè ab eodem edita est Authore; Extat etiam Gallicè. Antehac eam Arabicè transtuli. Initio conscripsi hanc Confessionem 1562. & contuli cum P. Martyre, qui probabat plurimùm. In hunc autem finem conscripseram, ut si quando morerer, post me relinquerem fidei meæ Confessionem. Caterùm, cùm Maximilianus II. Imperator anno 1566. Comitia conscriberet, Augustam Vindelicorum, & Illustrissimus Princeps Elector Palatinus, utile & necessarium existimaret, Confessionem habere planam, & à me talem requireret, misi Heidelbergam illam. Quæ cùm Principi placuisset & suis, eámque peteret vulgari, & tum quoque in Helvetia consultaretur de communi Confessione evulganda, hæc ipsa à Ministris inspecta & examinata placuit. Unde communi consensu & nomine Ministrorum Helveticarum Ecclesiarum est edita. Latinè, Germanicè, & Gallicè consentientibus Magistratibus. Passim ei subscripserunt postea Scotiæ, Poloniæ, Hungariæ seu Transsylvaniæ, & aliæ Ecclesiæ agnovere item & Gallicæ cum Anglicis.2. Ecclesias Evangelicas neque hæreticas, neque schismaticas, sed plane Orthodoxas & Catholicas esse Iesu Christi Ecclesias apodixis. Adllust. Principem D. Georgium, Comitem VVittenbergensem & Montisbeligardi 1552. Germanicè etiam ab Authore conscriptus & editus est. l. 3. Antithesis & compendium Evangelicæ & Papisticæ doctrinæ: unde nullo negotio quivis intelligat, quantum inter se hodie partes distent & quid partium quælibet vel probet vel improbet, Latinè & Germanicè 1551. extat. Hos duos libellos scribebam in gratiam ejusdem Principis VVitebergensis, qui hoc à me postulabat. 4. Antiqua fides, sive demonstratio Christianam fidem inde ab initio Mundi durâsse 1537. Inscriptus est liber Germanicè Ioh Henrico VVinckeli Solodorensi, Ex præfecto Dornacensi. Latinitate donatus est à Diethelmo Cellario. Multus erat hoc tempore sermo, quænam esset antiqua & vera fides & rogatus ab optimo Viro Joh. Henrico VVinckeli, Senatore Solodorensi, ut exponerem quænam esset antiqua & vera fides hunc librum composui. 4. Instructio, quomodo illis, qui propter Iesum Christum & Evangelium ejus de fide examinantur, variisque quæstionibus tentantur, respondendum sit, 1559. Germanic. Sed Latinè translulit Iosias Simlerus. Articulis hoc libello respondetur, qui Bavarici vocantur. Augustæ Vindelicorum erant viri boni, qui ad me scribebant, in Bavaria fideles variis divexari quæstionibus, quas ad me mittebant rogantes, ut quid ad eas responderi posset, ederetur. 5. De Testamento seu fœdere Dei unico & æterno, brevis expositio 1534. Germanicè Author scripsit. Multi hoc tempore omnia V. T. rejiciebant. Hi mihi dederunt occasionem scribendi de N. T. 6. Utriusque in Christo naturæ, tam divinæ quam humanæ contra varias hæreses, pro Confessione Christi Catholica, assertio Orthodoxa, conscripta 1534. Claudius quidam Allobrox veniebat Tigurum, & commiscebat in Christo divinitatem cum humanitate, imò negabat utramque: Inde occasionem sumsi scribendi de utraque. 7. S. Vigilii Martyris & Episcopi Tridentini libri quinque pii & elegantes, quos ille ante mille annos contra Eutychen, & alios hæreticos parùm piè de naturarum Christi proprietate & personæ unitate sentientes, conscripsit. Et quos nunc vitâ Auctoris, & argumentis singulis libris præfixis, una cum marginibus, annotationibus illustravit; ad D. Iohannem Travers, Rhetiæ Senatorem 1539. Adjunxit huic operi & evulgavit, ejusdem generis opusculum cui titulus: Orthodoxa & erudita D. Joachimi Vadiani Viri Clarissimi Epistola, quæ hanc explicat quæstionem, an Corpus Christi propter conjunctionem cum verbo inseparabilem alienas à corpore sibi sumat conditiones. Nostro seculo perquam utilis & necessaria scripta est à D. Vadiano ad Henricum Bullingerum 1536. Eodem consilio & Vigilium, & Epistolam D. Vadiani edidi, & quod nonnulli jam, & ipsi etiam Lutherani in hac causa exorbitârunt vehementer. 8. De institutione sacri matrimonii, quando, ubi, quomodo & à quo institutum sit: quid sit, quomodo rite contrahatur, quæ sint ejus causæ, fructus; contrà quàm indecora scortatio & adulterium, de conjugis electione, de fide, amore & officio conjugali, de recta liberorum educatione, German. 1540. Contra immunditiem pro commendatione castitatis & continentiæ hunc librum scripsit, quòd mores hujus seculi id viderentur expetere. 9. Institutio ægrotantium, qua paucis & simpliciter cùm ægrotantes, tum qui ægrotos instituunt docentur, & præparationis ad mortem doctrina continetur. German. 1538. Latinitate donavit Diethelmus Cellarius. Peste hic serpente, orantibus pluribus aliquid in gratiam simplicium pararem, hunc librum conscripsi.
units.tr: 2. Compendium of the Christian Religion, comprised in ten books, which contains a simple and brief summary of our faith drawn from the Word of God, in which is clearly set out what is necessary for all and each of Christ's faithful to know, what they must believe, do, and so on; 1556, addressed to William, Landgrave of Hesse. The author published it in German; Simler translated it into Latin, and another into French. I wished to commend and impress the whole matter of religion on the faithful in this summary, simply and without dispute or contention; and so to weave together an epitome of my five Decades. 3. Five Decades of Sermons, on the chief heads of the Christian religion, arranged in three volumes, dedicated to various people and published at different times. They have also been turned into the French language and printed, and were translated into German by Johann Haller of Bern. The purpose for which I wrote the Decades of sermons I set out in the dedicatory letter prefixed to the first two Decades. I dedicated them to my brethren in the Zurich countryside in 1549. I dedicated the third and fourth Decades to Edward VI, King of England, in 1550; the fifth, however, to Henry Grey, Marquess of Dorset, in 1551. Vol. II: The Confession and Simple Exposition of the orthodox faith and of the Catholic doctrines of the sincere Christian religion, agreed upon by the Ministers of the Church who are in Helvetia: at Zurich, at Bern (on the agreement of Basel, see the renowned D. Gernler, disputation 2 on the Helvetic Confession), at Schaffhausen, St. Gallen, Chur among the Rhaetians, and among the Confederates, likewise at Mulhouse and Biel. To these the Ministers of the Church of Geneva also joined themselves, in 1566. It was published in Latin and German by the same author; it also exists in French. I first wrote this Confession in 1562 and compared it with Peter Martyr, who approved it very much. I had written it with this end in view, that if I should die, I might leave behind me a confession of my faith. However, when the Emperor Maximilian II, in the year 1566, was convening a Diet at Augsburg, and the most illustrious Prince Elector Palatine thought it useful and necessary to have a plain confession, and asked me for one of this kind, I sent it to Heidelberg. When it pleased the Prince and his people, and he wished it made public, and at that time there was also discussion in Helvetia about publishing a common Confession, it was examined and approved by the Ministers themselves. Whence it was published by common consent and in the name of the Ministers of the Helvetic Churches. In Latin, German and French, with the consent of the magistrates. Afterwards it was signed by many, in Scotland, Poland, Hungary or Transylvania, and other Churches acknowledged it, also in French and English. 2. A demonstration that the Evangelical Churches are neither heretical nor schismatic, but plainly orthodox and catholic Churches of Jesus Christ. Addressed to the most illustrious Prince Lord George, Count of Württemberg and Mömpelgard, 1552. It was also written and published in German by the author. 3. Antithesis and compendium of Evangelical and Papist doctrine, whence anyone may understand with no trouble how far apart the parties now stand, and what either party approves or disapproves; it exists in Latin and German, 1551. I wrote these two little books for the sake of that same Prince of Württemberg, who asked this of me. 4. Ancient Faith, or a demonstration that the Christian faith has lasted from the beginning of the world, 1537. The book was inscribed in German to John Henry Winckel of Solothurn, former prefect of Dornach. It was given a Latin dress by Diethelm Keller. Discussion of what the ancient and true faith was was much talked of at this time, and at the request of the excellent man Johann Heinrich Winckel, senator of Solothurn, that I should set out what the ancient and true faith was, I composed this book. [4] Instruction on how to answer those who are examined about the faith on account of Jesus Christ and his Gospel, and are tested with various questions, 1559. In German; but Josias Simler translated it into Latin. It answers with articles which are called Bavarian. At Augsburg there were good men who wrote to me that in Bavaria the faithful were harassed with various questions, which they sent to me, asking that what answer could be given to them be published. 5. On the Testament, or the one and eternal covenant of God, a brief exposition, 1534. The author wrote it in German. At this time many rejected the whole of the Old Testament. These gave me occasion to write about the New Testament. 6. An orthodox assertion of both natures in Christ, divine and human, against various heresies, written in 1534 for the Catholic confession of Christ. A certain Claude of Savoy was coming to Zurich and mixing the divinity of Christ with his humanity, indeed denying both; from this I took occasion to write about both.

units.la: 10. Prosopopœia expostulationis Dei opt. Max. cum Helvetiis, quàm plurima beneficia Dei benignitate eis exhibita commemorantur, ipsíque ad resipiscendum invitantur, indicatis etiam rationibus, quæ ad verum Dei cultum & avitam concordiam eos perduɑturæ erunt 1518. Dum Capella Tigurinorum Ludi-Magister exercuit me inscribendo & dicendo, ut usum aliquem assequerer Linguæ Germanicæ & hunc libellum, ut plures alios, qui nunquam sunt editi, composui: Eum cùm legissent Clarísimi Viri, D. Henricus Brenvvaldius, & Henricus Utingerus curárunt nomine meo expunɛto, ἀνώνυμον imprimi Tigari. Repetita est editio paucis ab hinc annis, quam ceu novam supposititia Editione depravarunt oi ἐξ ἐναντίας; unde nata occasio Viro de Schola & Ecclesia nostra meritissimo, D. Johanni Wirzio, S.S. Theologiæ Doctori non modo scriptū ab illatis corruptelis vindicandi; sed & pleniùs illustrandi,& pleraque capita controversa doctè percurrendi. Libri titulus: Rettung der Anklag Gottes. Tom. III. 1. Festorum dierum Domini & Servatoris I. Ch. Sermones Ecclesiastici 24. Vbi Lector plenam ferè & continuam I.Ch.D N. Historiam, Incarnationis ejus, Nativitatis, Circumcisionis, Revelationis, Passionis & Mortis, denique Resurrectionis ex mortuis, & Ascensionis in cœlum, missionisque Sp. S. & quis inde ad nos fructus redeat, quæ vicissim illi debeamus officia. His præmissa præfatio de Sabbatho & feriis Christianorum 1554. Rogatus à multis Ecclesiarum Pastoribus, Doctoribús q. hanc operam sumsi, quò sincerius inferiis istiu prædicaretur Christus. 2. Sermones duo de officio Magistratus & subditorum; item de jurejurando ad Amplis. Virum Georgium à Stetten, Patricium Augustanum 1564. 3. De vera hominum peccatorum pœnitentia, & amplissima DEI erga eos misericordia. Homiliæ tres in duo postrema capita Ionæ, habitæ Tiguri mense Octob. 1552. Cùm Prophetas minores XII. pro concione publicè exponerem, & incidissem in hæc Jonæ Capita, orárunt me Viri boni, ut Conciones conscriptas ederem. Id quod feci. Eadem de causa, eóque consilio, reliquisermones sunt vulgati, a, de conversione hominis ad DEUM, conciones sex in caput octavum Actorum, de Conversione Eunuchi, ad D. Philippum Marschallum hæreditarium à Bappenheim 1568. b. Conciones duæ in Cap. 17. Matth. de Christi transfiguratione, & glorificatione fidelium in vita æterna: Item Iesum christum, verum esse Messiam 1552. c. De vero auxilio & liberatione ex omnibus periculis, ex Matth. 14. 1552, quo anno 12. Iulii fuit habi-
units.tr: 10. Prosopopoeia of the expostulation of God Almighty with the Helvetians, in which the very many benefits that God in his kindness has shown them are recalled, and they are invited to repentance, with the reasons also indicated that will lead them to the true worship of God and to their ancestral concord. 1518. While the schoolmaster of the Chapel of Zurich (Kappel) had me practise writing and speaking so that I might gain some facility in the German language, I composed this little book, as I did several others that were never published. When the most distinguished men, Mr Henry Brennwald and Henry Utinger, had read it, they saw to it that it was printed at Zurich anonymously, with my name removed. The edition was reissued a few years ago, but those of the opposite side [ἐξ ἐναντίας] corrupted it by passing it off as a new, supposititious edition. This gave the occasion to Mr John Wirz, Doctor of Sacred Theology and most deserving of our school and church, not only to vindicate the writing from the corruptions introduced, but also to illustrate it more fully and to treat learnedly many of the controverted chapters. Title of the book: Rettung der Anklag Gottes. Vol. III. 1. Sermons for the festival days of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, 24 ecclesiastical sermons, in which the reader has an almost full and continuous history of our Lord Jesus Christ: his incarnation, nativity, circumcision, revelation, passion and death, and finally his resurrection from the dead, ascension into heaven and the sending of the Holy Spirit, and what fruit comes from these to us, and what duties in turn we owe him. Prefaced by a preface on the Sabbath and the feast days of Christians, 1554. Asked by many ministers of the churches and by teachers, I undertook this work, so that Christ might be preached more sincerely at these festivals. 2. Two sermons on the office of the magistrate and of subjects; likewise on the oath, addressed to the most distinguished man, Georg von Stetten, patrician of Augsburg, 1564. 3. On the true repentance of sinful men and the most abundant mercy of God towards them. Three homilies on the last two chapters of Jonah, delivered at Zurich in October 1552. When I was publicly expounding the twelve minor prophets to the congregation and had come to these chapters of Jonah, good men urged me to publish the sermons in writing, which I did. For the same reason, and with the same intention, the remaining sermons were published: a. On the conversion of man to God, six sermons on the eighth chapter of Acts, on the conversion of the eunuch, addressed to Mr Philip Marschall, hereditary marshal of Bappenheim, 1568. b. Two sermons on Matthew 17, on the transfiguration of Christ and the glorification of the faithful in eternal life; likewise that Jesus Christ is the true Messiah, 1552. c. On true help and deliverance from all dangers, from Matthew 14, 1552, in which year it was delivered on 12 July. [continued on the next unit]

units.la: sa d. De vera & constanti fide in omnibus periculis & tentationibus, concio ex 15. Cap. Matth. 1552. habita 14. Augusti. De Cœna DOMINI nostri Iesu Christi, ejus institutione & præparatione, ad rectè eam sumendam, Conciones duæ 1555. Ludov. Lavaterus in Latinam Linguam transtulit. de salute fidelium, quomodo scil. ab origine salus hominibus per Verbum Dei & Sacramenta annunciata fuerit 26. Maji 1555. de veris Sacrificiis Christianorum, Concio ex 13. Cap. Epist. ad Hebr. 14. Aug. 1552. Hunc sermonem Latinum fecit D. Johannes Parkurstus, Nordovicensis in Anglia Episcopus: sed non est, quod ego sciam, excusus. de extremo judicio conciones duæ in c. 25. Matth. 1559. De summo gaudio, summoque luctu extremi diei, qua Christus ad judicandum vivos & mortuos veniet, & vocatis ad se fidelibus æternam felicitatem largietur, infideles vero repudiatos, perpetuæ damnationi addicet fidelis admonitio & consolatio ad N. V. Georgium à Stetten 1570. de fine sæculi & judicio futuro D. N. I. Ch. deque periculis nostri hujus sæculi corruptissimi gravissimis; & qua ratione fiant innoxia piis orationes duæ. Exponuntur verba Servatoris Matth. 25. De fine sæculi & judicio extremo. Verba item Danielis c. 7. de regno turbulentissimo & fine ejus; denique Apostoli verba, 2. Tim. 3. de extremis sæculi periculis; de Scripturæ Sacræ plenitudine ac præstantia; Basil. ab Oporino 1539. quod & petiit ab illo. De Prophetæ officio, & quomodo digne administrari possit; Oratio, in qua iterum celebratur laus D. Huldrici Zuinglii, Pastoris Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ 1537. In die Caroli, mox à Clade Capellana, hanc orationem habui. Adhortatio ad Ecclesiæ Christi Ministros omnes, ut abjectis controversiis Christum solum, ac veram in ipsum fidem & vitæ resipiscentiam concorditer & simpliciter prædicent. Latinè translatit Simlerus 1572. Quando adhortationem hanc scribebam, fervebant passim in Ecclesia plurima de Capitibus religionis certamina, multique Ministri ex Cathedra sacra proniores erant ad convitiandum, & rixandum, quàm ad docendum. Unde ad Ecclesiæ solatium hanc edidi. Turca, id est, de origine religionis Turcicæ sive Muhammedanæ; Turcarum, eorum Imperatoribus, & ampliatis intra 266. pomœriis, obtentisque contra Christianos victoriis. Libellus hic Matthiæ Erbii Pastoris Rotevillani in Alsatia Ministri nomine prodiit; quia ab illo fuit inchoatus, à Bullingero recognitus, auctus, Germanicè editus ad Generosum D. à Rappoltstein 1566. De persecutionibus, quas Ecclesia Christi patitur, & illarum causis, & pœnis persecutorum 1573. Latinè vertit Iosias Simlerus, Gallicè Ioh. Baptista Myllerus, Rhætus. In Gallia contra spem omnium Guysiana familia, Lotharingica opera potissimum, per derepentinam proditionem nem nem excitata est persecutio (quam latrocinium parricidale plerique vocant) quâ non tam Principes Viri & Nobiles Evangelici plurimi, quàm ex plebe per universum regnum aliquot fidelium millia sunt interemta atque interfecta crudelissimé. Inde cùm infirmiores plurimi offenderentur, & titubarent nonnihil in vera religione, hunc tractatum edidi ad institutionem & consolationem. p. Homilia duæ Consolatoriæ in Psal. 130. & 133. Germanicè, 1574.
units.tr: d. On true and steadfast faith in all dangers and temptations, a sermon on Matthew 15, delivered on 14 August 1552. On the Lord's Supper of our Lord Jesus Christ, its institution and the preparation for receiving it rightly, two sermons, 1555. Ludwig Lavater translated them into Latin. On the salvation of the faithful, namely how salvation has been announced to men from the beginning through the Word of God and the sacraments, 26 May 1555. On the true sacrifices of Christians, a sermon on Hebrews 13, 14 August 1552. Mr John Parkhurst, bishop of Norwich in England, made a Latin version of this sermon, but so far as I know it was not printed. On the last judgment, two sermons on Matthew 25, 1559. On the great joy and the great sorrow of the last day, on which Christ will come to judge the living and the dead, and will bestow eternal happiness on the faithful called to him, but will consign the unbelievers, who are rejected, to everlasting damnation: a faithful admonition and consolation, addressed to the honourable Georg von Stetten, 1570. On the end of the age and the future judgment: two prayers on our Lord Jesus Christ and on the most grievous dangers of this most corrupt age, and by what means they are made harmless to the pious. The words of the Saviour in Matthew 25 are expounded, On the end of the age and the last judgment. Likewise the words of Daniel chapter 7, on the most turbulent kingdom and its end; and finally the words of the Apostle, 2 Timothy 3, on the extreme dangers of the age. On the fullness and excellence of Holy Scripture, published by Basilius Oporinus at Basel, 1539, which he also asked of him. On the office of the prophet and how it may be administered worthily. An oration in which the praise of Mr Huldrych Zwingli, minister of the Church of Zurich, is again celebrated, 1537. I delivered this oration on the day of Charles, immediately after the defeat at Kappel. An exhortation to all ministers of the Church of Christ, that, setting aside controversies, they should preach Christ alone, and true faith in him and repentance of life, in harmony and simply. Translated into Latin by Simler, 1572. When I was writing this exhortation, very many contentions about the chief points of religion were raging everywhere in the Church, and many ministers from the sacred pulpit were more inclined to revile and quarrel than to teach. For that reason I published this for the comfort of the Church. The Turk, that is, on the origin of the Turkish or Muhammadan religion, and of the Turks, their emperors, and the extension of their borders into 266 [sic], and the victories they won against Christians. This little book was issued under the name of Matthias Erbius, minister at Rouffach in Alsace; because he began it, and Bullinger revised and enlarged it and published it in German, addressed to the noble Lord of Rappoltstein, 1566. On the persecutions that the Church of Christ suffers, and their causes, and the punishments of the persecutors, 1573. Josias Simler translated it into Latin, and John Baptist Muller of the Grisons into French. [Note: quotation of the French preface follows:] In France, contrary to the hope of all, the Guise family, chiefly by Lorraine's work, stirred up a persecution by a sudden treachery (which most people call the parricidal robbery), by which not only many of the evangelical princes and nobles, but several thousand faithful from the common people throughout the whole kingdom were most cruelly slain and killed. Since many of the weaker sort were offended and wavered somewhat in the true religion, I published this treatise for instruction and consolation. p. Two consolatory homilies on Psalms 130 and 133, in German, 1574.

units.la: Tom. IV. 1. Præfatio in Biblia Latina nova Tiguri 1544. impressa, de operis ejus instituto, & ratione ad Christianum Lectorem; de omnibus Scripturæ libris, eorúmque præstantia expositio ad Lectorem. Cùm Biblia edenda essent ex versione Leonis Judæ, Theodori Bibliandri, Petri Cholini, & Rodolphi Gualtheri, hanc præfationem præfixi. 2. Epitome temporum & rerum ab orbe condito ad primum usque annum Iothan Regis Judæ, in qua perspicuè attinguntur, quæ pertinent ad S. literas illustrandas, & ad veram, antequámque religionem, & ejus certitudinem, progressum item & mutationem cognoscendam: una cum sex tabulis Chronicis à temporibus Iothan usque ad excidium urbis Hierosolymorum deductis, potissimùm pertinentibus ad expositionem Danielis Prophetæ. Multis quidem annis & laboribus in hoc negotio laboravi, tandem ex omnibus meis laboribus hanc partem cum æquis lectoribus communicare volui, nemini invidens, si certiora pertulerit, meâque hac præteriens meliora receperit. Hac enim ejusmodi res est, ut nemo statim sibi in hoc argumento per omnia fecerit satis. 3. Daniel, sapientissimus Dei Propheta, qui à vetustis Polyhistor, 1. e multiscius dictus est, expositus homiliis 66. quibus non tam sensus Prophetæ redditur, quàm usus & fructus Prophetæ ostenditur, adeóque omnibus in Ecclesia docentibus commonstratur, quômodo perspicuè, justo ordine, & cum utilitate populo Dei hic Propheta prædicari posit: ad quinque Angliæ Episcopos 1565. & 1579. cui Editioni Epitome temporum accessit. Pro publicis Concionibus in Templo Danielem, Jesajam, & Jeremiam exposui populo, eáque, quæ viva voce explicui, in literas etiam retuli, & ut præconcs verbi juvarem conciones has edidi.
units.tr: Vol. IV. 1. Preface to the new Latin Bible printed at Zurich in 1544, on the design of that work and its method, to the Christian reader; an exposition of all the books of Scripture and their excellence, addressed to the reader. When the Bible was to be published in the translation of Leo Jud, Theodor Bibliander, Peter Cholin and Rudolf Gwalther, I prefixed this preface. 2. An epitome of the times and events from the creation of the world to the first year of Jotham, king of Judah, in which are clearly touched upon the matters that pertain to the illustration of the sacred letters and to the knowledge of the true and ancient religion, its certainty, its progress and its change; together with six chronological tables, drawn from the times of Jotham to the destruction of the city of Jerusalem, pertaining chiefly to the exposition of the prophet Daniel. I laboured for many years and with great effort in this business, and at last I wished to share this part of all my labours with fair readers, begrudging no one, if he has brought more certain things, and if, passing over my work, he has received better. For this is the kind of matter in which no one at once has done enough for himself in every respect. 3. Daniel, the most wise prophet of God, whom the ancients called a polyhistor, that is, very learned, expounded in 66 homilies, in which not so much the sense of the prophet is rendered as the use and fruit of the prophet is shown, and thus it is shown to all who teach in the Church how this prophet may be preached plainly, in right order and with profit to the people of God: addressed to five English bishops, 1565 and 1579, to which edition the epitome of the times was added. For the public sermons in the temple I expounded Daniel, Isaiah and Jeremiah to the people, and I have also set down in writing what I explained by the living voice, and, as an aid to those who proclaim the Word, I have published these sermons.

units.la: Tom. V. 1. Isajas, excellentissimus Dei Propheta, cujus testimoniis ipse Deus Christus & Apostoli creberrimè usi leguntur, expositus 1590. Homiliis, quibus non tam sensus Prophetæ redditur, quàm usus & fructus ejus in Ecclesia Dei ostenditur, ad Illust. Principem ac Dominum, D. Philippum Seniorem, Hassiæ Landgravium 1567. 2. Jeremias fidelissimus, & laboriosissimus Dei Propheta expositus per Henricum Bullingerum Concionibus 170. quibus perspicuè & verè docetur, quòd hodie multis Comitiis, & consultationibus nondum inveniri potuit, quomodo nempe bellis compositis infelicibus, tranquillitas in orbe Christiano recuperari, & pax, salusque publica, conservari posit. Mirificè enim pleraque hujus Prophetæ nostris temporibus, hominibusque congruit. Ad Ampliss. Virum VVolphgangum VVaidnerum, VVormatiensem.
units.tr: Vol. V. 1. Isaiah, the most excellent prophet of God, whose testimonies Christ God himself and the Apostles are read to have quoted very often, expounded in 1590 in homilies, in which not so much the sense of the prophet is rendered as its use and fruit in the Church of God are shown, to the illustrious prince and lord, Philip the Elder, Landgrave of Hesse, 1567. 2. Jeremiah, the most faithful and most laborious prophet of God, expounded by Heinrich Bullinger in 170 sermons, in which it is clearly and truly taught how, at a time when many assemblies and consultations have not yet been able to find it, peace and public safety may be preserved and tranquillity recovered in the Christian world once unhappy wars are ended. For many of this prophet's passages fit our own times and our own people remarkably well. To the most distinguished man, Wolfgang Waidner of Worms.

units.la: Diversis temporibus, & intervallis scripta, & edita sunt hæ conciones in Jeremiam. Nam prodierunt in publicum an. 1557. Conciones 26. in sex Prophetæ capita; anno 1558. Conciones 26. à 7. Cap. usque ad 14. Rursus 1559. à c. 14. usque ad 30. Conciones 44. Postremo an. 1562. à c. 30. ad finem Conc. 74. Habet itaque prima Editio diversos titulos. Ego verò hunc præsentem compositi, ut si quando omnes conciones imprimantur in unum volumen, operi universo hic præfigatur titulus, qui in hoc scriptus est ordine. 3. Threnorum seu lamentationum Ieremiæ brevis explicatio, qua causæ ostenduntur, cur præclaræ urbes & regna potentia intereant; & ne intereant salutaria adhibet optimus medicus medicamenta, ad D. Steigerum Reipublicæ Bernensis Senatorem, & Quæstorem.
units.tr: These sermons on Jeremiah were written and published at different times and intervals. For they came out publicly in 1557: 26 sermons on the first six chapters of the prophet; in 1558, 26 sermons from chapter 7 to chapter 14; again in 1559, from chapter 14 to chapter 30, 44 sermons; lastly, in 1562, from chapter 30 to the end, 74 sermons. The first edition therefore has different titles. I, however, have prepared this present one, so that if ever all the sermons are printed in one volume, a single title may be placed at the head of the whole work, written in the following order. 3. A short explanation of the Lamentations, or Threnes, of Jeremiah, in which the causes are shown why famous cities and powerful kingdoms perish, and in order that they may not perish, the best physician applies wholesome remedies; to Master Steiger, senator and treasurer of the Republic of Bern.

units.la: Tom. VI. 1. In Sacro-Sanctum Iesu Christi Evangelium secundum Matthæum commentariorum lib. 12. ad Clariss. Viros, D. Iohannem Habium, & Diethelmum Royftium, urbis Tigurinæ Consules. 1542. Non semel cursum (ut ita dicam) librorum Novi Testamenti, pro publicis concionibus, & in prælectionibus, absolvi. Ex omnibus autem meis laboribus hos Commentarios selegi, & in gratiam studiosorum diversis temporibus evulgavi. 2. In S. Marcum Commentar. lib. 6. ad industrium virum, D. Christophorum Froschoverum, Typographhum & civem Tigurinum 1545. 3. In luculentum, & sacro sanctum Evangelium secundum Lucam Comment. Libb. 9. ad D. VVelserum clarissimæ urbis Augustæ Vindelic. Consulem 1546. 4. In divinum Evangelium secundum Iohannem Comment. lib. 10. ad Amplis. Virum, D. Ioh. Rodolphum Lavaterum, Tigurinæ urbis Senatorem, & Quæstorem 1543. Hos Commentarios scriptis ad me literis Philipp. Melanchthon laudavit. 5. In Acta Apostolorum Comment. libb. 6. quibus exponitur, quæ fuerit S. Ecclesiæ infantia, qui auctus, quæ Ecclesiæ justæ facies, quæ doctrina Apostolorum, qui veteris Ecclesiæ ritus, quæ studia, religio, fides, ad Senatum populumque Francofurtensem ad Mœnum 1553. Hi postea libri ab authore recogniti, denuo fuerunt Tiguri recusi 1583. 6. series & sigillo temporum & rerum, à B. Luca in Actis Apostolorum descriptarum. In qua continentur primum quidem adumbratio Ecclesiæ & doctrinæ Apostolicæ. Deinde electissimi Dei organi, Sancti Pauli, magni illius Asiæ & Europæ Doctoris celeberrimi, labores & ærumnæ. Postremo omnium Regum Herodianorum & omnium Præsidum Iudæorum, omniumque Cæsarum Romanorum, qui Apostolorum; Pauli maximè seculo vixerunt, series & Historia brevis. Ad fidelissimum Ecclesiæ Dei Ministrum D. Rodolphum Gualtherum 1544. Adjeci libellum hunc Actis Apostolorum & Epistolis Paulinis veluti coronidem.
units.tr: Vol. VI. 1. Commentaries in 12 books on the most holy Gospel of Jesus Christ according to Matthew, to the most distinguished men, Johann Haab and Diethelm Roist, consuls of the city of Zurich, 1542. I have not once, so to speak, completed the course of the books of the New Testament, both for public sermons and in lectures. Of all my labours, however, I have chosen these commentaries and published them at various times for the benefit of students. 2. Commentary on St Mark in 6 books, to the diligent man Christoph Froschauer, printer and citizen of Zurich, 1545. 3. Commentary on the brilliant and most holy Gospel according to Luke in 9 books, to Master Welser, consul of the most famous city of Augsburg in Vindelicia, 1546. 4. Commentary on the divine Gospel according to John in 10 books, to the honourable man Johann Rudolf Lavater, senator and treasurer of the city of Zurich, 1543. Philipp Melanchthon praised these commentaries in a letter written to me. 5. Commentary on the Acts of the Apostles in 6 books, in which it is set out what the infancy of the holy Church was, how it grew, what the true face of the Church was, what the teaching of the Apostles was, what the rites, pursuits, religion and faith of the ancient Church were; to the Senate and people of Frankfurt on the Main, 1553. These books were afterwards revised by the author and reprinted at Zurich in 1583. 6. A series and seal of the times and events described by St Luke in the Acts of the Apostles. In it are contained, first, a sketch of the Church and of apostolic doctrine; then the labours and hardships of St Paul, that most famous teacher of Asia and Europe, the most chosen instrument of God; lastly, a brief series and history of all the Herodian kings, all the governors of the Jews, and all the Roman Caesars who lived in the age of the Apostles, and especially of Paul. To the most faithful minister of God's Church, Master Rudolf Gwalther, 1544. I have added this little book to the Acts of the Apostles and the Pauline Epistles as a kind of crown.

units.la: Tom. VII. 1. In omnes Apostolicas S. Pauli Epistolas XIV. Commentarii. Hi uno in opere vel volumine sunt editi 1539. Alioquin scripsi diversis temporibus, & diversis dicati viris honoratis. In Epistolam ad Hebraeos 1532. Romanos 1533. Priorem ad Corinthios 1534. Posteriorem ad Corinthios, ad Galatas, Ephesios, Philippenses, Colossenses 1535. Ad Thessalon. Timoth. Tit. 1536. Philemonem 1537. 2. In Epistolas Apostolorum Canonicas lib. 7. Comment. etiam diversis temporibus, & ad diversos scripti, 1539. Jacobi 1537. Petri utramque 1534. 1. Johannis 1532. 2. & 3. Johann. Judæ 1537. 3. In Apocalypsin Iesu Christi, revelatam quidem per Angelum Domini, visam vero & exceptam atque conscriptam à Iohanne Apostolo & Evangelista, Conciones C. 1557. Versæ sunt in Germanicam Linguam à Ludovico Lavatero, præterea translatæ sunt ab aliis in Linguam Gallicam, Anglicam & Polonicam. Magni semper hoc Scriptum à Theologis fuit æstimatum. sub finem (ita ipse scribit Bullinger in vita sua ἀνεκδότῳ ad an. Chr. 1565.) Julii scribit ad me M. Antonius Clofelius, Jesuita, Concionator Aulicus; Archiducis Austriæ Ferdinandi; Quod ex libris meis, Apocalypticis maximè concionibus conversus statuerit deserere locum suum, & transfire ad nos, ac elapsus aufugit ab aula. Celeberrimus fuit Jesuita.
units.tr: Vol. VII. 1. Commentaries on all fourteen Apostolic Epistles of St Paul. These were published together in one work or volume in 1539. Otherwise I wrote them at various times and dedicated them to various honourable men. On the Epistle to the Hebrews, 1532; Romans, 1533; the First Epistle to the Corinthians, 1534; the Second to the Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians and Colossians, 1535; to the Thessalonians, Timothy and Titus, 1536; Philemon, 1537. 2. Commentaries in 7 books on the Catholic Epistles of the Apostles, also written at different times and for different persons, 1539: James, 1537; Peter, both epistles, 1534; 1 John, 1532; 2 and 3 John, Jude, 1537. 3. On the Apocalypse of Jesus Christ, revealed indeed by an angel of the Lord, but seen, received and written down by John the Apostle and Evangelist, 100 sermons, 1557. It has been turned into German by Ludwig Lavater, and has also been translated by others into French, English and Polish. This writing has always been held in high esteem by theologians. Towards the end of July (so Bullinger himself writes in his unpublished autobiography [ἀνεκδότῳ], under the year of Christ 1565) Master Antonius Clofelius, a Jesuit and court preacher of the Archduke Ferdinand of Austria, wrote to me that, having been converted by my books, especially my sermons on the Apocalypse, he had resolved to abandon his post, to come over to us, and had secretly fled from the court. He was a most distinguished Jesuit.

units.la: Tom. VIII. 1. Præfatio christianorum, i. e. Iesum Christum, Dominum nostrum à Patre cœlesti datum esse Mundo Salvatorem, in quo fideles velati in compendium redacta habeant omnia quæ ad veram pietatem discendam, vitamque verè beatam consequendam & retinendam pertinent. Ita ut nihil sit opus ea aliunde colligere, ad Christianissimum eundémque potentissimum Francorum Regem Henricum II. demonstratio, 1552. Hunc libellum scribebam, cùm Rex Francorum cum Duce Mauricio de reliquis Germanis principibus conspirârunt, pro liberatione captivorum Principum Saxonis & Hassi. Libellum mittebam ad Regem per Capitaneum Sebastianum Schertelinum. 2. De Scripturæ S. authoritate, certitudine & absoluta perfectione: Déque Episcoporum, qui verbi DEI Ministri sunt, institutione & unctione, contra superstitionis tyrannidisque Romanæ Antistites, ad Serenissimum Angliæ Regem Henricum VIII. lib. 2 1538. Cùm Angli, Viri pii & docti studiorum gratiâ in Helvetiam venissent, & quidam eorum meo uterentur hospitio, omnésque affirmarent, hodie nulla de re uberiori cum fructu Angliæ scribi posse, quàm de Scriptura & Episcopis, sumsi hoc laboris mihi veritatis studio, & hos duos libros conscripsi, & ad Regem impressos misi. 3. De gratia justificante propter Christum, per solam fidem, absque operibus bonis, fide interim exuberante in opera bona lib. 4. ad Serenissimum Daniæ Regem Christianum. Disseritur in his de gratia DEI, de redemptione per Christum, de fide vera, qua Christus recipitur, & quæ nobis ad justitiam imputatur. Quomodo hæc sola absque operibus justificare dicatur: de operibus Legis & fidei, adeóq; de verè bonis operibus 1554. Hunc librum in lectione publica commendavit Melanchthon, & literis ad me scriptis mihi gratulatus est. Regi autem Dano inscripseram, rogatus à viris piis & cordatis, si forte in Dania & iis partibus nostras Ecclesias Helveticas minus ædiffent.
units.tr: Vol. VIII. 1. A preface for Christians, that is, that Jesus Christ our Lord has been given to the world as Saviour by the heavenly Father, in whom the faithful have in summary form all that pertains to learning true piety and attaining and keeping a truly blessed life, so that there is no need to gather these things from elsewhere; a demonstration addressed to the most Christian and most powerful King of the Franks, Henry II, 1552. I was writing this little book when the King of the Franks and Duke Maurice conspired with the other German princes for the liberation of the captive princes of Saxony and Hesse. I sent the little book to the King through the captain Sebastian Schertlin. 2. On the authority, certainty and absolute perfection of Holy Scripture, and on the institution and anointing of bishops, who are ministers of the Word of God, against the prelates of Roman superstition and tyranny, in 2 books, to the most serene King of England, Henry VIII, 1538. When English men, pious and learned, came to Helvetia for the sake of study, and some of them used my hospitality, and all affirmed that today nothing more fruitful could be written for England than about Scripture and bishops, I undertook this labour for the sake of the study of truth, wrote these two books, and sent them printed to the King. 3. On justifying grace through Christ, through faith alone, without good works, faith meanwhile overflowing into good works, in 4 books, to the most serene Christian, King of Denmark. In these things is discussed the grace of God, redemption through Christ, the true faith by which Christ is received and which is imputed to us for righteousness; how these alone, without works, are said to justify; concerning the works of the Law and of faith, and so concerning truly good works, 1554. Melanchthon commended this book in public lecture and congratulated me in a letter written to me. I had, however, addressed it to the Danish King at the request of pious and sensible men, in case perhaps in Denmark and those regions our Helvetic churches were less edified.

units.la: 4. De origine erroris libri duo ab ipso authore nunc demùm recogniti, & aliquot locis præclarè aucti. Priori agitur de DEI veri invocatione justa, & cultu vero, de Deorum item falsorum religionibus, & simulachrorum cultus errore. Posteriori autem libro de institutione Sacrae Coenae Domini, & de origine & progressu Missæ Papisticæ contra varias superstitiones, pro religione vera & orthodoxa 1568 ad Clarissimos viros D. Ambrosium Blaarerum & Petrum Simlerum. Opusculum de origine erroris initio Capellæ Tigurinorum formavi 1527, 1528. ad imitationem Lactantii, ut me exercerem, non autem ut ederetur in publicum. At placuit D. Oecolampadio, cujus suasu Basileæ primum excusus est libellus per Thomam VVolphium 1529. Cæterùm post annos decem ann 1539. recognitum ac locupletatum ipse edidi Tigurì. Postremò autem à prima Editione anno quadragesimo i. e. 1560. extremam ei impositi manum, recognito toto opere & aucto, editóque à Froschovvero nostro, sicut hic titulus ejus est consignatus. De hoc scripto ita Zanchius ad ipsum Bullingerum ann. Chr. 1568. Placet recitare, quid mihi olim Monachus ille Montalpinus, qui tandem combustus fuit Romæ propter Evangelium, de libro tuo, de origine erroris, dixerit. Cùm ego nunquam eum legissem aut vidissem, hortabatur ille ut emerem, & si, inquiebat, non habes nummos, erue tibi oculum dextrum, illôque persolvas, & lege sinistro. Dei beneficio mox reperi librum &c. Imò jam an. Chr. 1540. Comes Donzarensis illud ipsum scriptum luculento ornavit elogio. De quo alibi. 5. De Concilijs, quomodo Apostoli Christi in primitiva Ecclesia suum illud Concilium Hierosolymis celebrârint, & quanto cum fructu, quanraque cum pace. Quomodo item Romani Pontifices in extrema Mundi senecta, à quingentis, & amplius annis sua illa Concilia celebrârint, & quanto cum damno fidelium, brevis ex Historiis commemoratio in duos distincta libros ad D. Bernhardum à Cham, Reipubl. Tigurinæ Consulem 1560. Dum reparatur denuo Concilium Tridentinum, postulârunt Viri pii, authoritate graves, ac eruditi, ut hoc argumentum exponerem. Hæc de Didacticis, Polemica nunc sequuntur; sequentibus duobus Tomis. IX.
units.tr: 4. On the origin of error, two books, now at last revised by the author himself and greatly improved in several places. The first treats of the right invocation of the true God and true worship, and likewise of the religions of false gods and the error of worshipping images. The second book treats of the institution of the Lord's Supper and of the origin and progress of the Papistical Mass, against various superstitions, for the true and orthodox religion, 1568, to the distinguished men Ambrosius Blaarer and Peter Simler. I composed the little work On the Origin of Error at the beginning, for the Zurich chapel, in 1527 and 1528, in imitation of Lactantius, to exercise myself, not to have it published. But it pleased Oecolampadius, at whose urging the little book was first printed at Basel by Thomas Wolff, 1529. Afterwards, however, ten years later, in 1539, I myself revised and enlarged it and published it at Zurich. Lastly, in the fortieth year from the first edition, that is 1560, I put the final touch to it, the whole work having been revised and enlarged, and it was published by our Froschauer, as its title records. Zanchius wrote about this work to Bullinger himself in the year of Christ 1568: "It pleases me to recount what that monk of Montalpino, who was at last burned at Rome on account of the Gospel, once said to me about your book On the Origin of Error. Since I had never read or seen it, he urged me to buy it, saying, 'If you have no money, tear out your right eye, pay with that, and read with the left.' By God's kindness I soon found the book, etc." Indeed, already in 1540 the Count of Donzarensis adorned that very writing with an elegant eulogy. Of this more elsewhere. 5. On Councils: how the Apostles of Christ in the primitive Church held their council at Jerusalem, and with how much fruit and how much peace; likewise how the Roman Pontiffs, in the old age of the world, have for more than five hundred years held their councils, and with how much loss to the faithful. A brief account from the histories, divided into two books, to Master Bernhard von Cham, consul of the Zurich Republic, 1560. Since the Council of Trent is being reconvened, grave, learned and authoritative pious men asked that I expound this subject. These are the didactic works; the polemical ones follow in the two following volumes, IX.

units.la: 1. Præfatio ad libros. 4. Iosiæ Simleri de æterno Dei filio, qua respondetur libello anonymo, qui inscribitur judicium de Censura Ministrorum Tigurinorum, & Heidelbergensium, de dogmate contra adorandam Trinitatem in Polonia nuper sparso 1568. Ajunt authorem hunc ἀνώνυμον Hosium fuisse Cardinalem, Varniensem in Polonia Episcopum: Et Poloni rogarunt ut responderem huic libello.
units.tr: 1. Preface to the books. 4. Josias Simler's On the Eternal Son of God, in which is answered an anonymous pamphlet entitled Judgment on the Censure of the Ministers of Zurich and Heidelberg concerning the Doctrine against the Adoration of the Trinity, recently circulated in Poland, 1568. They say this anonymous [ἀνώνυμον] author was Hosius, the Cardinal, Bishop of Warmia in Poland. And the Poles asked me to reply to this pamphlet.

units.la: 2. Ad Johannem Fabri Viennensis Episcopi libellum, de admirabili nova victoria responsio, in qua disseritur, an religionis causa victi sint Helvetii Evangelicæ Professionis a. D. 1552. Mox ab initio ob infelix bellum Capellanum, Faber epinicium cecinit scripto libello venenato: cui respondendum judicârunt boni viri. Respondi, & responsionem hanc misit per Melchiorem Tscheli, Viennam Austriæ ad ipsum Fabrum. Respondit, nolo cum illo disputare, quem video succelsisse Zuinglio, non tam in officio, quàm in audacia. Nuncium verò benignè excepit, & dimisit cum benedictione.
units.tr: 2. Reply to the little book of John Faber, Bishop of Vienna, On the Admirable New Victory, in which it is argued whether the Helvetians were defeated for the sake of religion, in the year 1552 of the Evangelical profession. Soon after the unhappy war of Kappel, Faber sang his triumph in a venomous little writing, and good men judged that it should be answered. I replied, and sent this reply through Melchior Tscheli to Faber himself at Vienna in Austria. He answered: "I do not wish to dispute with a man whom I see to have succeeded Zwingli, not so much in his office as in his audacity." However, he received the messenger kindly and dismissed him with a blessing.

units.la: 3. Ad Iohannem Cochleum de Canonicæ Scripturæ & Catholicæ Ecclesiæ dignitate responsio orthodoxa 1544.
units.tr: 3. Orthodox response to John Eck [Cochleus] on the dignity of Holy Scripture and of the Catholic Church, 1544.

units.la: 4. Brevis Anti-Byλη, seu responsio secunda ad maledictam Cochlei de Scripturæ & Ecclesiæ authoritate replicam, una cum expositione de sancta Christi Ecclesia Catholica: Ad Ottonem Henricum Palatinum Rheni, & utriusque Bavariæ Ducem 1544. Prior Cochleus, editis libris oppugnavit libros meos de Scriptura & Episcopis ad Angliæ Regem scriptos, unde coactus sum veritatem tueri.
units.tr: 4. A brief Anti-Byle [Anti-Byλη], or second reply to the abusive rejoinder of Cochleus on the authority of Scripture and the Church, together with an exposition of the holy Catholic Church of Christ. Addressed to Otto Henry, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of both Bavarias, 1544. Cochleus had earlier attacked my books on Scripture and on the Bishops, which I wrote to the King of England, and so I was compelled to defend the truth.

units.la: 5. De Anabaptistarum origine, progressu, variis sectis, deque præcipuis eorum dogmatibus & argumentis, quibus sua probant, una cum accurata singulorum confutationS tione lib.6. Germanicè ad Ampliss. Reipubl. Tig. Consulem, Georgium Mullerum. Latinitate donavit Iosias Simlerus. Quod in inferiori Germania, & multis in locis augerentur Anabaptistæ, rogárunt me viri boni, rogavit & ipse Senior Froschovverus, ut scriberem contra sectam illam maxime. Obtemperavi, præsertim quòd sperarem, plurimos admonitos, pestem illam fugituros.
units.tr: 5. On the origin and progress of the Anabaptists, their various sects, and their principal doctrines and arguments by which they support their views, together with a careful refutation of each, in six books. Written in German for the most distinguished consul of the Republic of Zurich, Georg Müller. Turned into Latin by Josias Simler. Good men asked me, and the elder Froschauer also asked me, to write especially against that sect, because the Anabaptists were growing in Lower Germany and in many places. I complied, chiefly because I hoped that many who were warned would flee that plague.

units.la: Tom X. 1. Apologetica expositio, qua ostenditur, Tigurinæ Ecclesiæ Ministros nullum sequi dogma hæreticum in Cœna Domini, libellis quorundam acerbis opposita, & ad omnes veritatem amantes Christi fideles placidè scripta 1556. Reparavit dissidium Sacramentarium Vvestphalus, rixas excitárunt & alii homines inepti Lutherani; quibus, prateritis eorum nominibus, hanc opposui apologiam. 2. Confessio Ministrorum Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ, in qua exponitur eorum fides, & doctrina veteri Orthodoxæ Ecclesiæ consentiens, de præcipuis Capitibus religionis nostræ, & præcipuè de Cœna Domini, ac respondit convitiis Lutheri, quæ effudit in sua brevi confesione, edita 1545. Germanicè scriptum Librum Latinè transtulit Rodolphus Gualtherus. Edita est hæc Confessio sub nomine omnium Ministrorum Tigurinorum, quam tamen ipse composui; inde verò cum Fratribus contuli; præsentibus etiam Senatoribus ad hoc deputatis, qui in eam unanimiter consenserunt. 3. Tractatio verborum DOMINI: In domo Patris mei mansiones multæ sunt ex cap. 14. Iohannis, qua demonstratur, spem salutemque fidelium certissimam esse. Et cœlum, in quod ascendit Christus, & in quod suscipiuntur Electi omnes, locum esse in excelsis certum. Vbi & de dextra Dei, & ubiquitate Corporis Christi disseritur. Ad D. Nicolaum à Diesbach, Prætor. Bernensem 1562. Et hunc libellum edidi in patrocinium veritatis, quam multi variis impetebant scriptis. Interim contra neminem nominati scripsi. 4. Responsio, qua ostenditur, sententiam de Cœlo, & Dei dextera, libello Bullingeri ex S. Scriptura & beatis Patribus propositam, adversarii D. Iohannis Brentii sententia, nondum esse ev…
units.tr: Vol. X. 1. Apologetic exposition, which shows that the ministers of the Church of Zurich follow no heretical doctrine concerning the Lord's Supper, written calmly against the bitter little books of certain men and addressed to all Christ's faithful who love the truth, 1556. The Westphalian revived the sacramentarian quarrel, and other foolish Lutherans stirred up brawls; I have set this apology against them, without naming them. 2. Confession of the ministers of the Church of Zurich, in which their faith is set out, and their doctrine, which agrees with the old doctrine of the orthodox Church, on the principal heads of our religion, and especially on the Lord's Supper; it also answers the insults which Luther poured out in his brief confession, published 1545. The book, written in German, was translated into Latin by Rudolf Gwalther. This Confession was published under the name of all the Zurich ministers, though I composed it myself; then I conferred on it with the brethren, and with the senators appointed for this purpose present, who agreed to it unanimously. 3. Treatise on the words of the Lord: "In my Father's house are many mansions" (John 14), in which it is shown that the hope and salvation of believers is most certain, and that heaven, into which Christ ascended and into which all the elect are received, is a definite place on high. The right hand of God and the ubiquity of Christ's body are also discussed. To Nicolas von Diesbach, Bernese magistrate, 1562. I published this little book in defence of the truth, which many attacked with various writings. Meanwhile I wrote against no one by name. 4. Reply, which shows that the opinion about heaven and the right hand of God, set out from Scripture and the blessed Fathers in Bullinger's little book, has not yet been ev…

units.la: fam, sed firmam perstare adhuc; ad eundem Germanicè & Latinè 1561. Brentius, jussus à Principe suo, Christophoro Duce Vvittenbergense, contrame nominatim scripsit, quod Landgravius Hassiæ senior vehementer laudâssèt, illam nostram tractationem verborum DOMINI. Metuebat, ne quid causæ suæ, quam semel defendendam, & obtrudendam omnibus instituerat, libellus meus derogaret; Protractus ergò in in arenam, perrexi (DEO juvante) veritatem tueri. 5. Fundamentum firmum, cui tuto, quivis fidelis niti potest, hoc praesertim difficili seculo quo disidiis, Doctorumque adversariis scriptis omnia conturbata sunt, positum ad institutionem consolationemque omnium simplicium &c. In hoc libro breviter & simpliciter respondetur Brentii libro contra Petrum Martyrem & Henricum Bullingerum edito, de Majestate D. N.I. Chr. ad dexteram Dei Patris; Latine & Germanice; ad eundem 1563. Rursus in Martyrem, & ms. scripsit librum copiosum Brentius, quem inscripsit de Majestate Christi, cui, qua potui, brevitate respondi, & in duas partes librum sum partitus.
