Volui autem cavere prima hujus libri parte, ne simpliciores nostra offenderentur rixa, sed ut inde aliquid utilitatis perciperent. Secunda parte respondi ejus sophismatibus. 6. Repetitio & dilucidior explicatio consensus veteris Orthodoxae Catholicae Christi Ecclesiae in doctrina Prophetica & Apostolica de inconfusis proprietatibus Naturarum Christi, in una indivisa Persona permanentibus, adeoque de veritate carnis Christi ad dexteram Dei Patris in Coelo sedentis, & non ubique praesentis. At altera parte hujus libelli perstringitur ultimus ille Johannis Brentii liber, inscriptus Recognitio 1564. Suaserant Vitebergenses Theologi Brentio, ut desineret hac de causa altercari, & subtilitates nectere. Ille vero nihilominus edidit librum obscurissimum, quem inscripsit Recognitio. Ego brevem ei opposui libellum, quem inscripsi: Repetitio &c. & in hunc recollegi universae vetustatis orthodoxam hac de re doctrinam, totiusque disputationis nostrae summam. 7. Ad Iohannis Brentii Testamentum nuper publicatum, brevis, necessaria, & modesta responsio Ministrorum Ecclesiae Tigurinae, omnibus fidelibus ad judicandum proposita 1571. Latinitate donavit Iof. Simlerus. Guilelmus Bydenbachius, Doctor, (qui paulo post editum Brentii Testamentum, mania percussus, sibi ipsi mortem conscivit) a morte Brentii, hoc ejus Testamentum edidit, quo cum intolerabilibus vitiis flagrat, responsionem hanc meam scripsi, quam cum vidissent & legissent Symmystae Fratres Tigurinae Ecclesiae voluerunt, ut concorditer ederetur, non meo tantum; sed omnium Fratrum Administrorum nomine communi. 8. Bulla Papistica ante biennium, contra Serenissimam Franciae, Angliae & Hiberniae Reginam Elizabetham. & contra inclytum Angliae Regnum promulgata refutatio, Orthodoxaeque Reginae & universi regni Angliae defensio; ad Reverendissimos
units.tr: …overthrown, but still stands firm; to the same, in German and Latin, 1561. Brentius, ordered by his prince, Duke Christoph of Württemberg, wrote against me by name, because the elder Landgrave of Hesse had greatly praised that treatise of mine on the words of the Lord. He feared that my little book would detract from his cause, which he had once determined to defend and to press on everyone. So, dragged into the arena, I went on, with God's help, to defend the truth. 5. A firm foundation, on which any believer may safely rest, especially in this difficult age, when all things are thrown into confusion by dissensions and by the writings of doctors who oppose one another, laid for the instruction and comfort of all the simple, etc. In this book I briefly and plainly answer Brentius's book, published against Peter Martyr and Henry Bullinger, on the majesty of our Lord Jesus Christ at the right hand of God the Father; in Latin and German; to the same, 1563. Again Brentius wrote a long book against Martyr and me, which he entitled On the Majesty of Christ. I answered it as briefly as I could, and divided my book into two parts. I wished to guard the first part of my book so that our simpler folk would not be offended by the quarrel, but would gain some profit from it. In the second part I answered his sophisms. 6. A repetition and clearer explanation of the agreement of the old orthodox Catholic Church of Christ, in the prophetic and apostolic doctrine, concerning the unconfused properties of the natures of Christ, remaining in one undivided Person, and so concerning the truth of the flesh of Christ seated at the right hand of God the Father in heaven, and not present everywhere. In the other part of this little book, that last book of Johannes Brentius, entitled Recognition, is attacked, 1564. The Wittenberg theologians had urged Brentius to stop wrangling over this matter and to stop weaving subtleties. He nevertheless published a very obscure book, which he entitled Recognition. I opposed to it a short little book, which I entitled Repetition, etc., and in it I gathered the orthodox doctrine of all antiquity on this matter, and the sum of our whole dispute. 7. Brief, necessary and modest reply of the ministers of the Church of Zurich to the recently published Testament of Johannes Brentius, set before all believers for judgement, 1571. Turned into Latin by Josias Simler. Wilhelm Bidenbach, a doctor (who, shortly after the publication of Brentius's Testament, was struck with madness and took his own life), published this Testament of Brentius after his death. Since it burns with intolerable faults, I wrote this reply of mine. When my fellow ministers of the Zurich Church saw and read it, they wished it to be published in harmony, not in my name alone, but in the common name of all the brethren who administer the Church. 8. Papal bull promulgated two years ago against the most serene Elizabeth, Queen of France, England and Ireland, and against the famous kingdom of England; a refutation, and a defence of the orthodox Queen and of the whole kingdom of England; addressed to the most reverend

units.la: diisimos difsimos Angliæ Episcopos Eboracensem, Elienfem, & Sarisburiensem, Londini liber excusus, & in Linguam Anglicam translatus. Episcopus Angliæ nonnullus mittebat mihi Bullam Papæ, quæ seditionem excitaret in Anglia, rogantibus ut Bullam hanc ad veritatis pacisque defensionem confutarem, libenter obsecutus sum iis, scriptum à me librum in Angliam ad Episcopos misi, quem illi, Regina consentiente & approbante, curárunt Londini typis excudi, & evulgari: Si qui alii libri sub nomine meo ante hunc annum 1573. prodierunt, eos ipse nonedidi, excepto libello de hebdomadibus Danielis, sed hunc retractavi in Homiliis in Danielem. Anno 1530. cum Bremogarti in patria mea inservirem Ecclesiæ, scripsi Germanica Lingua quatuor libros contra Anabaptistas pro isto tempore, & pro illis, qui tunc erant, dispositos: quorum mentionem feci in Præfatione sex librorum, postremo à me contra eosdem editorum. Illos ipsos Leo Judæ in Latinam Linguam, & ex Elencho Zuinglii multa meis intertexuit, & sub hoc titulo vulgavit: Adversus omnia Catabaptistarum prava dogmata Henrici Bullingeri libri 4. per Leonem Judæ aucti, adeo ut priorem editionem vix agnoscas 1535. Adjeci illis libellum de decimis & annuis reditibus, quem adhuc agnosco, & quem Zuinglius in annotationibus in Jeremiam commendavit. Anno 1546. Scripsi librum de Sacramentis, quem primo quidem misi, ad D. Calvinum. Dedicavi etiam Serenissimæ Principi & Dominæ, D. Elisabethæ Reginæ Angliæ Eduardi VI. Sorori &c. Ipse vero postea, quæ mihi videbantur necessaria, transtuli in nostras Decades. Cùm anno 1573. & 74. ex variis calamitatibus, & per dilfensiones ubique pestiferas affligeretur populus, edidi duos sermones in Psalmum 130. & 133. consolandi, & ad concordiam adhortandi gratiâ, Germanicè. Illis ipsis annis edidit Iacobus Andreas Schmidelinus contra Zuinglianos sermonem posteriorem habitum apud Memmingenses. Ediderunt & alii contra nos libellos convitiis & calumniis redundantes, quibus brevissimè respondi Germanicè: liber die siben Klagarticul, nomine Ministrorum Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ responsio hæc Germanicè prodiit; postea à Iosia Simlero Latinè translata 1574. Hæc quidem pleraque ex digestione, quam sua manu instituit Bullingerus. In vita tamen ejus, sive Diario, reperio adhuc Catalogum tam Latinorum, quàm Germanicorum Scriptorum, quæ intra sexennium Capellæ elaboravit, oratoria maximè, quæ tamen non omnia prodierunt. Sunt autem sequentia, ut plurimum, magnam tamen partem adhuc in Bibliotheca Civica αὐτογράφως custodita. Latina sunt:
units.tr: most reverend bishops of England, of York, Ely and Salisbury; a book printed at London and translated into English. A certain English bishop sent me the Pope's bull, which was stirring up sedition in England, and asked me to refute this bull in defence of truth and peace. I gladly complied. I sent the book I wrote to the bishops in England, and with the Queen's consent and approval they had it printed and published at London. If any other books have appeared under my name before this year 1573, I have not published them myself, except the little book On the Weeks of Daniel, which I revised in my Homilies on Daniel. In 1530, when I was serving the Church in my native Bremgarten, I wrote in German four books against the Anabaptists, suited to that time and to those who then existed; I mentioned them in the preface to the six books which I later published against the same people. Leo Jud translated these very books into Latin, weaving into them much from Zwingli's Elenchus and from my own work, and published them under this title: Against all the perverse doctrines of the Catabaptists, by Henry Bullinger, four books, enlarged by Leo Jud, so that you would scarcely recognise the earlier edition, 1535. To them I added a little book On tithes and annual revenues, which I still acknowledge, and which Zwingli commended in his notes on Jeremiah. In 1546 I wrote a book On the Sacraments, which I first sent to Master Calvin. I also dedicated it to the most serene Princess and Lady, Lady Elizabeth, Queen of England, sister of Edward VI, etc. Later I myself transferred into our Decades whatever seemed to me necessary. When in 1573 and 1574 the people were afflicted by various calamities, and by dissensions that were everywhere pestilential, I published, in German, two sermons on Psalms 130 and 133, to console and to exhort to concord. In those same years Jacob Andreas Schmidlin published a second sermon against the Zwinglians, delivered at Memmingen. Others also published books against us, overflowing with insults and calumnies, to which I replied briefly in German. The book Die siben Klagarticul came out, and this reply in the name of the ministers of the Church of Zurich came out in German; afterwards Josias Simler translated it into Latin in 1574. These are most of the works from the list which Bullinger drew up with his own hand. In his life, or diary, I still find a catalogue of both Latin and German writings which he produced within six years of the Chapel, chiefly orations, though not all of them were published. The following are, for the most part, but a large part of them is still kept in the Civic Library in autograph. The Latin works are:

units.la: 1. Narratio, quomodo a vulsi à traditionibus humanis, solis Scripturis hærere & credere cœperimus. 2. De ratione studiorum, cùm sacrarum literarum, tum prosanarum, ad Vuernh. Steinerum, liber justus. 3. De Prophetâ, libri duo, quorum primus habet cap. 24. secundus a duodecim. 4. In duos locos communes Phil. Melanchth. nempe in lib. Arbitri, & peccatum commentarius 5. De divina providentia, contra impium carnis judicium liber. 6. In Evangel. Matth. comment. lib 8. 7. In Evangel. Iohannis Comment. lib. 7 8. In historiam Passionis Domini ex 4. compositam, commentarius. 9. Evangel. Lucae Comment. Lib. 8. 10. In Acta Apostol. annotationes. 11. In Epistol. ad Tit. annotationes 12. In Epistol. Iacobi, Iohannis, Petri, annotationes. 13. Epistola ad accusationem Christophori Stiegii, Ferimontani, in qua agitur de modestia Christiana, de convitiis, de Fide justificante, de conjugio sacerdotum, de lib. arb. & de Eucharistia. 14. Aethiologia, cur missa non sit sacrificium. 15. De institutione & gemino usu Eucharistiae ad Vuernh Stein. & Bart. Stokerum 16. Declamationes de Eucharistia quinque. 17. Oratio de cruce & patientia. 18. Alia de charitate & pace. 19. Alia de contemnendo Mundo. 20 Alia de nomine Iesu, quam ipsius habeo manu exaratam. 21. Invectiva contra libidinem. 22. Sylva omnium Evangelicorum Dominicalium. 23. Ratio scribendi 24. Methodus perveniendi ad philosophiam sermocinalem 25. Scholia in utramque lib. de Cop. Erasmi De fructu & usu copiae Epistolae. 26. Scholion in proverbium, Dulce bellum inexperto. 27. Vita, & encomium Ciceronis. 28. Commentarius in orationem Ciceronis pro lege Manilia. 29. Symbolum suavis & probae matris familiae. Germanice scripsimus consequentes, in hoc, ut linguam Patriam discerem rectius & melius. 1. De universa ratione Scripturae sanctae, ad Iacobum a Madiis Bernensem. 2. Parenetica ad vitam Christianam. 3. Parænetica ut fidelem pastorem agat Matthias, Sengensis. 4. De uno, solo, vero, vivo, & aeterno DEO, deque multis fictitiis, & falsis Diis, liber. 5. Epistolam Pauli ad Rom. Comment. lib. 10. 6. In Epistol. ad Galat. Comm. hb. 3. & paraphrasin. 7. In Epist. ad Ephes. lib. 2. & paraphrasin. 8. In Epistolam ad Philipp. to. lib 4. & paraph. 9. In Epist. ad Coloss. lib 2. 10. In utramque ad Thessal. 11. In utramque ad Timoth. lib. 5 & paraphr. 12. In Epist. ad Titum Comm. lib. 1 & paraph. 13. Totidem in Epistolam ad philem. in Epist. ad Hebr. libri 5. & paraphr. 14. De Baptismo, & parvulorum baptismo ad Henricum Sinlerum. 15. De veteri & novo ritu Eucharistiae. 16. Apologia ad librum Rodolphi Vuingarteri, Tugini, super Eucharistiae negotio. 17. De moribus, & institutionibus probae puellae, ad Annam Adolphi Mergerlin. 18. Institutio christiani matrimonii. 19. Paraclesis ad Evangelicam religionem, scripta Coss Brengartini, Mattschio, & Schodelero. 19. Super Lucae 14 cap copiosa commentatio, de resurrectione mortuorum. 20 Brutus sive Lucretia, Germanico carmine scripta Tragoedia, quae postea anno Domini 1543. Basileae publice a civibus acta est, & impressa, sine meo nomine. Alios libros, Latinos & Germanicos, quos in superioribus Annalibus annotavi in hoc Catalogo, non putavi repetendos esse. Sequentes libri, & Epistolae etiam Germanice scriptae sunt. sint, sed vel interciderunt, vel non absoluti sunt, velipud alios delitescunt. Commentarii varij in Psalm. 1 2. 4. 5. 8. 14. 18. 22. 44. 45. 116. 127. 138 ad varios. Commentarius in Symbolum Nicenum, ad Verenam Huseram. Declaratio 24. Articulorum Ioh. Huss. ad Annam Kolinam. Dialogi 2. de Eucharistia ad V. Brandeburgicum. Loci communes rerum Sacrarum, ad Tuginos. De nova & veteri fide contra lapsos. De poenitentia, confessione & satisfactione liber. De vera & falsa amicitia libellus. De sancta cruce expositio. De contemnenda morte. Contra invidiam pro concordia. Accusatio amoris cupidinei. Defensio ejusdem. Consolatoria super morte Filii, sive Epitaphium Ioh. Rusingeri ad Marcum Patrem. Accusatio homicidae & consolatio ejusd. De scandalo. De peccatorum remissione in Ezech. 18. De libertate Christiana. Acta Tig. disputationis de Catabaptismo, & puerorum Baptismo. Quod Chtiftianus jusjurandum & praestare & exigere posit. 124. axiomata adversus Fridolinum Lindoerum. Anno Domini 1520. Latine scripsimus duos Dialogos adversus Scholasticos Theologos: Duos item adversus Pipericornum, pro Iohanne Reuchlino unum quoque, quem promotores nuncupavimus. Ita ad an. Chr. 1569. Cum multis annis statuissem ex omnibus, quos habere potuissem, authoribus, vitas Pontificum Romanorum in compendium contrahere, hoc anno, mense Augusto, opus illud absolvi. Nunquam tamen, etsi a multis desideratum, editum est. Misc, adhuc servatur a nostris. Et quia inter praecipua Bibliothecae meae refero κειμηλια omnia illa, quae Bullingeri vel ingenio sunt elaborata, hactenus tamen nondum vulgata: vel manu exarata, brevem illorum, Coronidis loco, subjiciam indicem. Habeo ergo manu ipsius Bullingeri scripta. 1. Librum contra Anabaptistas, una cum brevi tractatu de ratione censuum 2. Partem Psalterii Germanici 3. Epistolarum Latino-Germanicarum aliquot centurias. 4. De Republica Tigurinorum (Regimenthuch) Nomenclatura eorum, qui Reipublicae praefuerunt cum observationibus Historicis. 5. In Epistolas Jacobi, Iudae, Iohannis, Lucam, &c. Schematismos 6. Acta Concordiae VVittebergensis, ex publicis scriptis 7. Leges Scholae Reformatae Tigurinae, &c.
units.tr: 1. A narrative of how we began, once freed from human traditions, to cling to Scripture alone and believe it. 2. On the method of study, both sacred and secular letters, a just book addressed to Wernher Steiner. 3. On the Prophet, two books, of which the first has 24 chapters and the second twelve. 4. A commentary on two of Philip Melanchthon's commonplaces, namely on the book On Free Will and on Sin. 5. A book against the impious judgment of the flesh, on divine providence. 6. A commentary on the Gospel of Matthew, 8 books. 7. A commentary on the Gospel of John, 7 books. 8. A commentary on the history of the Lord's Passion, composed from the four Gospels. 9. A commentary on the Gospel of Luke, 8 books. 10. Annotations on the Acts of the Apostles. 11. Annotations on the Epistle to Titus. 12. Annotations on the Epistles of James, John and Peter. 13. An epistle in reply to the accusation of Christopher Stiegius of Pfaffenhofen, dealing with Christian modesty, reproaches, justifying faith, the marriage of priests, free will and the Eucharist. 14. An Aetiology, why the mass is not a sacrifice. 15. On the institution and twofold use of the Eucharist, addressed to Wernher Steiner and Bartholomew Stocker. 16. Five declamations on the Eucharist. 17. A speech on the cross and patience. 18. Another on love and peace. 19. Another on despising the world. 20. Another on the name of Jesus, which I have in his own handwriting. 21. An invective against lust. 22. A compendium of all the Gospels for the Sundays. 23. The method of writing. 24. The method of arriving at dialectic. 25. Scholia on both books of Erasmus's De copia, On the Fruit and Use of Copia of Letters. 26. A scholion on the proverb, "War is sweet to those who have not tried it." 27. The life and encomium of Cicero. 28. A commentary on Cicero's speech for the Manilian Law. 29. The symbol of a gentle and upright mother of a family. I later wrote in German, in order to learn my native tongue more correctly and better: 1. On the whole method of Holy Scripture, addressed to Jacob von Madiis of Bern. 2. Exhortations to the Christian life. 3. Exhortations on how Matthias of Sengen should act as a faithful minister. 4. A book on the one, sole, true, living and eternal God, and on the many fictitious and false gods. 5. A commentary on Paul's Epistle to the Romans, 10 books. 6. On the Epistle to the Galatians, a commentary in 3 books and a paraphrase. 7. On the Epistle to the Ephesians, 2 books and a paraphrase. 8. On the Epistle to the Philippians, 4 books and a paraphrase. 9. On the Epistle to the Colossians, 2 books. 10. On both Epistles to the Thessalonians. 11. On both Epistles to Timothy, 5 books and a paraphrase. 12. On the Epistle to Titus, a commentary in 1 book and a paraphrase. 13. Likewise on the Epistle to Philemon; on the Epistle to the Hebrews, 5 books and a paraphrase. 14. On baptism and infant baptism, addressed to Henry Sinler. 15. On the old and new rite of the Eucharist. 16. An apology against the book of Rudolf Wingarter of Thurgau concerning the question of the Eucharist. 17. On the morals and training of an upright girl, addressed to Anna, wife of Adolph Mergerlin. 18. An institution of Christian marriage. 19. A paraclesis to the Evangelical religion, written with Caspar Brengartin, Matthew and Schödeler. 19. A copious commentary on Luke chapter 14, on the resurrection of the dead. 20. Brutus, or Lucretia, a tragedy written in German verse, which was afterwards publicly performed and printed at Basel by the citizens in the year of the Lord 1543, without my name. I have not thought it necessary to repeat in this catalogue the other Latin and German books which I noted in the earlier Annals. The following books, and letters also written in German, exist, but have either perished, or were not finished, or lie hidden with others: Various commentaries on Psalms 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 14, 18, 22, 44, 45, 116, 127, 138, addressed to various persons. A commentary on the Nicene Creed, to Verena Huser. A declaration of the 24 articles of John Huss, to Anna Kolin. Two dialogues on the Eucharist, to V. Brandenburg. Commonplaces of sacred things, for the Thurgauers. On the old and new faith, against the lapsed. A book on repentance, confession and satisfaction. A small book on true and false friendship. An exposition of the holy cross. On despising death. Against envy, for concord. An accusation of carnal love, and a defence of the same. A consolation on the death of a son, or an epitaph for John Rusinger, to Mark the father. An accusation of a murderer and a consolation for him. On scandal. On the forgiveness of sins, on Ezekiel 18. On Christian liberty. The Acts of the Zurich disputation on Catabaptism and infant baptism. That a Christian may both render and require an oath. 124 axioms against Fridolin Lindoer. In the year of the Lord 1520 I wrote in Latin two dialogues against the scholastic theologians; likewise two against Pfefferkorn, and one for Johann Reuchlin, which we called the Promotores. Thus far to the year of Christ 1569. Although for many years I had resolved to condense the lives of the Roman Pontiffs into a compendium from all the authors I could obtain, I finished that work this year, in August. Yet, though desired by many, it has never been published. It is still kept by my people. And since I count among the chief treasures of my library all those writings of Bullinger which were either composed by his talent but not yet published, or written out by his own hand, I shall add, as a crown, a short index of them. I therefore have the following writings in Bullinger's own hand. 1. A book against the Anabaptists, together with a short treatise on the method of levying the census. 2. Part of the German Psalter. 3. Several hundred Latin-German letters. 4. On the Commonwealth of the Zurichers (Regimenthuch), a list of those who governed the state, with historical observations. 5. Schematisms on the Epistles of James and Jude, John, Luke, etc. 6. The Acts of the Concord of Wittenberg, from public writings. 7. The Laws of the Reformed School of Zurich, etc.

units.la: Aliorum 1. Historiae Tigurinae libros 14 2. Historiam Reformationis Tigurinae 3. Reformationem Collegii Carolini. 4. Varia consilia. 5. De veneficis & Sortilegis. 6. De excommunicatione. 7. De militia Turcica. 8. Orationem de persecutione Ecclesiae. 9. De Concilio Tridentino. 10. Sermonem, quomodo Ministri debeant gubernare Ecclesiam. 11. De Capitibus, quibus Ecclesia absolvatur. 12. Vitam ab ipso Authore consignatam. 13. Historiae universalis Compendium, Methodice satis dispositum, ab initio Mundi ad annum Chr. 1575. ab aliis, tamen postea continuatum. Bullingerum esse authorem, in anno ejus emortuali expresse monetur.
units.tr: Of others': 1. The fourteen books of the Zurich History. 2. A history of the Zurich Reformation. 3. The reformation of the Carolinum College. 4. Various counsels. 5. On poisoners and sorcerers. 6. On excommunication. 7. On the Turkish warfare. 8. A speech on the persecution of the Church. 9. On the Council of Trent. 10. A sermon on how ministers ought to govern the Church. 11. On the chapters by which the Church is absolved. 12. His life, written down by the author himself. 13. A compendium of universal history, arranged methodically enough, from the beginning of the world to the year of Christ 1575, later continued by others. It is expressly noted in the year of his death that Bullinger is its author.

units.la: Bumannus Iohannes Iacobus, Tigurinus, Ecclesiae Kilchbergensis, ad lacum Tigurinum, Minister. Carmine Latino & Germanico promtus, opusculorum aliquot Theologicorum Latinorum & Germanicorum Interpres. Theodoreti libros de Providentia Dei in Germanicam Linguam transtulit, Basil. Edidit etiam sermonem de Sabbatho. Tig. 1596. Vixit 1590.
units.tr: Bumann, Johann Jakob, of Zurich, minister of the church of Kilchberg on Lake Zurich. Ready in Latin and German verse, and translator of several Latin and German theological tracts. He translated Theodoret's books On the Providence of God into German. He also published a sermon on the Sabbath. Zurich, 1596. He lived in 1590.

units.la: Bumannus Iacobus, Chirurgus, Tigurinus, Germanicè edidit Compendium Anatomiæ Vesalii, cum figuris. Norimbergæ, ubi aliquamdiu vixit, suaeque luculenta artis specimina dedit. Mortuus in Patria, anthrace correptus 1586. ætat. 66.
units.tr: Bumann Jacob, surgeon of Zurich, published in German a compendium of Vesalius's Anatomy, with figures. He lived for some time at Nuremberg, where he gave excellent examples of his skill. He died in his homeland, seized by anthrax, in 1586, aged 66.

units.la: Burckhardus, Iohannes Conradus, Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Minister Catechesin Tigurinam Concionibus exposuit, eásque vulgavit 1659.
units.tr: Burckhard, Johann Conrad, minister of the Zurich Church, expounded the Zurich Catechism in sermons, and published them in 1659.

units.la: Burckhardus; Marcus, Rickenbacensis nuper in agro Tigurino Minister, Capituli Vitodurani Decanus meritissimus, conciones edidit inaugurales de consecratione & cultu Templorum alteram; alteram de impositione manuum, Tig. 1651.
units.tr: Burckhard, Marcus, of Rickenbach, lately minister in the Zurich territory, most deserving dean of the chapter of Winterthur, published two inaugural sermons: one on the consecration and use of churches, the other on the laying on of hands. Zurich, 1651.

units.la: Carolstatt Andreas. Archidiaconus Ecclesiæ Tigur. an. 1525. inde Basileam vocatus; scripsit 1. de Cælibatu, Monachatu & viduitate 1521. 2. Institutionem de aqua benedicta & sale, VVitteb. 1520. 3. De Antichristiano abusu panis & calicis Dominici 1524. 4. Sermonem de usu Sacramenti VVitteb. 1522. 5. de statu animæ Christiani, deque Purgatorio animæ defunctorum 1523. 6. De varietate simplicis unicæ voluntatis Dei, quid sit peccatum, utrum lentè procedendum & offendiculo infirmiorum parcendum in causis ad Dei voluntatem pertinentibus, 1524. 7. De virtute indulgentiarum. §. Apologeticas conclusiones pro scriptura.
units.tr: Karlstadt, Andreas. Archdeacon of the Zurich Church in 1525, afterwards called to Basel. He wrote: 1. On celibacy, monasticism and widowhood, 1521. 2. An instruction on holy water and salt, Wittenberg, 1520. 3. On the anti-Christian abuse of the bread and cup of the Lord, 1524. 4. A sermon on the use of the Sacrament, Wittenberg, 1522. 5. On the state of the Christian soul, and on the Purgatory of departed souls, 1523. 6. On the variety of the simple and single will of God, what sin is, and whether one ought to proceed slowly and spare the stumbling of the weaker in matters pertaining to the will of God, 1524. 7. On the power of indulgences. Apologetic conclusions for Scripture.

units.la: Cellarius Diethelmus, Tigurinus, V.D.M. Transtulit in Linguam Latinam libellum Bullingeri, de consolandis ægrotantibus; item de vera & antiqua fide. Præterea scripsit Scholia in omnes Terentii Comœdias 1546. Poëta & Historicus, Ecclesiæ Muranæ ad lacum Gryphæum fuit Minister.
units.tr: Cellarius Diethelmus, of Zurich, V.D.M. (Verbi Divini Minister), translated into Latin Bullinger's little book on comforting the sick; also on the true and ancient faith. Besides this he wrote Scholia on all the comedies of Terence, 1546. He was a poet and historian, and was minister of the congregation of Muri by Lake Zug.

units.la: Chelidonius, Tigurinus. Petrus Bojasteau, cognomento Launeus, transtulit in Linguam Gallicam, chelidonij Tigurini (sic habet Gallica inscriptio) de institutione Principis. Lugduni.
units.tr: Chelidonius, of Zurich. Petrus Bojasteau, called Launeus, translated into French Chelidonius of Zurich's (so the French title has it) "On the Education of a Prince." Lyon.

units.la: Cholinus Petrus, Tugiensis, Ecclesiæ & Scholæ Tigurinæ Minister, dedit 1. Dictionarium Latino Germanicum 1541. Tig. 2. Grammaticam Linguæ Gallicæ Latinè scriptam, & exemplis Germanicis illustratam Msc. 3. Libellum de conspiciliis. 4. Ecclesiasticos V. T. libros Latinè reddidit, in nota illa Bibliorum Tigurinorum Editione. Obijt. 1542. eo die, quo Typographus opus absolvit.
units.tr: Cholinus Petrus, of Zurich, minister of the Church and School of Zurich, published: (1) a Latin-German Dictionary, 1541, Zurich; (2) a grammar of the French language, written in Latin and illustrated with German examples, in manuscript; (3) a little book on spectacles; (4) he rendered the Old Testament ecclesiastical books into Latin, in the notable edition of the Zurich Bible. He died in 1542, on the very day the printer finished the work.

units.la: Clauserus Christophorus, Tigurinus, Medicus, scripsit 1. Ephemerides sive Diaria &c. 2. Dialogum de urinæ judicio. Vrinæ inspectionem sine aliis signis inutilem esse. 3. Secreta secretorum, vel de regimine Dominorum Msc.
units.tr: Clauserus Christophorus, of Zurich, a physician, wrote: (1) Ephemerides, or diaries, etc.; (2) a dialogue on the judgment of urine, arguing that inspection of urine without other signs is useless; (3) Secreta secretorum, or on the government of lords, in manuscript.

units.la: Clauserus Conradus, Tigurinus, in Agro primùm Tigurino Minister, postea Gymnasiarcha Brugensis, & Pastor etiam in Ergovia. Scripsit 1. Theologica, ut sunt, Tetras, sive in D. N. Iesu Christi Passionis & Resurrectionis Historiam lib. 4. Sermonum liber, Tig. 1551. De oratione liber, quid sit, in quibus versetur, quae ejus materia, forma & circumstantiae, cum pluribus Deum orandi formulis & expositione Decalogi, Tig. 1553. Dissertatio de studio Theologiae, praefixa translat. Procopij Gazaei. Artificiosa Methodus declamandi, concionandi, disputandi, conscribendi Epistolas II. philosophica. Perbrevis admonitio de legendis Poetis, ad Antonium Clauserum, Moguntiae 1536. Phrases Isocratis. Methodus Analytica ex Platone, Aristote, Hermogene & Cicerone conflatae. Progymnasmata Grammatica Linguae Latinae. Liber Syllabarum quotidiani sermonis, Latinae Linguae. III. Ex Graecis multos translatulit, Cornuti sive Pharnati Commentarium de natura Deorum Gentilium, Basil. 1543. Commentarios quosdam Graecos in Epistolas Pauli. Item Laonici de origine & Rebus gestis Turcarum lib. 10. Theophili Antiocheni ad Autolycum lib. 3. Procopij Gazaei Sophistae Commentarios in priores aliquot Veteris Testamenti libros. Tig. 1555.
units.tr: Clauserus Conradus, of Zurich, first minister in the countryside of Zurich, afterwards schoolmaster of Brugg, and also pastor in Ergovia. He wrote, (1) theological works, namely: Tetras, or a history of the Passion and Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, in four books; a book of sermons, Zurich 1551; a book on prayer, what it is, what it concerns, its matter, form and circumstances, with several formulas for praying to God and an exposition of the Decalogue, Zurich 1553; a dissertation on the study of theology, prefixed to the translation of Procopius of Gaza. (2) Philosophical works: an artful method of declaiming, preaching, disputing and writing letters, in two parts; a very brief admonition on reading the poets, to Antonius Clauserus, Mainz 1536; Phrases of Isocrates; an analytical method drawn from Plato, Aristotle, Hermogenes and Cicero; Progymnasmata of Latin grammar; a book of syllables of everyday Latin speech. (3) From the Greek he translated many works: the commentary of Cornutus, or Phurnutus, on the nature of the pagan gods, Basel 1543; certain Greek commentaries on the Epistles of Paul; also Laonicus on the origin and deeds of the Turks, in ten books; Theophilus of Antioch to Autolycus, in three books; the commentaries of Procopius of Gaza, the sophist, on some of the earlier books of the Old Testament, Zurich 1555.

units.la: Collinus Rodolphus, Guadalinga Lucernensis, natus an. Chr. 14. denatus 1578. aetatis 80. publici muneris 52, quo ad 3. diem obitus, sine intermissione fuit functus. Vitae cursum ipse conscripsit, quem habeo ἀνέκδοτον. Summam autem comprehendit hoc terasticho.
units.tr: Collinus Rodolphus, of Lucerne, born at Guadalinga in the year of Christ 14, died 1578 at the age of 80. He held public office for 52 years, and served without interruption up to the third day before his death. He wrote the course of his own life, which I have in manuscript unpublished. He summed it up in this tetrastich.

units.la: 1. Gundelij natus. 2. Studiosus 3. Restio 4. Miles, 5. Mox Tiguri Civis. 6. Deinde Professor eram: 7. Nunc quoque in extremis, qualis me cunque manet fors, Sors haec in manibus stat Deus almetuus.
units.tr: 1. I was born the son of Gundelius. 2. A student. 3. A rope-maker. 4. A soldier. 5. Soon after, a citizen of Zurich. 6. Then I was a professor. 7. And now too, at the end, whatever fortune awaits me, this lot stands in the hands of God Almighty.

units.la: Plura scripsit, quàm edidit. Extat translatio Euripidis, sub nomine Dorothei Camilli, edita Basileae, auctore nescio. Observationes & annotationes Grammaticae, Historicae, Rhetorologicae in Homerum, Aristophanem, Hesiodum, Xenophontem, Plutarchum, Isocratem, Demosthenem, Nonnum denique, MS. quae ab haeredibus asservabantur. Carmina ejus multa extant vel edita, Epicidia cum primis, in obitum Petri Martyris, Conradi Gesneri, Iacobi Ammiani, Henrici Bullingeri vel ἀνέκδοτα, ut sunt argumenta singulorum Capitum in Evangelium Matthaei carmine elegiaco. Heroici de pugna Capellana. Elegia in Senecae Epistolam adversus ebrietatem. Encomium praedii sui Snelleriani. Epigrammata ad amicos & collegas, Iohannem VVolfium, Iohannem Frisium, Iohannem Fabricium Montanum, Generum.
units.tr: He wrote more than he published. There exists a translation of Euripides under the name Dorotheus Camillus, published at Basel, the author of which I do not know. Grammatical, historical and rhetorical observations and annotations on Homer, Aristophanes, Hesiod, Xenophon, Plutarch, Isocrates, Demosthenes and, finally, Nonnus, in manuscript, which were kept by his heirs. Many of his poems exist, some published, especially his epicedia on the deaths of Peter Martyr, Conrad Gesner, James Ammianus and Henry Bullinger; others unpublished, such as the arguments of the individual chapters of the Gospel of Matthew in elegiac verse; heroic verses on the battle of Kappel; an elegy on Seneca's letter against drunkenness; an encomium of his estate at Snellerius; epigrams to friends and colleagues, John Wolf, John Frisius, John Fabricius Montanus, and his son-in-law.

units.la: Collinus Rodolphus, Tigurinus, F dedit quaedam Carmina, 1. de malo ebrietatis, Tig. & VVitteberg. 2. Ad Iohannem Frisium Praeceptorem, 3. Varia Epicedia.
units.tr: Rodolphus Collinus, of Zurich, published certain poems: (1) on the evil of drunkenness, Zurich and Wittenberg; (2) to John Frisius, his teacher; (3) various funeral poems.

units.la: Dunus, Thaddæus, Locarnensis, Medicus postea Tigurinus, scripsit adhuc adolescens librum de arithmetica, excusum Basileæ à Iacobo Parco, 1545. Item folium unum de Nonis, Idibus & Calendis: Ibidem. Francisci Stancari Commentariorum in Epistolam D. Iacobi, ex Italico sermone in Latinum convertit. Ibidem 1547. Idem adultior edidit Epistolas medicinales & libellum de Semitertiana. Tiguri, apud Adream Gesnerum, 1555. De muliebribus morbis librum, excusum Argentinæ apud Rihelium, 1565. De venæ sectione libros tres: Tiguri apud Frosch. 1570. De respiratione contra Galenum, quòd respiratio non sit motus voluntarius, Bernard. Ochini libros de cœna Domini contra VVesphalum, & Dialogum ejus de purgatorio, ex Italico in Latinum convertit. Tiguri apud Gesnerum, anno 1556. Ejusdem de curandi ratione per venæ sectionem, liber quartus, tribus aliàs editis addendus. 8. Tiguri.
units.tr: Dunus, Thaddaeus, of Locarno, a physician later of Zurich, wrote while still young a book on arithmetic, printed at Basel by James Parcus, 1545. Also a single sheet on the Nones, Ides and Calends, printed there. He translated from Italian into Latin the Commentaries of Francis Stancarus on the Epistle of James, 1547, there. Later, as an adult, he published Medicinal Letters and a little book on the semitertian fever, Zurich, at the house of Andrew Gesner, 1555. A book on women's diseases, printed at Strasbourg by Rihelius, 1565. Three books on bloodletting, Zurich, at Frosch's, 1570. On breathing, against Galen, that respiration is not a voluntary motion. He translated from Italian into Latin the books of Bernardino Ochino on the Lord's Supper against Westphal, and his Dialogue on purgatory, Zurich, at Gesner's, 1556. A fourth book of his on the method of healing by bloodletting, to be added to three others already published. Zurich.

units.la: Edlibachius Geroldus, Reipublicæ Tigurinæ Senator & Quæstor, diligentissimè conscripsit bella Tigurina, Lombardica, Burgundica. Habetur exemplar Msc. in Bibliotheca Civica.
units.tr: Gerold Edlibach, senator and treasurer of the Republic of Zurich, most diligently wrote the wars of Zurich, of Lombardy and of Burgundy. A manuscript copy is held in the Civic Library.

units.la: Eglinus Raphael Iconius, Tigurinus Ecclesiæ & Scholæ Tigurinæ 'adan. Chr. 1605. Minister, inde SS. Theologiæ Doctor & Professor Marpurgi, ubi mortuus est. Scripsit A. Theologica, ut sunt, expressa & solida totius Apocalypsis Dominicæ epilysis, perpetuo Homiliarum archetypo sensus literalis lucem Ecclesiæ De i fœnerans, Tigur. 1600. Hanov. bis 1611. Disputationes quatuor de Cœna Domini & fœdere gratiæ Marp. 1613. Prophetia Halicutica verè nova ad Danielis & Apocalypseos calculum Chronographicum, Tig. 1597. Hanov. 1611. Oratio inauguralis de spirituali ædificio Ecclesiæ fundamento Apostolorum & Prophetarum superstructo, habita Marpurgi. Marp. 1615. Genealogia D. N. Iesu Christi ex regia Davidis stirpe per Salomonis lineam rectam deducta. Marp. 1608. Nucleus enucleatus potissimi Apocalyptici mysterii Carminicè. Assertio doctrinæ Orthodoxæ de peccato in Spiritum Sanctum. Francof. 1617. Explicatio divini propositi, de gratuita Electorum salute, & justa reproborum damnatione. Marp. 1608. Thesis de S. Scripturæ plenitudine, authoritate, perspicuitate. Tig. Disputatio in Genesin. Disputatio de symbolo Apostolico. De magno insitionis mysterio; Rom. 6.1. Antithesis Concilio Tridentino opposita de Principiis Fidei & Scripturæ. De Interpretatione S. Sc. Vulgata. De Decretis & prædestinatione. De Creatione in genere. Antithesis Concil. Trident. opposita de peccato originali & libero arbitrio. De peccato inhabitante, post fidem. Quæstiones & resp. de Decalogo. Aphorismi de justificatione. De Incarnatione Filii Dei. An Ecclesia posšit errare. ΩΕ ἕ καθολικῇ. Dialexis, utrum ea, quæ nunc est Ecclesia Romana, sit vera Ecclesia. Elenchus de Anti-Christo. Eglini de modo & formula precum Luc.6.17. De precatione & jejunio. Assertio veritatis Eucharisticæ fticæ. Antilogia veterum & recentiorum Pontif. de Cæna D. De pœnitentia & fide. De Causis justificationis.
units.tr: Raphael Eglinus Iconius, of Zurich, minister of the Church and School of Zurich in the year of Christ 1605, then Doctor of Sacred Theology and professor at Marburg, where he died. He wrote theological works, namely: a clear and solid exposition of the whole Apocalypse of the Lord, in perpetual homilies, a lamp of the literal sense; On usury, Zurich 1600, Hanau twice 1611; four disputations on the Lord's Supper and the covenant of grace, Marburg 1613; a truly new Halicutic prophecy, according to the chronological calculation of Daniel and the Apocalypse, Zurich 1597, Hanau 1611; an inaugural oration on the spiritual building of the Church, founded on the Apostles and Prophets, delivered at Marburg, Marburg 1615; the genealogy of our Lord Jesus Christ, deduced from the royal stock of David through the direct line of Solomon, Marburg 1608; a kernel unfolded of the chief Apocalyptic mystery, in verse; an assertion of orthodox doctrine on the sin against the Holy Spirit, Frankfurt 1617; an explanation of the divine purpose concerning the free salvation of the elect and the just damnation of the reprobate, Marburg 1608; a thesis on the fullness, authority and perspicuity of Holy Scripture, Zurich; a disputation on Genesis; a disputation on the Apostles' Creed; on the great mystery of ingrafting, Romans 6:1; an antithesis opposed to the Council of Trent on the principles of faith and Scripture; on the interpretation of Holy Scripture by the Vulgate; on the decrees and predestination; on creation in general; an antithesis opposed to the Council of Trent on original sin and free will; on sin dwelling in the believer after faith; questions and answers on the Decalogue; aphorisms on justification; on the incarnation of the Son of God; whether the Church can err; on the catholic Church; a dialexis, whether that which is now the Roman Church is the true Church; an elenchus on the Antichrist; Eglinus on the manner and form of prayers, Luke 6:17; on prayer and fasting; an assertion of the truth of the Eucharist; an antilogy of the ancient and recent Papists on the Lord's Supper; on repentance and faith; on the causes of justification.

units.la: B. Historica. Captivitatis Babylonicæ Historia inde à morte Iofiæ, usque ad primam Hierosolymorum destructionem.
units.tr: B. Historical works. A history of the Babylonian captivity from the death of Josiah to the first destruction of Jerusalem.

units.la: C. Philosophica, ex Iordani Bruni descensu entis excerpta summa terminorum Metaphysicorum Tig. 1595. Ephormofis Mundi, five contextus rerum universi, quadrata rotundis, h. e. divina Physicis, Mathematicè juxta, ac Hieroglyphicè conjungens. Marp. 1615. Francof. 1617. Poetica præsertim, ut felicissimus fuit Poeta, non pauca dedit, de syllabarum quantitate. Genev. & Tig. 1585. Epigrammata, Cucullus clinicus, Apollo seu Carminum Decas. Ode funebris in obitum Guilelmi Stuckij, &c.
units.tr: C. Philosophical works: a summary of the terms of metaphysics, excerpted from Giordano Bruno's "Descent of Being," Zurich 1595; Ephormis of the World, or the connection of the things of the universe, joining squares with circles, that is, divine things with physical, mathematically as well as hieroglyphically, Marburg 1615, Frankfurt 1617. Chiefly poetic, since he was a most fortunate poet, he gave not a few works, on the quantity of syllables, Geneva and Zurich 1585; epigrams; Cucullus clinicus; Apollo, or a decade of poems; a funeral ode on the death of William Stuck, etc.

units.la: Eglinus Tobias Fravenfelda Turgovienfis, in Schola Tigurina educatus, Davosii primùm, postea Curiæ Evangelium docuit. Et in prosa fuit disertus, Curienfis pastor, & felicissimus etiam Poeta, cujus prostant Carminum fragmenta, à Filio Raphaele edita Tig. 1591. Vixit. 1560.
units.tr: Tobias Eglinus of Fravenfeld in Thurgau, educated in the Zurich school, taught the Gospel first at Davos, afterwards at Chur, and he was eloquent in prose, pastor at Chur, and a most fortunate poet too. Fragments of his poems survive, published by his son Raphael, Zurich 1591. He lived to 1560.

units.la: Ernius, Henricus S. S. Theologiæ Schola in Tigurina ad an. Chr. 1619. Profeffor meritissimus, disputationes potissimùm scripsit de variis thematibus doctas & solidas, ut sunt, 1. Quæstionum πιστις contra Anabaptistas 2. contraeosdem Tetras problematica de scriptorum V. T. dignitate. 3. De principio cognoscendi h. e. Scriptura. 4. De omnium Controversiarum judice. 5. De SS. Trinitate. 6. De Diabolica hominum obsessione; 7. De unitate Ecclesiæ utriusque Testamenti. 8. De vocatione Ministrorum Ecclesiæ Reformatæ. 9. De spirituali infantium conditione. 10. Vestis nuptialis, sive de iustificatione. 11. De perseverantia sanctorum.
units.tr: Henry Ernius, professor of Sacred Theology in the Zurich school until the year of Christ 1619, a most deserving professor, wrote learned and solid disputations chiefly on various topics, namely: 1. Questions of faith against the Anabaptists; 2. against the same, problematic theses on the dignity of the writings of the Old Testament; 3. on the principle of knowing, that is, Scripture; 4. on the judge of all controversies; 5. on the Holy Trinity; 6. on the diabolical obsession of men; 7. on the unity of the Church of both Testaments; 8. on the calling of ministers of the Reformed Church; 9. on the spiritual condition of infants; 10. the wedding garment, or on justification; 11. on the perseverance of the saints.

units.la: Faber Conradus, studiis Basileæ absolutis, Domus Iohanniticæ Kusnachtensis ad lacum Tigurinum Commendator, ut vocant, seu Administrator, ejusdemque Reformator; Evangelii insignis Promotor. Interfuit aliquot Disputationibus, Tigurinæ præsertim contra Pontificios & Anabaptistas. Ex actis publicis, in quibus ejus nomen frequens, & eruditio & dexteritas ejus patet. Præses fuit disputationis Anti Anabaptisticæ Bernensis, quæ prodiit cum concione ejus ibidem habita. Sed & aliæ ejus editæ sunt conciones. Occubuit Capellæ 1531, sed ab Osvvaldo Sægiffero Conventuali Kusnachtam deportatus, sepultus ibidem fuit.
units.tr: Conrad Faber, after completing his studies at Basel, became commander, as they call it, or administrator, of the Knights of St John's house at Küsnacht on Lake Zurich, and was its reformer. He was a distinguished promoter of the gospel. He took part in several disputations, chiefly at Zurich against the Papists and the Anabaptists. The public records, where his name often appears, show both his learning and his skill. He presided over the anti-Anabaptist disputation at Bern, which was published together with the sermon he preached there. Other sermons of his were also printed. He died at Kappel in 1531, but was carried back to Küsnacht by Oswald Sägesser, the conventual, and buried there.

units.la: Faber Felix, Vernac. Schmid. Fuit enim ex nobili Schmidiorum familia, patre natus, qui 1443 pro Patria sortirer occubuit, ut ipse refert in Antiquit. Suevic. Lector in Conventu Vlmensi Ordinis Prædicatorum, scripsit 1. Annales Suevicos, ubi tamen multa domestica, præsertim de bello Tigurino immiscuit. 2. Vitam Henrici Susonis, Prædicatorii ordinis, quem inter Asceticorum Helveticorum Patriarchasferè referunt, eúmque in agro Tigurino positissimum claruisse, (Henric. Murer. Helvet. Sanct. p. 315.) tradunt. 3. Peregrinationem tionem Bernhardi Breitenbach, Decani Ecclesiæ Moguntinæ in terra sancta, Latinè & Germanicè.
units.tr: Felix Faber, in the vernacular Schmid. He was born of the noble Schmid family, the son of a father who fell in 1443 for his homeland, as he himself reports in the Antiquitates Suevicae. He was a lector in the convent of the Order of Preachers at Ulm. He wrote: (1) the Annales Suevici, in which, however, he mixed in much that is local, especially about the Zurich war; (2) the life of Henry Suso, of the Order of Preachers, whom they generally count among the Swiss patriarchs of asceticism, and whom they report to have flourished in the Zurich countryside (Henric. Murer, Helvet. Sanct. p. 315); (3) the Journey of Bernhard Breitenbach, dean of the church of Mainz, to the Holy Land, in Latin and German.

units.la: Fabricius Iohannes, Berckemå Alsatus, Leonis Iudæ, ex sorore, nepos, ob excellens ingenium, ut loquitur Bullingerus, & avunculi merito, receptus fuit in numerum Stipendiariorum Ecclesiæ Collegiatæ Tigurinæ. Vir magnus tam in literatura, quàm Theogia Practica: Felix Poëta. Ex Provisore & Paedagogo Tigurino electus Antiites Curiensis, peste abripitur. Extant 1. Theologica: Dispositiones in Epistolas Iacobi, Petri, Iohannis, & alias Canonicas. De Providentia DEI Dialogus, Tig. Oratio, qua docetur, Concilium Tridentinum sine scelere à Christianis hominibus frequentari non posse, Basil. Defensio justa, pro Christi Ecclesia, adversus improbas Fontidonij & Condelli Hispanorum pro Concilio Tridentino calumnias, Genev. 1565. Explicatio Symboli German. In Cap. I. Habacuc Tig 2. philologica Historia Wilhelmi Tellij, carmine, ad Conrad. Pellicanum, quae incscio authore Bernæ fuit excusa. Carmen ad Iohannem Frisium. Epistola ad Hyperium, de Schola Tigurina Msc. quæ statum illius temporis Ecclesiæ & Scholæ nostræ graphicè depingit, digna quæ edatur. 3. philosophica. De differentiis animalium quadrupedum, secundum locos communes. Tigur. 1555.
units.tr: Johann Fabricius, an Alsatian from Berckheim, grandson through his sister of Leo Jud, was received, as Bullinger says, on account of his excellent talent and his uncle's merit, into the number of the stipendiaries of the Collegiate Church of Zurich. He was a great man both in literature and in practical theology, and a happy poet. Chosen from provisor and schoolmaster of Zurich to be chief minister of Chur, he was carried off by the plague. There survive: (1) theological works: notes on the Epistles of James, Peter, John and the other Catholic epistles; a dialogue On the Providence of God; an oration at Zurich showing that the Council of Trent cannot be attended by Christian men without sin; a just defence, printed at Basel, of the Church of Christ against the wicked calumnies of Fontidonius and Condellus, Spaniards, in favour of the Council of Trent (Geneva, 1565); an Explanation of the Creed in German; on Habakkuk chapter 1, Zurich. (2) Philological works: the history of William Tell in verse, addressed to Conrad Pellican, which was printed at Bern without the author's name; a poem to Johann Fries; a letter to Hyperius on the Zurich school, in manuscript, which depicts vividly the state of the Church and school of our time at that period and deserves to be published. (3) Philosophical works: on the differences of four-footed animals, according to the common places. Zurich, 1555.

units.la: Fabricius Sebastianus, Tigurinus, Ecclesiæ Hypervitoduranæ Minister. Encomium à nostris habet pastoris fidelissimi, Viri pii & eruditi, in omni genere rerum diligentissimi. Habentur scripta quædam ejus Mathematica, ut est supputatio Horologiorum solarium Arithmetica, Basil. 1579. Illustratio Petri Nonii de crepusculis lb. 1583. Fabrica Quadrantis horarii & Geometrici. Institutio de usu Astronomici & Geometrici Quadrantis. Descriptio Cylindri, mobilem licèt, tamen eccentricum habentis Indicem. Descriptio horologij annularis. Habeo Historiam Reformationis Bullingeri, manu Fabricii hujus scriptam, & non contemnendis mantisis auctam. Edicta enim Magistratuum publica suis quoque locis omnia sunt inserta.
units.tr: Sebastian Fabricius, of Zurich, minister of the church at Hohenthurm (Hypervitoduranus). Our people praise him as a most faithful pastor, a pious and learned man, most diligent in every kind of business. There are extant some of his mathematical writings, such as the Calculation of Sundials, Arithmetic (Basel, 1579); an illustration of Pedro Nunes's work on twilight (1583); the construction of a horary and geometrical quadrant; an instruction on the use of the astronomical and geometrical quadrant; a description of a cylinder which has a movable but eccentric index; a description of an annular sundial. I have Bullinger's history of the Reformation, written in the hand of this Fabricius and enlarged with not contemptible additions; for the public edicts of the magistrates are inserted in all their places.

units.la: Forerus Conradus Vitoduranus. Medicum vocat Frisius in Biblioth. & Verbi Ministrum. Transtulit Gesnerii lib. 2. de quadrupedibus, & de Aquatilibus in Linguam Germanicam. 2. Stirpium differentias, ut Benedictus Textor digesit, non quidem è Dioscoridis solum, sed etiam Plinii & Theophrasti editionibus.
units.tr: Conrad Forer of Winterthur. Frisius in the Bibliotheca calls him a doctor of medicine and minister of the Word. He translated the second book of Gesner on quadrupeds, and the work on aquatic animals, into German. (2) The differences of plants, as Benedikt Textor arranged them, drawn not only from the editions of Dioscorides but also of Pliny and Theophrastus.

units.la: Frisius Iacobus, Iohannis F. Tigurinus; Philosophiæ primum, Ammiano datus Parastates, postea Theologiæ ab an. Chr 1576 ad 1610. Professor. scripsit A. Theologica. Orationem de officio Doctoris Ecclesiæ. Sermones feriæ Carolina habitos ad ministros agri Tigurini 1. De dignitate Ministrorum verbi DEI, & causis contemptus eorundem. 2. De servanda concordia Ministrorum Ecclesiæ. 3. Scripturæ sanctæ lectionem assiduam Ministris Ecclesiarum necessariam esse. 4. Ministros Ecclesiæ, ut professione, sic vita, non debere esse mundanos. Lectiones in Leviticum Msc. habeo. Compendium Examinis Theologici. B. philosophica. Iodoci VVillichii Dialecticae partem posteriorem ῥητορικὴν, & Rhetoricae ejusdem omnia praecepta in tabulas Methodicas redegit aliaque de quibus ipse in Biblioth. C. philologica. 1. Linguarum; Carmina aliquot Hebraica composuit in obitum Celeberrimorum Virorum D. Bullingeri, & Iohannis Halleri, illius Tigurini, hujus Bernensis Antistitis. 2. Historiae, quo pertinent Bibliotheca ipsius gemina, prior est Epitome, Simlerianae revisio, tum augmentatio ex Catalogis variis; praesertim Viennensi; posterior Nomenclatura, complectens omnis generis scriptorum libros 21. In quibus authorum opera secundum artes & disciplinas, earumque titulos & locos Communes disponuntur: Nomina vero operibus praefixa ordine Alphabetico recensentur. Illa continuata est ad an. Chr. 1583. digna quae ad nostram usque aetatem deduceretur.
units.tr: James Frisius, son of John Frisius of Zurich. He was first appointed to philosophy, a parastates to Ammianus, and afterwards was professor of theology from 1576 to 1610. He wrote: A. Theological works: an oration on the office of the teacher of the Church; sermons delivered at the Carolina feriae to the ministers of the Zurich countryside: (1) on the dignity of the ministers of the Word of God and the causes of contempt for them; (2) on keeping concord among the ministers of the Church; (3) that constant reading of Holy Scripture is necessary for the ministers of the Churches; (4) that the ministers of the Church, in life as in profession, ought not to be worldly. I have his lectures on Leviticus in manuscript. A compendium of the theological examination. B. Philosophical works: he reduced the latter part of Jodocus Willich's Dialectic, the rhetoric [ῥητορικήν], and all the precepts of Willich's rhetoric into methodical tables, and other things of which he himself speaks in the Bibliotheca. C. Philological works: (1) of languages: he composed some Hebrew poems on the death of the most celebrated men, Heinrich Bullinger, Zurich's chief minister, and Johann Haller, the Bernese chief minister. (2) Of histories: to this belong his twofold Bibliotheca. The former is an epitome, a revision of Simler's, then enlarged from various catalogues, especially the Vienna catalogue. The latter is a nomenclature containing books of writers of every kind, in 21 volumes, in which the works of authors are arranged according to arts and disciplines, with their titles and common places, and the names prefixed to the works are listed in alphabetical order. The former was continued to the year 1583, and deserves to be carried down to our own age.

units.la: Frisius Iohannes, superioris Pater, ad lacum Gryphaeum ditionis Tigurinae. Natus 1505. Parisiis & in Germania literis operam dedit, comes D. Gessneri, cujus ipse in Bibliotheca de anno 1545. meminit, primus post Reformationem, cum duobus aliis Sebastiano Guldibeck, & Benedicto Finslero, Collegiatae Ecclesiae Tigurinae stipendiarius fuit. Scholae postea Carolinae Classicae per annos 27. Moderator fidelissimus, obiit an. Chr. 1565. aetatis 60. hoc ornatus encomio, quod formator juventutis felicior non fuerit; sive mores & pietas spectentur, sive literae, teste Sigism. Gelenio; Epist. dedicator. lib. 7. Epigrammat. Graec. Quanquam & ipse commune fidelium operariorum expertus fatum, de quo in Lexico suo majori, voce sustento, o quam (scribit occasione phrascos Schola se sustentare) ibi miseriam vidi, quot labores hausi, quam animo molestiam cepi. Orem ad patiendum tolerandumve difficilem, praesertim cum ab iis a quibus non expectabas; imo quod multo gravius est, a Tua disciplina alumnis ἀχαρίστιας crimen te subire aperte intelligas! Labores ejus, quos edidit, erant 1. Theologici. Ex Hebraeo in Latinum transtulit Jobum, Psalmos, Proverbia, Canticum Canticorum, Ruth, Lamentationes, Ecclesiasten, Estheram, Prophetas majores, Prophetas minores; quam Interpretationem octo voluminibus comprehensam describi aliquando a discipulis suis curavit. Ego Proverbia & Iobum habeo manu Pellicani Fil. descripta, dono a nepote D. Iohanne Iacobo Frisio, M.D. & Collegij Carolini Praepósito, Collega nuper & Affine honoratissimo oblata cum exemplari Hebraico Roberti Stephani. Transtulit etiam in Linguam Germanicam Henrici Bullingeri in Evangelium Iohannis, de justificatione. Ex Commentin Matth. de resurrectione. Cumque praeter libros Hebraicos Venetiis à Bombergo emtos, Tatiani & Theophili Alexandrini libros contra Gentes Msc. advexisset, excudi etiam eos curavit. II. philosophici, & quidem vel Latini, vel Græci. Ex illis alii sunt translati. Ita vertit Maturini Corderii opus Latino Gallicum de corrupti sermonis emendatione, Carmen Iohannis Sulpitii Verulani de moribus & civilitate puerorum : selectas aliquot Epistolas Ciceronis, additis sententiis Iohannis Ludovici Vivis de ratione studiorum 1562. Annotationes in Vergilii Bucolica & Georgica, addita explicatione difficiliorum vocum Germanica. Composituit totius Musicæ breve compendium; cui accesserunt postea omnia Horatii carminum genera: Item heroica, elegiaca &c. quatuor vocibus ad Studiosorum usum accommodata 1554. Laudes honestæ matris familias ex Proverb. 31. carmine Germanico complexus est. Epigramma in poculum ventrosum & patulum; quod Germani Kopf vocant; quo seculi nostri intemperantiam describit. Laudatissimam impendit operam scribendis Lexicis Latinis. Primo dedit Roberti Stephani Epitomen Latino Gallicam, addita versione Germanica. Alterum deinde opus, vulgo Dictionarium Frisii majus semel privatis curis emissum ubique fere locorum placere cœpit. Observat filius, Iacobus, jam suo tempore an Chr 1583. à Froschovero plusquam decies fuisse typis in folio repetitum. Eidem tribuitur novum Dictionariolum puerorum Latino Germanicum, & vice versa: cui accesserunt rerum nomenclaturæ per classes digestæ multo copiosissime. In Græcis ei debemus, præter alia, quod compendium Grammaticæ Græcæ Iacobi Ceporini castigavit & auxit, iis, quæ maximè desiderabantur adjectis. Hesiodi etiam opera vertit Latinè notas Ceporini auxit, quibus ratio carminis declaratur 1562.
units.tr: John Frisius, father of the above, of the Lake Greifensee in the Zurich territory. Born in 1505, he devoted himself to letters in Paris and in Germany, and was a companion of Dr Gesner, whom he mentions in his Bibliotheca of 1545. He was the first, after the Reformation, to be a stipendiary of the Collegiate Church of Zurich, together with two others, Sebastian Guldibeck and Benedict Finsler. Afterwards he was for 27 years the most faithful head of the Carolina classical school. He died in 1565, aged 60, and was honoured with this praise, that there has been no happier moulder of youth; whether morals and piety are regarded, or letters, as Sigismund Gelenius testifies in the dedicatory epistle of his seventh book of Greek epigrams. Although he himself experienced the common lot of faithful workmen, of which he writes in his larger Lexicon, under the word sustento (writing on the occasion of the phrase schola se sustentare): Oh, what misery I saw there, what labours I endured, what vexation I felt in my mind. A burden hard to bear and to endure, especially when it comes from those from whom you did not expect it; indeed, what is much more serious, that you clearly understand you incur the charge of ingratitude [ἀχαριστίας] from your pupils in your own school! His published works were: 1. Theological: he translated from Hebrew into Latin Job, the Psalms, Proverbs, the Song of Songs, Ruth, Lamentations, Ecclesiastes, Esther, the greater Prophets and the lesser Prophets. He arranged for his pupils to copy out this translation, which fills eight volumes. I have Proverbs and Job, copied in the hand of Pellican the younger, a gift from his grandson, Dr John James Frisius, and provost of the Carolina college, offered by a colleague and most honourable kinsman lately, together with the Hebrew copy of Robert Estienne. He also translated into German Henry Bullinger's work on the Gospel of John, on justification, and his commentary on Matthew, on the resurrection. Since he had brought back from Venice, besides the Hebrew books bought from Bomberg, the books of Tatian and Theophilus of Alexandria against the Gentiles in manuscript, he also had them printed. II. Philosophical works, either Latin or Greek. Some of the Latin ones have been translated by others. Thus he rendered into Latin and French the work of Maturin Cordier on the correction of corrupt speech; the poem of Johannes Sulpicius of Veroli on the morals and civility of boys; a selection of some letters of Cicero, with the maxims of Juan Luis Vives on the method of study (1562); notes on Virgil's Bucolics and Georgics, with an explanation of the harder words in German. He composed a short compendium of all music, to which were later added all the kinds of Horace's odes, and also heroic, elegiac and other verse, adapted to four voices for the use of students (1554). He wove the praises of the honest mother of a household, from Proverbs 31, into German verse. An epigram on a big-bellied and wide-mouthed cup, which the Germans call a Kopf, describing the intemperance of our age. He devoted most praiseworthy effort to writing Latin lexicons. First he published an epitome of Robert Estienne's Latin-French dictionary, with a German translation added. Then his other work, commonly called Frisius's larger Dictionary, which was issued once by private effort, began to please almost everywhere. His son James observes that already in his own time, in 1583, it had been reprinted in folio by Froschauer more than ten times. A new little Latin-German dictionary for boys is also ascribed to him, and vice versa, to which were added lists of things arranged by classes, very copious indeed. Among the Greek works we owe to him, besides others, that he corrected and enlarged James Ceporinus's Greek grammar compendium, adding the things most in need. He also translated the works of Hesiod into Latin, and enlarged Ceporinus's notes, in which the method of the verse is explained (1562).

units.la: Frey Casparus Reipublicæ Tigurinæ quondam à Secretis, cujus situm Helvetiæ habemus ἀνεκδοτον.
units.tr: Frey Casparus, formerly Secretary of the Republic of Zurich. I have his situation of Helvetia [ἀνέκδοτον], unpublished.

units.la: Frey Felix Magister artium Parisiensis; Collegiatæ Ecclesiæ Præpositus, ab an Chr. 1518 ad 1555. quo obiit. Habeo statuta Collegii paulò ante Reformationem sub, & forte ab ipso recognita, quod ita habet: In nomine Domini. Nos Felix Frey Præpositus, totumque Capitulum Collegiatæ Ecclesiæ S. Felicis & Regulæ Præposituræ Thuricensis Constantiensis diœcesios, Deo nobis auxilium præstante, omnia, quæ pro decore domus Domini, ad Dei placitum, pro ampliore divini cultus augmento in nostro generali capitulo, quo pro aliis congregationibus majores nostræ Ecclesiæ tractare, ordinare, consuevimus in nostra capitulari synodo capitulariter congregati diligentiori præmissa consideratione perpendimus antiquum nostri chori breviarium olim Anno Domini 1260. opera Magistri Conradi de Mure, quondam Cantoris & Canonici hujus Ecclesiæ editum, propter multitudinem festorum &c. & servitiorum interim usque ad nostra tempora à nostris pradecessoribus & nobis institutorum & receptorum ulterius ad unguem observari nequaquam posse; Ad tollendas ergo confusiones, quas ex superabundantibus & defectuosis dicti aboliti breviarii regulis indies oriri liquidò conspicimus, matura deliberatione prahabita, unanimi omnium nostrum ad hoc accedente consensu præsens hoc directorium, modum & formam in nostra Ecclesia ritè divina peragendi, aut aliâs secundùm usum dictæ Ecclesiæ nostræ orandi breviter dilucidè & sine magna requisitione complectens atque peritorum Sacerdotum consuetudinis dicti nostri Chori judicio denuo revifum, tanquam nostræ Ecclesiæ membris non solùm utile sed & necessarium, acceptare, erigere & approbare duximus, prout tenore præsentium in nostrum & Ecclesiæ nostræ usum acceptamus, erigimus & in ipso facto approbamus, volentes denique, universos & singulos dictæ nostræ Ecclesiæ beneficiatos clericos, illo dicto directorio nostro tanquam authentico ad divina persolvenda inconcussè uti: dignum enim censemus, unum quemque orando aliáque divina peragendo se illi Ecclesiæ conformare, à quahabet honorem, & emolumentum percipit: Actum Thuregi in supra dicto nostro capitulo generali Anno Domini 1520. dieverò. 27. mensis Junii indictione 8. Pontificatus S. Domini nostri Domini, Leonis Papæ Decimi, anno octavo. Atque hanc quidem ... ex restauratis Collegii Carolini proximè ante Reformationem publicam, legibus depromere propterea placuit, quòd quædam contineret ... cujusmodi sunt: Antiqui chori Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Breviarii de anno 1260. authorem esse Conradum de Muri, quod quidem in exemplari authentico (admanus illud adhuc est) etiam fuit observatum; sed recentiori scriptura. Miror etiam, ipsum Conradum de Muri mentionem ejus in Catalogo operum non facere. 2. Inde ab anno 1260. ad 1520. superstitionem, per augmenta dierum festorum ita crevísse, ut vel propterea, mutatio hic aliqua fuerit instituenda. Confessio Capituli ingenua satis est. Cui accinit, qui sua manu primæ statim paginæ autographi Conradi, pergameno inscripti, addidit: Breviarium Chori Thuricensis anno 1260. compilatum: Vide, quid subinde accesserit, donec superstitio in immensum crevit! De hac Festorum multiplicatione etiam querulas dedimus voces Felicis Malleoli, alibi. De ipsis jam statutis agendi tempus non est. Ex una tamen adhuc cautela colligere liceat, quàm irreligiosè Templa à multis fuerint tum profanata: Turpem etiam (ita textus Statutorum sonat) illum abusum in quibusdam frequentatum Ecclesiis: quo in certis anni celebritatibus nonnulli cum mitra, baculo ac vestibus Pontificalibus more Episcoporum benedicant: alii ut Reges ac Duces induti: quod festum fatuorum vel innocentum, seu puerorum in quibusdam regionibus nuncupatur: alii larvas ac theatrales jocos: alii choreas ac tripudia marium ac mulierum ideo facientes, ut homines ad spectacula & cachinnationes moveant: alii comessationes & convivia illis praeparant. Haec sancta Synodus detestatur, statuit & jubet tam ordinarijs, quàm Ecclesiarum Decanis, Praepositis & Rectoribus sub poena suspensionis omnium proventuum Ecclesiasticorum trium mensium spacio: ne haec aut similia ludibria neque etiam mercantias seu negotiationes nundinarum in Ecclesia, quae domus orationis esse debet, & etiam in caemiterio exerceri amplius permittant: transgressoresque per censuram Ecclesiasticam, aliàque juris remedia punire non negligant.
units.tr: Frey Felix, Master of Arts of Paris, Provost of the collegiate church, from 1518 until his death in 1555. I have the statutes of the college, written shortly before the Reformation and perhaps revised by him personally. They read as follows: In the name of the Lord. We, Felix Frey, Provost, and the whole Chapter of the collegiate church of St. Felix and St. Regula, Provostry of Zurich, in the diocese of Constance, with God granting us help, having assembled in our chapter synod, as we are accustomed to do in our general chapter, where the greater matters of our church are dealt with and ordained together with the other congregations, have weighed with careful consideration everything that pertains to the honour of the house of the Lord, according to God's pleasure and for the greater increase of divine worship. We have considered that the ancient breviary of our choir, published in the year of the Lord 1260 through the work of Master Conrad of Muri, formerly cantor and canon of this church, on account of the multitude of feasts etc. and services, cannot be observed to the letter in our time, as it was instituted and received by our predecessors and by us. Therefore, to remove the confusions which we clearly see arising daily from the superfluous and defective rules of the said abolished breviary, after mature deliberation and with the unanimous consent of all of us, we have judged it right to accept, establish and approve this present directorium, a brief, clear and undemanding guide to the manner and form of performing the divine office in our church, or otherwise of praying according to the custom of our church, revised anew by the judgement of the skilled priests of our choir's custom, as useful and indeed necessary for the members of our church. By the tenor of these presents we accept, establish and in fact approve it for our use and that of our church. Finally, wishing all and each of the beneficed clergy of our said church to use the said directorium of ours, as authentic, unshakably in performing the divine offices, for we think it right that each one, in praying and performing the divine offices, should conform himself to that church from which he receives honour and emolument. Done at Zurich in the aforesaid general chapter of ours, in the year of the Lord 1520, on the 27th day of June, in the 8th indiction, in the eighth year of the pontificate of our holy lord, Pope Leo the Tenth. I have thought it fitting to draw this from the restored laws of the Collegium Carolinum shortly before the public Reformation, because it contains certain things, such as: that the author of the ancient breviary of the choir of the Church of Zurich of 1260 was Conrad of Muri, which indeed was observed in the authentic copy (which is still at hand), but in a more recent hand. I also wonder that Conrad of Muri himself does not mention it in his catalogue of works. (2) From the year 1260 to 1520 superstition grew by the addition of feast days so much that for this reason alone some change had to be instituted here. The confession of the chapter is frank enough. To this agrees the one who, in his own hand, added on the first page of the autograph of Conrad, written on parchment: The breviary of the Zurich choir compiled in 1260. See what was added afterwards, until superstition grew to an immense size! I have also raised complaints about this multiplication of feasts elsewhere, in the words of Felix Malleolus. There is no time to deal with the statutes themselves now. Yet from one caution alone it may be gathered how irreverently the temples were then profaned by many: Also (so the text of the statutes runs) that shameful abuse, practised in certain churches, by which on certain annual celebrations some bless with mitre, staff and pontifical vestments in the manner of bishops, others dress up as kings and dukes, which in some regions is called the feast of fools or of the innocents or of boys, others (perform) masks and theatrical jests, others dances and leapings of men and women, done so as to move people to spectacle and laughter, others prepare feastings and banquets for them. This holy Synod detests these things, and decrees and orders, under penalty of suspension of all ecclesiastical revenues for three months, both ordinaries and deans, provosts and rectors of churches, that they no longer permit such mockeries or similar things, nor trade or business of fairs, to be carried on in the church, which ought to be a house of prayer, nor even in the churchyard, and that they not neglect to punish transgressors by ecclesiastical censure and other remedies of law.

units.la: Fueslinus Johannes, scripsit librum adversus Hieronymum Gebvvilerum, defendentem Ecclesiam Romanam, ejusque ceremonias Tig. 1524. cum praefatione Zuinglij. Idem est author Annalium Helveticorum; quorum Bullingerus meminit in Antiquit. Tigur. Appendice. Ἀνώνυμον quidem appellat; sed Iohannem Fueslinum esse, patet ex collatione autographi Fueslinian (à pag. 77. ad 138. quae D. Bullingerus omnia textui suo inseruit) quod in haeredum adhuc manibus est; apographum verò, eorundem beneficio, in Bibliotheca Civica. Natus est 1477. denatus 1538. Libri initium fecit 1533. finem cum ipsa vita.
units.tr: Fueslinus Johannes wrote a book against Hieronymus Gebwiler, who defended the Roman Church and its ceremonies, Zurich 1524, with a preface by Zwingli. He is also the author of the Helvetian Annals, which Bullinger mentions in the appendix to his Antiquities of Zurich. Bullinger calls it anonymous [Ἀνώνυμον], but that it is by John Fuesslin is clear from a comparison with Fuesslin's autograph (from page 77 to 138, all of which Bullinger incorporated into his own text), which is still in the hands of his heirs; a copy, by their kindness, is in the Civic Library. He was born in 1477 and died in 1538. He began the book in 1533 and finished it with his life.

units.la: Fueslinus Petrus, superioris frater, natus 1482. vir fortis, & praelio ad Marignanum 1515, probatus. Iter suscepit an. Chr. 1523. aetatis 41. Hierosolymitanum, ibique (ita habent verba testimonii à F. Iacobo de Porta, ordinis Minorum, Regularis observantiae Sacri Conventus Montis Sion Guardiano, exhibiti) sanctissimum Domini nostri Jesu Christi sepulchrum, sanctos Calvariae, Sion, Oliveti montes, intemeratae Mariae virginis sepulturam in valle Josaphat, Dominica nativitatis ac praesepii locum sacratissimum, caeteraque terra sancta loca a modernis peregrinis visitari solita, in quibus sua ineffabili Clementia Salvator noster humani generis salutem operatus est, manibus propriis contrectavit, visitavit pariter & adoravit. Describit iter, quod uno absolvit anno, sed nunquam editum, diligenter. Pro ratione illius temporis multa observavit tam superstitiosa, quam Historica, quae, usum suum habent varium, atque multiplicem. Monstratum sibi interalia, scribit, a Monachis locum, in quo & vitae diem claudisset B. Virgo, & Eidem Evangelista Iohannes frequenter Missam legisset: Indulgentias Visitatoribus promitti pro culpa & poena: locum, ubi Iudaei, duodecim Apostolis corpus B. V. ad sepulchrum deducturis eripere voluerunt: sepulchrum Mariae, sacello ornatum &c. Fabricam etiam sive consecturam agnorum Dei, Hierosolymitanis Monachis usitatam prolixe describit. Discalceati, inquit, terram ex locis sanctis omnibus colligunt, in pulverem redigunt, aqua postea ex Iordane promta macerant, massam conficiunt, indeque Agnos Dei, quos peregrinis distribuunt. Primo in Catalogo materiae ponitur terra Damascena, ex qua Adam formatus: deinde vallis lachrymarum, ubi Adam annos centum sua deploravit peccata: nativitatis, mortis, sepulturae Mariae &c. Duos secum attulit ex terra sancta Fueslinus, sed cereos, quorum alter in manibus haeredum, alter mihi aliquando donatus fuit, a viro doctissimo D Petro Fueslino, Theologiae Catecheticae Professore solertissimo, de quo P. III. Hodeg pag 241. Priori massae multum deferunt. Unde idem ille, qui Catalogum scripsit, postea subjicit: Dis ist nit ein gering ding/ und darumb so hand die agnos Dei in grossen ehren/ dannes ein köstlich ding ist in einem hauß/ und mögends denen auch sagen / woraus die Agnus Dei gemacht sind. Ist ein glückhafftig ding in einem hauß. Sed & hoc observavi, Turcas & Arabes λῃστεύσις ita viatorum insidiari bonis, ut ne quidem vinum, cujus tamen usum Muhammedismus prohibet, tutum ab iis fit: id quod duobus probat exemplis. Idem, bellum superioris seculi descripsit vir, ipsis etiam tum adversariis honoratus & acceptus, Capellanum, cui interfuit, diligenter etiam & bona fide.
units.tr: Fueslinus Petrus, brother of the above, born 1482, a brave man, proved in battle at Marignano in 1515. He undertook a journey to Jerusalem in the year of Christ 1523, at the age of 41, and there (as the words of the testimony given by Fr. James of Porta, of the Order of Friars Minor, guardian of the Holy Convent of Mount Zion of the regular observance, state) with his own hands touched, visited and likewise adored the most holy sepulchre of our Lord Jesus Christ, the holy mounts of Calvary, Zion and Olivet, the burial place of the immaculate Virgin Mary in the valley of Jehoshaphat, the place of the Lord's nativity and crib, most sacred, and the other holy places of the Holy Land, which modern pilgrims are accustomed to visit, in which our Saviour by his ineffable clemency wrought the salvation of the human race. He describes the journey, which he completed within one year, carefully, but it was never published. In keeping with the taste of that time, he observed many things, both superstitious and historical, which have various and manifold uses. Among other things he writes that the monks showed him the place where the Blessed Virgin had also ended her days, and where the Evangelist John had often read Mass; that indulgences for visitors were promised for guilt and punishment; the place where the Jews wanted to snatch the body of the Blessed Virgin from the twelve Apostles who were bearing it to the sepulchre; the sepulchre of Mary, adorned with a little chapel, etc. He also describes at length the making, or consecration, of the Agnus Dei, customary among the Jerusalem monks. The barefoot monks, he says, gather earth from all the holy places, reduce it to powder, then steep it in water taken from the Jordan, make a paste, and from it make Agnus Dei which they distribute to pilgrims. In the first place in the catalogue of materials is Damascene earth, from which Adam was formed; then the valley of tears, where Adam lamented his sins for a hundred years; and the nativity, death and burial of Mary, etc. Fuesslin brought back two candles from the Holy Land, of which one is in the hands of his heirs and the other was once given to me by the most learned Mr. Peter Fuesslin, a most diligent professor of catechetical theology, about whom see P. III, Hodegus, p. 241. They attach great value to the first paste. Hence that same man who wrote the catalogue afterwards adds: This is no small thing, and therefore they hold the Agnus Dei in great honour, for it is a precious thing in a house, and they can tell those who ask what the Agnus Dei are made of. It is a thing of good fortune in a house. But I have also observed this, that the Turks and Arabs lie in wait for travellers to plunder their goods, so that not even wine, the use of which Muhammadanism nevertheless forbids, is safe from them; this he proves with two examples. He also described a war of the previous century, diligently and in good faith, as a man honoured and accepted even by his adversaries of that time, as the chaplain who took part in it.

units.la: Furst Conradus, Tigurinus, Caesareae Majestatis Medicus & eques, scripsit opuscula genethliaca, Mathematicae observationis Nativitatum Francisci Mariae Sforzia, Vice Comitis Papiae, & Caesaris Sforzia filij, Ludovici Mariae; quae MSS. exiterunt aliquando apud Christophorum Clauserum.
units.tr: Furst Conradus, of Zürich, physician and knight to the Imperial Majesty, wrote short treatises on nativities, mathematical observations of the births of Francis Maria Sforza, Vice-Count of Pavia, and of Ludovicus Maria, son of Caesar Sforza. These manuscripts at one time came into the hands of Christophorus Clauserus.

units.la: Gesnerus Conradus, Tigurinus, nascitur Tiguri 1516. Medicus Philosophus clarissimus Professor Collegii Carolini Physicus ab an. Chr. 1558, ad 1565 quo peste mortuus 13 Decemb. aetatis an. 49. decessit. Duo in hoc authore sunt observanda, utrumque mirandum magis, quam imitandum. primum, quod juvenis non eam observavit Methodum, quae ad solidam eruditionem viam sterneret, sed vagam & tumultuariam; alterum, quod inter scriptores suae aetatis fuerit πολυγραφώτατος, etsi vix mediocrem attigerit aetatis terminum. De priori ipsum audire placet, ex priori Bibliothecae Editione, ita loquentem: Praeceptores puero & adolescenti in patria mihi contigere Clarissimi viri, Osvvaldus Myconius, Theodorus Bibliander, Petrus Dasypodius, Iohannes Iacobus Ammianus, Gymnasij nostri Scholarcha, & Rodolphus Collinus. His Doctoribus a primis rudimentis ad medicorum utriusque Linguae cognitionem institutus sum, praecipue ab Ammiano doctissimo viro, qui me triennium integrum eximia liberalitate domi suae gratuito fovit, & erudivit familiariter.
