Deum supplex venero, ut sua porrò benedictione meos qualescunque prosequatur labores, ad sanctissimi Nominis sui gloriam, & tum veritatis confirmationem, tum bonarum literarum incrementum. Libenter plantabo & rigabo, modò cælestis Paterfamilias largiatur clementissimum αὐξανὲιν. Ordine jam, quæque in lucem prodierunt opuscula, recensere lubet.
units.tr: 16. 1657. 17. 1658. 18. 19. 1659. ...I shall satisfy. Of these I have published both the Primitiae Heidelbergenses and a bundle of Disputations from Heidelberg, choosing a selection of topics for each. In the former I set out disputations on explaining the middle terms of Scripture; on the efficient and material cause of the Reformation; and on the use of Hebrew writings in the New Testament. I added Irenic Meletemata; Sabbathismus, or dissertations on the Jewish, Christian, Marian, Muhammadan and Gentile Sabbath, and Idolographia of the Old Testament. In the latter I treated the resurrection of the dead; the marks of the visible Church; the translations of the Bible into various vernacular languages, occasioned by the English work; the Oriental names of God: the attributes of the Hebrews. There were also added two centuries of philological-theological questions on the principles of the Christian faith in general and the Word of God in particular; a Theological Course set out in the method of Altingius, with an oration on the requirements of a theologian. These were published at Heidelberg in the year of Christ 1661, as it was ending. On my return home I gathered the remaining disputations into an Ennead, with some public academic programmes added. The Ennead contains the following disputations: on the spurious books of the Old Testament, especially the prophecy of Enoch, and the Samaritans' book of Joshua, and from it a compendium of Samaritan theology, Askimasia Abrahami [Ασκιμασια]; Paradise; the necessity of the ecclesiastical ministry; Baptism; Melchizedek, with a short apology attached against the Jesuit Labbe; on the causes of the Lord's Supper, to which is added a specimen of sacred analysis, on the sense of the words This is my body; on the charge of excessive rashness against Leo Allatius, and the perpetual dissent of the Latin and Greek Churches. To this is appended a compendium of Jewish theology, mentioned above. At home I gradually girded myself again for the same studies. To keep our students occupied with exercises no less useful than varied, I set up philological and theological disputations, both topical and textual, of which we shall have, I hope, another bundle before long. I preferred that our synodal disputations be textual, so that not only students but others too might have a method and manner of explaining Sacred Scripture systematically and of bringing it back to practical use. The chief disputations published were on theology, on the virtues of a good interpreter, on theological sophisms, on the reading and interpretation of Scripture, and on catechetical theology. I added a specimen of Sacred Philology, from chapter 5 of Matthew in its proper place. Driven also by the constant urging of friends, I have undertaken the Bibliothecarius, which is already at the press, or a Treatise, both on libraries in general and on theological libraries in particular; likewise the Origins of the Carolingian School of the Tigurines, or a historical demonstration of the school of the Tigurine Republic to be founded by Charles, with the Tigurine Library, or a catalogue of those who have become famous for their writings, either at Zurich or in Zurich's public services, over many centuries. I humbly pray God that he will continue with his blessing to bless my labours, such as they are, to the glory of his most holy Name, both for the confirmation of the truth and the growth of good letters. I shall gladly plant and water, provided the heavenly Householder graciously grants the increase [αὐξάνειν]. Now I am pleased to list, in order, the little works that have come to light.

units.la: I. Exercitationes Anti-Morinianæ, de Pentateucho Samaritano, ejusque Vdentica authentia; Oppositæ Canonicæ ejusdem αὐθεντία, à Ioh. Morino Blesensi, gregationis Oratorij, ut vocant, Presbyterorum, temerè asserta: In quibus, non tantùm firmis rationibus Pentateuchus Samariticus magno conatu ab ipso Canonizatus convellitur; Apographum vitiosum ex Hebræo autographo demonstratur; sed etiam nonnulla S. Scripturæ & antiquitatis loca difficiliora de Samaritanorum Religione scriptis, moribus illustrantur, atque ex monumentis variis eruuntur. Quibus 2. accedit Epitome omnium Capitum LIBRI IOSVÆ h.e. Chronici illius Samaritani, quod ex Legato magni Scaligeri, in instructissima Leidensi Bibliotheca Arabicè contextum, sed Samaritico-characterè exaratum, asservatur. Tiguri, Typis Bodmerianis. 4.
units.tr: I. Anti-Morinian Exercitations, on the Samaritan Pentateuch and its divine authenticity, opposed to the canonical authority of the same, rashly asserted by John Morinus of Blois, of the congregation of the Oratory, as they call it, of the Presbyters: in which not only is the Samaritan Pentateuch, which he tried with great effort to make canonical, overthrown by firm arguments; a faulty copy is shown to derive from the Hebrew autograph; but also some difficult passages of Holy Scripture and antiquity concerning the religion and customs of the Samaritans are illustrated and drawn out from various monuments. To these is added, in the second place, an epitome of all the chapters of the Book of Joshua, that is, of that Samaritan chronicle which, from the legacy of the great Scaliger, is kept in the very well-stocked Leiden Library, written in Arabic but set down in Samaritan characters. Zurich, Bodmer press. 4to.

units.la: Erotematum Linguæ Sanctæ, libri duo, cum appendice Aphorismorum ad lectionem Bibliorum Hebraicorum, Isagogicorum. ib. 8.
units.tr: Erotemata of the Holy Language, two books, with an appendix of aphorisms, introductory, for the reading of the Hebrew Bible. Zurich. 8vo.

units.tr: 2. Hodegos christianus, showing the way and method of investigating the faith, with the truth and purity which obtained in the first three centuries after Christ's birth; Part I, on Sacred Scripture, its authority, office and properties. Zurich, 4to.

units.tr: The same writing, Part III, on images, justification, the merit of works, Purgatory, indulgences, etc. Ibid.

units.la: 2. Thesaurus Philologicus, seu clavis Scripturæ; qua quicquidferè Orientalium, Hebræorum maximè & Arabum habent monumenta, de religione, ejusque variis speciebus, Iudaismo, Samaritanismo, Muhammedismo, Gentilismo; de Theologia & Theologis, verbo Dei ἀγγέλφω & ἐγγεγράφω, varijs Bibliorum exemplaribus: Fontium Hebraeorum integritate: Scripturæ Accidentibus, Partibus, Distinctionibus, sensu & commentarijs: De Thargumim seu Paraphrasibus Chaldaicis, Syriacis, Arabicis, Persicis, Samaritanis, Græcis & Latinis. De Masora & Kabbala: de singulorum V.T. librorum, Canonicorum, & Apocryphorum authoritate in genere, & de Lege, Prophetis & Prophetijs infpecie breviter & Aphoristicè ita referatur & aperitur,ut multiplex inde ad Philologiæ & Theologiæ Studiosos, fructus redundare posset. Bodmer. 4. Secunda jam prodijt Editio ex eorundem Typographia Orientali, ubi Samaritica, Arabica, Syriaca, suisquæque nativis characteribus exprimuntur.
units.tr: 2. Philological Thesaurus, or Key to Scripture; in which nearly whatever monuments the Orientals have, especially the Hebrews and the Arabs, concerning religion and its various kinds, Judaism, Samaritanism, Muhammadanism, Gentilism; concerning theology and theologians, the Word of God [ἀγγέλφω and ἐγγεγράφω], the various copies of the Bibles, the integrity of the Hebrew sources, the accidents, parts, divisions, sense and commentaries of Scripture; concerning the Targums or Chaldean, Syriac, Arabic, Persian, Samaritan, Greek and Latin paraphrases; concerning the Masorah and Kabbalah; concerning the authority of each of the Old Testament books, canonical and apocryphal, in general, and concerning the Law, the Prophets and prophecies in particular, is treated briefly and in aphoristic form and laid open, so that a manifold fruit might spring from it for students of philology and theology. Bodmer, 4to. A second edition has now appeared from the same Oriental press, in which the Samaritan, Arabic and Syriac are printed in their own native characters.

units.la: Commercium Epistolicum Helveticum, quo breviter & amicè disceptatur, an & quatenus, salva pace, de religione disceptare in Helvetia liceat: Apologeticum est scriptum saperioris Hodegetici, contra P. Laurentium Forerum, Iesuitam.
units.tr: Helvetic Epistolary Exchange, in which it is briefly and amicably debated whether, and to what extent, it is permitted to dispute about religion in Helvetia while keeping the peace. It is an apologetic writing supporting the earlier Hodegeticus, against P. Laurentius Forerus, a Jesuit.

units.la: 1. Historiæ Ecclesiasticæ Novi Testamenti Enneas, seu Pars. I. qua res Christianorum, Judæorum, Gentilium, Muhammedanorum, juxta novem, post natum Christum, primorum seculorum seriem, breviter, succinctè & Aphoristicè primò proponuntur, deinde fusius explicantur: Capita etiam doctrinæ, tum veræ, per commodam & luculentam uniuscujusque seculi συμβίβασιν; tum falsæ, per ἔλεγχον subjiciuntur, sicque ad multiplicem usum, necessariámque rerum notitiam applicantur. 8. Tiguri, & Hanovie Edit. 2. Schaufelb. sumtib.
units.tr: 1. Ninefold Ecclesiastical History of the New Testament, or Part I, in which the affairs of Christians, Jews, Gentiles and Muhammadans are first set out briefly, succinctly and aphoristically, according to the series of the first nine centuries after the birth of Christ, and then explained more fully. The doctrines also are added, both true, by a convenient and clear συμβίβασις [symbibasis, reconciliation] for each century, and false, by an ἔλεγχος [elenchos, refutation]; and so they are applied to a manifold use and to the necessary knowledge of affairs. 8vo. Zurich and Hanau, 2nd edition. At the expense of Schaufelberger.

units.la: 2. Historiæ Ecclesiasticæ Novi Testamenti, Dyas, seu pars II. qua res &c. juxta duorum X. & XI. post Christum natum seculorum seriem, &c. proponuntur.
units.tr: 2. Ecclesiastical History of the New Testament, Dyas, or Part II, in which the affairs, etc. are set out according to the series of the tenth and eleventh centuries after the birth of Christ, etc.

units.la: 3. Historia Orientalis, quæ ex variis Orientalium monumentis collecta, agit I. de Muhammedifmo, ejusque causis tum procreantibus, tum conservantibus, inprimis Muhammede, ejus parentibus, Majoribus, patria, nativitate, educatione, Pseudoprophetia, æmulis, dogmatibus, Hegira, præliis, successoribus, morte. II. De Saracenifmo, seu religione veterum Arabum. III. De Chaldaismo, seu superstitione Nabatæorum, Chaldæorum, Charranæorum. IV. De statu Christianorum & Judæorum tempore orti & nati Muhammedifmi. V. De variis inter ipsos Muhammedanos, circa Religionis dogmata, & administrationem, sententiis, Schismatis, & Hæresibus excitatis. VI. Accessit, ex occasione Genealogia Muhammedis, plenior illustratio Taarichbene Adam, qua, ex ipsis Arabum scriptis, vita & res gestæ Prophetæphetarum, Patriarcharum, quorundam etiam Apostolorum, Regum Persia, aliorumque ab Adamo ad Muhammedis usque natales in orbe degentium & regentium, explicantur. 4. Tigur. Bodmer.
units.tr: 3. Oriental History, which, collected from various Oriental monuments, treats I. of Muhammadism, and of its causes, both those that produced it and those that sustained it, above all Muhammad himself, his parents, ancestors, homeland, birth, upbringing, false prophecy, rivals, doctrines, Hegira, battles, successors and death. II. Of Saracenism, or the religion of the ancient Arabs. III. Of Chaldaism, or the superstition of the Nabataeans, Chaldeans and Harranians. IV. Of the state of the Christians and Jews at the time when Muhammadism arose and was born. V. Of the opinions and schisms and heresies stirred up among the Muhammadans themselves concerning the doctrines and administration of their religion. VI. There is added, occasioned by the genealogy of Muhammad, a fuller illustration of the Taarichbene Adam, in which, from the Arabs' own writings, the life and deeds are explained of the prophets, patriarchs, some apostles, kings of Persia, and others who lived and ruled in the world from Adam down to the birth of Muhammad. 4to. Zurich, Bodmer.

units.la: Grammaticæ Chaldæo-Syriacæ libri duo, cum triplici appendice Chaldaa, Syra, & Rabbinica. 8. Ib.
units.tr: Two books of a Chaldee-Syriac Grammar, with a threefold appendix on Chaldee, Syriac and Rabbinic. 8vo. Ibid.

units.la: 1. Historiæ Ecclesiasticæ Trias, seu Pars III. quarum Christianorum, &c. juxta trium XII.XIII. & XIV. post Christum natum seculorum seriem proponuntur. 8. Schufelb.
units.tr: 1. Ecclesiastical History, Trias, or Part III, in which the affairs of the Christians, etc. are set out according to the series of the twelfth, thirteenth and fourteenth centuries after the birth of Christ. 8vo. Schaufelberger.

units.la: 2. Analecta Historico Theologica, octo dissertationibus proposita 1. de necessitate Reformationis, superiori seculo instituta. 2. De Heptaplis Parisiensibus, sive Bibliis Regiis. 3. De jubilæo Judaico, Christiano, & Pontificio. 4. Judicia Hebræorum & Arabum de terræ motibus. 5. De usu Linguæ Hebraæ contra Pontificios & Anabaptistas. 6 De usu Linguæ Arabicæ in Theologia, Medicina, juris prudentia, Philosophia & Philologia. 7. Introductio ad lectionem Patrum. 8. De usu Patrum. Accessit appendix, de Cyrilli, Patriarchæ Constantinopolitani confessione, Scripturæ & Patrum Testimoniis vestita: vitæ, scriptis, & Martyrio. 8. Bodmer. Tiguri.
units.tr: 2. Historico-Theological Analecta, presented in eight dissertations: 1. On the necessity of the Reformation undertaken in the previous century. 2. On the Parisian Heptapla, or the Royal Bibles. 3. On the Jewish, Christian and Papal jubilee. 4. Judgments of the Hebrews and Arabs on earthquakes. 5. On the use of the Hebrew language against the Papists and Anabaptists. 6. On the use of the Arabic language in theology, medicine, jurisprudence, philosophy and philology. 7. Introduction to the reading of the Fathers. 8. On the use of the Fathers. There is added an appendix on the confession of Cyril, Patriarch of Constantinople, clothed in the testimonies of Scripture and the Fathers: his life, writings and martyrdom. 8vo. Bodmer, Zurich.

units.la: 1. Dissertationum miscellanearum πεντας 1. De abusu Patrum. 2. Catalogus scriptorum Ecclesiasticorum suppositiorum. 3. Specimen Philosophiæ Historicæ. 4. Irenicum Helveticum. 5. Methodus legendi Historias Helveticas. 8. Bodmer. Sæpe citavi nomine Partis II. Analector.
units.tr: 1. Miscellaneous Dissertations, Pentas [πεντάς, a group of five]: 1. On the abuse of the Fathers. 2. A catalogue of spurious ecclesiastical writers. 3. A specimen of Historical Philosophy. 4. The Helvetic Irenicum. 5. A method of reading Helvetic histories. 8vo. Bodmer. I have often cited it under the name of Part II of the Analecta.

units.la: 2. Historiæ Ecclesiasticæ N. T. Pars IV. seu seculum XV. quo res Christianorum, &c. Cingü-Chanicorum seu Tartarorum breviter, &c. proponuntur. Accedunt, Andreæ Archiepiscopi Crainensis & Cardinalis gesta, commentariis Petri Numagen, Trevirensis, illustrata, & primum nunc ex Bibliotheca Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ in lucem edita.
units.tr: 2. Ecclesiastical History of the New Testament, Part IV, or the fifteenth century, in which the affairs of the Christians, etc., and of the Cingu-Chanids, that is, the Tartars, are briefly set out, etc. To this are added, the deeds of Andreas, Archbishop of Krajina and Cardinal, illustrated by the commentaries of Petrus Numagen of Trier, and now first published from the Library of the Zurich Church.

units.la: 1. Iuris Hebræorum Leges 261. juxta Νομοθεσίας Mosaicæ ordinem atque seriem depromta, & ad Judæorum mentem, ductu R. Levi BarZelonitæ, indicato cujuslibet præcepti fundamento, materia, Subjecto, fine, Accidentibus, transgressoris pœna, ita propositæ, ut non Theologiæ tantum & Linguæ Hebraeæ; sed & juris Studiosis magno usui esse possint. 4. Tig. Bodmer.
units.tr: 1. Laws of the Hebrews, 261 in number, taken from the order and series of the Mosaic legislation, and set out according to the mind of the Jews, under the guidance of R. Levi ben Gershon, with the foundation, matter, subject, end, accidents and penalty for the transgressor of each precept indicated, so arranged that they may be of great use not only to students of theology and the Hebrew language, but also to students of law. 4to. Zurich, Bodmer.

units.la: 2. Historiæ Ecclesiasticæ N. T. pars V. seu seculi XVI. quo res Christianorum potissimum; Orientalium & Occidentalium breviter proponuntur, deinde fusius ita explicantur, ut Reformationis Ecclesiasticæ superiori seculo institutæ necessitas haud obscure evincatur. 5. Tig. Schufelb.
units.tr: 2. Ecclesiastical History of the New Testament, Part V, or the sixteenth century, in which the affairs of the Christians, chiefly of the Eastern and Western churches, are briefly set out, and then explained more fully, so that the necessity of the ecclesiastical Reformation undertaken in the previous century is made clear beyond doubt. 8vo. Zurich, Schaufelberger.

units.la: 1. Collegium Sapientiæ restitutum, sive Oratio secularis de Collegio Sapientiæ, quod Heidelbergæ est: Accesserunt notæ ejusdem de Heidelbergensi Academia, origine, Progressu, privilegiis, &c. 4. Heidelbergæ, typis & impensis AEgid. Valteri.
units.tr: 1. The Restored College of Wisdom, or a secular oration on the College of Wisdom, which is at Heidelberg. Notes are added on the same Heidelberg Academy, its origin, progress, privileges, etc. 4to. Heidelberg, printed and paid for by Aegidius Walter.

units.la: Smegma Orientale Sordibus Barbarismi, contemtui præsertim Linguarum Orientalium oppositum: ubi 1. de occasione scripti. 2. Contemtu Linguæ & Scripturæ sacræ superioribus seculis. 3. De usu Linguarum Hebraica, Chaldaica, Syriaca, Arabica, Persica, AEthiopica in genere multiplici. 4. De Linguarum confusione, earundemque in Ecclesia pretio. 5. De usu Linguarum Hebraicæ, Chaldaicæ, Arabicæ, Persicæ, AEthiopicæ, AEgyptiacæ, in translatione Sacræ Scripturæ. 6. De usu Linguarum Orientalium, Syriacæ maximè & Arabicæ in collatione scripturæ sacræ; instituto examine ex Deuteronomio Heptaplorum Parisiensium. 7. De usu Linguæ Arabicæ in restituendis vocibus Hebraeis vel plane obsoletis, vel raro in contextu sacro obviis. 8. De usu Linguarum Orientalium in Theologia Historica; ubi ordine, veteris Testamenti Historia Prosopographicè ex Hebraeorum & Arabum, Patriciis cumprimis, Elmacini, & annalium Samaritanorum scriptis ἀνεκδότοις, ad Iudicum usque tempora pertexitur. Heidelb. Typ. & impens. Adriani Vyngard.
units.tr: Oriental Smegma, opposed to the filth of barbarism and especially to the contempt of the Oriental languages, in which: 1. The occasion of the writing is given. 2. The contempt of language and Scripture in earlier centuries. 3. On the manifold use of the Hebrew, Chaldee, Syriac, Arabic, Persian and Ethiopic languages in general. 4. On the confusion of languages, and their value in the Church. 5. On the use of the Hebrew, Chaldee, Arabic, Persian, Ethiopic and Egyptian languages in the translation of Holy Scripture. 6. On the use of the Oriental languages, especially Syriac and Arabic, in comparing Scripture; with an examination of Deuteronomy from the Parisian Heptapla as a model. 7. On the use of the Arabic language in restoring Hebrew words either quite obsolete or rarely found in the sacred text. 8. On the use of the Oriental languages in historical theology; where, in order, the history of the Old Testament is woven together prosopographically, from the writings of the Hebrews and Arabs, especially Elmacinus, and from unpublished Samaritan annals, down to the times of the Judges. Heidelberg, printed and paid for by Adrian Vyngaert.

units.la: 1. Promtuarium, sive Bibliotheca Orientalis, exhibens Catalogum, sive Centurias aliquot, tam authorum, quàm librorum Hebraicorum, Syriacorum, Arabicorum, AEgyptiacorum; addita mantissa Bibliothecarum aliquot Europaearum, &c. 4. Heidelb. Typ. & impensf. Adriani VVyngaerden.
units.tr: 1. Promptuarium, or Oriental Library, showing a catalogue, or several centuries, of authors and books in Hebrew, Syriac, Arabic and Egyptian; with an appendix on several European libraries, etc. 4to. Heidelberg. Printed and published by Adrian Wyngaerden.

units.la: 2. Grammatica quatuor Linguarum Hebraicae, Chaldaicae, Syriacae & Arabicae Harmonica, ita perspicuè instituta, ut ad Linguam Hebraicam, tanquam matrem caeterarum etiam ceu filiarum, Linguarum, accommodentur praecepta. Cui accedit Technologia Lingua Arabica Historico-Theologica. 4. lb.
units.tr: 2. A harmonious grammar of the four languages, Hebrew, Chaldee, Syriac and Arabic, so clearly set out that the rules are adapted to Hebrew as the mother of the others, as to her daughters. To which is added a technology of the Arabic language, historical and theological. 4to. Ibid.

units.la: 1. Cippi Hebraici, sive Hebraeorum, tam veterum (Prophetarum, Patriarcharum) quàm recentiorum, Tannaeorum, Amoraeorum, Rabbinorum monumenta, Hebraicè à Iudaeo quodam, teste oculato, tum intra, tum etiam extra terram sanctam observata & conscripta; nunc verò Latinitate donata, notisque illustrata. Accedunt Dissertationes
units.tr: 1. Hebrew Cippi, that is, monuments of the Hebrews, both ancient (of the Prophets and Patriarchs) and more recent (of the Tannaim, Amoraim and Rabbis), written in Hebrew by a certain Jew, an eyewitness, observed and recorded both inside and outside the Holy Land; now translated into Latin and illustrated with notes. Added are dissertations

units.la: A. De variis Orientis monumentis, mensuris & inscriptionibus. B. De nummis Orientalium, Hebraeorum maximè & Arabum. III. Editio secunda, auctior prodijt Heidelbergae, Typis Samuelis Broun, Acad. Typog. & Bibliopolae Angli M DC LXII.
units.tr: A. On various monuments, measures and inscriptions of the East. B. On the coins of the Orientals, especially of the Hebrews and Arabs. Third edition, enlarged, published at Heidelberg by Samuel Broun, printer to the Academy and bookseller of England, 1662.

units.la: 2. Primitiae Heidelbergenses, sive Tomus disputationum, à restituta Academia ab authore tam publicè, quàm privatim habitarum. 2. De medijs explicandae Scripturae Sacrae. 2. de Reformationis causa efficiente & Materiali. 3. De usu Scriptorum Hebraicorum in N. Testamento 4. Meletemata Irenica. 5. Sabbathismus, sive dissertationes de Sabbatho Iudaico, Christiano, Mariano, Muhammedico, Gentili. 6. Idolographia Veteris Testamenti. 4. Ægid. VValt. Heidelb.
units.tr: 2. First Fruits of Heidelberg, that is, a volume of disputations held by the author, both publicly and privately, since the Academy was restored. 1. On the means of explaining Holy Scripture. 2. On the efficient and material cause of the Reformation. 3. On the use of Hebrew writings in the New Testament. 4. Irenic meditations. 5. Sabbathismus, or dissertations on the Jewish, Christian, Marian, Muhammadan and Gentile Sabbath. 6. Idolography of the Old Testament. 4to. Ægidius Walter, Heidelberg.

units.la: 3. Κτίσις ἐξαήμερος, i. e. Historia Creationis Examen TheologicoPhilologicum, ita institutum, ut opera sex dierum ex primo Geneseos capite strictim enarrentur, singulae penè voces, obscuriores cum primis & Emphaticae, quaestionibus 164 elucidentur, & ad varios usus accommodentur. 4. ibid. Sam. Broun.
units.tr: 3. Κτίσις ἐξαήμερος [Ktisis exaēmeros], that is, a theological-philological examination of the history of Creation, arranged so that the works of the six days are briefly expounded from the first chapter of Genesis; almost every word, especially the more obscure and emphatic ones, is elucidated by 164 questions and adapted to various uses. 4to. Ibid. Samuel Broun.

units.la: 4. Duae quaestionum Philologico-Theologicarum centuriae de Theologia, Principijs fidei Christianae in genere, verbo Dei, ejusque causis, effectis, Subjecto, Adjunctis in specie, disputationibus triginta in Collegio Sapientiae discussae, &c. 16. 4. Ægid. VValter.
units.tr: 4. Two centuries of philological-theological questions on theology, the principles of the Christian faith in general, the Word of God and its causes, effects, subject and accidents in particular, discussed in thirty disputations in the College of Wisdom, etc. 16. 4. Ægidius Walter.

units.la: I. Dissertationum Theologico-Philologicarum fasciculus. 1. De Resurrectione mortuorum 2. de notis Ecclesiae visibilis. 3. De translationibus Bibliorum in varias Linguas vernaculas, tum in Synagoga Iudaica Pharisaorum sive Rabbanitarum, Karraeorum & Samaritanorum, quàm in Ecclesia Christiana Syrorum, Armenorum, Aegyptiorum, Arabum, Persarum, Graecorum, Aethiopum, earumque origine, virtutibus, & vitiis. 4 De nominibus Dei Orientalium Hebraeorum, Chaldaeorum, Syrorum, Arabum, Samaritanorum, Aethiopum, Persarum &c. publice ventilatus in Academia Heidelbergensi. Accedit mantissa doctrinae Hebraeorum de Essentia Dei, variisque ejus attributis &c. 16. 4. Sam. Broun.
units.tr: I. A bundle of theological-philological dissertations. 1. On the resurrection of the dead. 2. On the marks of the visible Church. 3. On the translations of the Bible into various vernacular languages, both in the Jewish synagogue of the Pharisees or Rabbanites, Karaites and Samaritans, and in the Christian Church of the Syrians, Armenians, Egyptians, Arabs, Persians, Greeks and Ethiopians, and on their origin, virtues and faults. 4. On the Oriental names of God among the Hebrews, Chaldeans, Syrians, Arabs, Samaritans, Ethiopians, Persians, etc., publicly debated in the Academy of Heidelberg. Added is an appendix on the doctrine of the Hebrews concerning the essence of God and its various attributes, etc. 16. 4. Samuel Broun.

units.la: 2. Cursus Theologicus, Methodo Altingiana expositus, cui accedit Prim, i. e. oratio, Theologi ideam nobis exhibens Theoretici. 16. 8. sumtibus Adriani VVyngarden.
units.tr: 2. Theological Course, set out by the method of Altingius, to which is added Prim, that is, oration, presenting us with the idea of the theologian as theorist. 16. 8. At the expense of Adrian Wyngaerden.

units.la: I. Etymologicum Orientale; sive Lexicon Harmonicum Heptaglotton, quo, non matris tantum, Hebraicae Linguae, radices Biblicae omnes vel constituuntur, vel, ubi inter Iudaeos, temporis injuria usitatae esse desierunt, ex Chaldaea, Syria, Arabia, Aethiopia & restituuntur, diversisque suis significationibus explicantur, sed & Chaldaicae, Syriacae, Arabicae, Samaritanae, Aethiopicae, Talmudico-Rabbinicae Dialectorum, seu filiarum voces juxta seriem Hebraicam ex libris tam Canonicis, quàm Ecclesiasticis exhibentur: Harmonia simul vel matris cum filiabus, vel filiarum inter se luculenter ostenditur; propriae denique cujusvis radicis significationes adjiciuntur, cum praesat de gradibus studij Philologici, & Apologetico brevi contra Abrahamum Ecchellensem Maronitam. Francofurt. Ammon & Serlin.
units.tr: I. Oriental Etymologicon; or Harmonic Heptaglot Lexicon, in which not only the biblical roots of the mother tongue, Hebrew, are all either established or, where they have ceased to be used among the Jews through the injury of time, are restored from Chaldee, Syriac, Arabic and Ethiopic, and their meanings explained in their various senses; but also the words of the daughter dialects, Chaldee, Syriac, Arabic, Samaritan, Ethiopic and Talmudic-Rabbinic, are presented in Hebrew order from both canonical and ecclesiastical books. The harmony of the mother with the daughters, or of the daughters among themselves, is clearly shown, and the proper meanings of each root are added, with a preface on the stages of philological study and a short apologetic against Abraham Ecchellensis the Maronite. Frankfurt: Ammon & Serlin.

units.la: 2. Compendium universa Theologia Iudaica, Methodo Scholastica, breviter quidem & succincte exhibitum, collegiorum tamen privatorum usibus ita accommodatum, ut ad plenissimam dogmatum Regiminis & Leiturgiae sive rituum Iudaicorum notitiam, indicatis cujusve materiae fontibus, tutam ostendat viam. In collegio privato expositum. Heidelb. 8. VValt.
units.tr: 2. A compendium of the whole Jewish theology, set out in scholastic method, briefly and succinctly, yet so adapted to the use of private lectures that it shows a safe path, with the sources of each subject indicated, to full knowledge of the dogmas, the government and the liturgy or rites of the Jews. Expounded in a private lecture. Heidelberg. 8. Walter.

units.la: 3. Epitome utriusque juris Hebraici, aphorismis Majmonidis exhibita, locis Scripturae, unde depromti sunt, confirmata, & notis generalibus illustrata. 1b.
units.tr: 3. An epitome of the whole Hebrew law, presented in the aphorisms of Maimonides, confirmed by the places of Scripture from which they are drawn, and illustrated by general notes. Ibid.

units.la: 4. Ἀρχαιολογία Orientalis, exhibens A. compendium Theatri Orientalis, de Arabum, Persarum, Turcarum, Tartarorum, Indorum, Mauritanorum, Muhammedanorum potissimum, statu Politico, Ecclesiastico, Scholastico & Oeconomico, Collegio privato, Heidelbergae expositum, & ex illorum monumentis magnam partem, depromtum. Vbi ordine 1. De Saracenis sive Arabisino Gentili: 2. De Muhammedismo, ejusque statu Ecclesiastico, ubi a. de initio Islamismi & variis in casibus, haeresibus & schismatibus. b De varia tradendae Theologiae Muhammedicae methodo in genere, in specie compendio Theologiae Alkoranicae, c. Compendium Theologiae Scholasticae 3. De Politia Muhammedismi Arabica, adeoque Arabum imperio, ubi a. de Politia in genere, Imperatorum serie & diversis familiis. b. Magistratibus inferioribus, modo administrandae justitiae. c. Militia. 4. De Academiis & studiis Arabum 5. De Oeconomia eorum. Eadem, quantum fieri potuit. Methodo de caeteris etiam supra expressis agitur Muhammedanis, Persis, Indis, Tartaris &c. Heidelb. Sam. Brown.
units.tr: 4. Ἀρχαιολογία [Archaiologia] Orientalis, showing A. a compendium of the Oriental theatre, concerning the political, ecclesiastical, scholastic and domestic state of the Arabs, Persians, Turks, Tartars, Indians, Moors and, above all, the Muhammadans, expounded in a private lecture at Heidelberg and largely drawn from their own monuments. Here, in order: 1. On the Saracens, or the Gentile Arabs. 2. On Muhammadanism and its ecclesiastical state: (a) on the beginning of Islam and its various cases, heresies and schisms; (b) on the varied method of teaching Muhammadan theology in general, and in particular a compendium of Qur'anic theology; (c) a compendium of scholastic theology. 3. On the Arabic polity of Muhammadanism, and so the empire of the Arabs: (a) on polity in general, the succession of emperors and the various dynasties; (b) the lower magistrates and the manner of administering justice; (c) the military. 4. On the academies and studies of the Arabs. 5. On their domestic economy. The same, as far as possible, is treated by the same method of the other peoples mentioned above, the Muhammadans, Persians, Indians, Tartars, etc. Heidelberg. Samuel Broun.

units.la: B. Topographiam Ecclesiasticam Orientalem, quae brevis est Ecclesiae Orientalis, secundum Nominum, dogmatum, sedium Patriarchalium, Linguarum, Climatum denique diversitatem, descriptio: Annexis quibusdam de statu ejusdem observationibus, publicorum quorundam scriptorum Syriacorum, Arabicorum, Aethiopicorum &c. compendiosa Anatome. Inseruntur opusculo Confessio Claudij Regis Aethiopum, & vindiciae pro Confessione Cyrilli, Patriarchae Constantinopolitani, contra Neuhusium, Allatium, &c.
units.tr: B. Oriental Ecclesiastical Topography, which is a brief description of the Eastern Church according to the diversity of its names, dogmas, patriarchal sees, languages and, finally, climates; with added some observations on its present state and a concise anatomy of some public Syriac, Arabic, Ethiopic, etc. writings. Included in the work are the Confession of Claudius, King of the Ethiopians, and a defence of the Confession of Cyril, Patriarch of Constantinople, against Neuhusius, Allatius, etc.

units.la: Enneas Dissertationum Philologico-Theologicarum Heidelberg- ensium
units.tr: The Nine Philological-Theological Dissertations of Heidelberg

units.la: 1. De Libris Veteris Testamenti suppositiis, Prophetia praesertim Enochi, & Samaritanorum libro Iosuae, indeque deducto Compendio Theologiae. 2. Δοκιμασία Abrahami, ex Genes. 22. 3. Paradiso. 4. Ministerij Ecclesiastici necessitate. 5. Baptismo. 6. Melchisedeco, annexa brevi Apologia, contra Labbaeum Iesuitam. 7. Causis Coenae Dominicae, cui subjungitur specimen Analyseos Sacrae, de sensu verborum: Hoc est corpus meum. 8 Leone Allatio, nimiae temeritatis convicto, & perpetuo Ecclesiarum Latinae & Graecae dissensu. 9. Subjicitur compendium Theologiae judaicae. Quibus accedunt Programmata Heidelbergensia a me vel Rectore vel Decano Facultatis Theologicae conscripta. Tiguri, sumtibus Melchioris Stauffacheri, in 4. Labbaeus Iesuita, & Leo Allatius, Bibliothecarius Vaticanus nonnulla ex Historia mea Ecclesiastica magna intemperie susceperunt refutanda. Ille faltuatim quaedam; hic, quae Tom. V. secul. XVI scripsi de dogmatibus Graecorum, aggressus est. Nolui deesse officio, aut modestae Apologiae provinciam detrectare; sed breviter, quae spisso mihi volumine objecta sunt, dilui, ne bonae horae melioribus occupationibus eriperentur. Lectoris judicio relinquo, annon uterque magno conatu magnas egerit nugas.
units.tr: 1. On the spurious books of the Old Testament, especially the prophecy of Enoch and the Samaritans' book of Joshua, and the compendium of theology deduced from them. 2. The testing of Abraham [Δοκιμασία], from Genesis 22. 3. Paradise. 4. The necessity of the ecclesiastical ministry. 5. Baptism. 6. Melchizedek, with an appended brief apology against the Jesuit Labbé. 7. The causes of the Lord's Supper, to which is added a specimen of sacred analysis on the sense of the words, "This is my body." 8. Leo Allatius, convicted of excessive rashness, and the perpetual disagreement of the Latin and Greek Churches. 9. A compendium of Jewish theology is added. To these are joined the Heidelberg programmata, written by me either as Rector or as Dean of the Faculty of Theology. Zurich, at the expense of Melchior Stauffacher, in quarto. The Jesuit Labbé and Leo Allatius, Vatican librarian, took up for refutation some points from my great Ecclesiastical History, written amid great turmoil. The former attacked certain points here and there; the latter attacked what I wrote in volume V of the sixteenth century about the dogmas of the Greeks. I did not want to fail in my duty or to shirk the task of a modest apology, but I have briefly answered in a few words what was objected to me in that thick volume, so that good hours would not be snatched from better occupations. I leave it to the judgment of the reader whether each of them, with great effort, has achieved great trifles.

units.la: 1. Bibliothecarius, sive Tractatus de officio Bibliothecarij: de Bibliothecis, Veteribus & novis, toto orbe dispersis in genere, in specie de scriptis & scriptoribus Anglicanis: Regulis in collectione Bibliothecarum observandis: Ratione & modo Bibliothecas tam disponendi, quàm dispositas in Catalogos redigendi. Accedit Bibliotheca Theologico Historico Critica, de Theologia Biblica, Patristica, & Topica. Insertæ Leonis Africani vitæ celebrium quorundam inter Arabes virorum, tam Muhammedanorum, quàm judæorum & Christianorum, ex Msc. ἀνεκδότων. In 4. Tig. ejusdem sumtibus.
units.tr: 1. The Librarian, or a Treatise on the office of the librarian: on libraries, ancient and new, scattered throughout the whole world, in general; in particular, on the writings and writers of England; the rules to be observed in gathering libraries; the method and manner both of arranging libraries and of reducing them into catalogues. To this is added a Theological, Historical and Critical Library, on Biblical, Patristic and Topical theology. Inserted are the lives of certain famous men among the Arabs, both Muslims and Jews and Christians, of Leo Africanus, taken from unpublished manuscripts. In quarto. Zurich, at the same expense.

units.la: 2. Schola Tigurinorum Carolina: Id est Historica Demonstratio, Schola Illust. Reipubl. Tigurinæ, à Carolo Magno deducendam: Duabus absolutæ periodis; quarum illa, à Carolo M. ad Reformationem, Trivialem; hæc, à Reformatione, publicam exhibet. Accedunt,
units.tr: 2. The Carolingian School of Zurich: that is, a historical demonstration, to be traced back to Charlemagne, of the Illustrious School of the Zurich Republic. It is presented in two complete periods: the former, from Charlemagne to the Reformation, is the Trivial; the latter, from the Reformation, is the Public. To these are added:

units.la: 1. Bibliotheca Tigurina, sive Catalogus Scriptorum, ante & post Reformationem à Tigurinis editorum. II. Nota de Schola Tigurina Doctoribus, Collegij Carolini Ori- gine, incrementis, &c.
units.tr: 1. The Zurich Library, or a catalogue of writers, before and after the Reformation, published by the Zurich men. II. A note on the Zurich teachers of the School, on the origin and growth of the Carolingian College, etc.

units.la: 3. Paratus iterum est variarum dissertationum, Orationum & lectionum Fasciculus, de Theologia Catechetica, ex Deut. c. 6. 7. v. 7. 8. Theologia Naturali, Psalm. 19 Scripturæ Lectione, translatione & explicatione ex Nehem. c. 8. v. 9. Vindiciæ Cap. V. Matthæi, ex antiquitate judaica institutæ. De Translationibus Scripturæ sacræ in Linguas Vernaculas, & boni Interpretis virtutibus sive requisitis. Gymnasij Theologici disputationes Isagogicæ 1. de Theologiæ Etymologia & Synonymia. 2. De falsis Sophistarum distinctionibus Theologicis. 3. de Theologia Systematica in genere, in specie de Catechetica, Exomolegetica, Apologetica &c. 4 de Theologia Scholastica, Theoretica & Practica. Oratio de Theologi requisitis Practicis &c.
units.tr: 3. There is again a bundle of various dissertations, orations and lectures: on catechetical theology, from Deuteronomy 6:7–8; on natural theology, Psalm 19; on the reading, translation and explanation of Scripture, from Nehemiah 8:9; a defence of Matthew chapter 5, established from Jewish antiquity; on translations of Holy Scripture into the vernacular languages, and on the virtues or requisites of a good interpreter. The disputations of the Theological Gymnasium, introductory: (1) on the etymology and synonyms of theology; (2) on the false theological distinctions of the Sophists; (3) on systematic theology in general, and in particular on catechetical, confessional, apologetic theology, etc.; (4) on scholastic, theoretical and practical theology. An oration on the practical requisites of a theologian, etc.

units.la: Atque hæc sunt, quæ paulatim, inter ordinarias occupationes, prælo per me destinata fuerunt. Recensio hæc temporis sequitur seriem, si ὁμογενείας habenda esset ratio, ad sequentes commodè omnia revocari possent classes.
units.tr: These are the works which, little by little, amid my ordinary occupations, I have destined for the press. This list follows the order of time; if account were to be taken of kinship [ὁμογενείας], all of them could conveniently be referred to the following classes.

units.la: I. Theologica, Atque sic uno volumine exhiberentur scriptum Hodegeticum, cum Apologia, Disputationes variæ, juxta locos communes dispositæ; Orationes denique de rebus Theologicis. II. Dialectologia philologica, sive Encyclopædia Linguarum Orientalium; Adeò ut quæcunque de Linguis tum in genere agunt, tum in specie vel Hebræa, vel Arabica, vel alia etiam, in unum totum referrentur, ut sunt Grammatica, Hebraica, Chaldaeo Syriaca, Harmonica quatuor Linguarum. Lexica, Technologiæ &c. De usu Linguarum Orientalium. Addi his postea debent Theologica tam Iudæorum, Samaritanorum, quàm Muhammedanorum: Iuridica, &c. cæteraque omnia quæ ad Historiam Orientalem spectant, sive sacram, sive profanam. III. Historia Ecclesiastica Universalis, Christiana, Iudaica, Muhammedica, Gentilis &c. IV. τὰ Πάντοια, sive Speculum Helveticum, quo exhibentur 1. Methodus legendi Historias Helveticas, 2. Irenicum Helveti-cum. cum. 3. Compendium Historiae Tigurinae Naturalis, Ecclesiasticae, Politicae, Militaris. Hoc scriptum a me vernacula Lingua conscriptum adhuc est ἀνέκδοτον. 4. Herologium & Hierologium Tigurinum, sive prolixior Prosopographia virorum in Ecclesia & Schola Tigurina celebrium 5. Origines Scholae Tigurinae. 6. Bibliotheca Tigurina, sive Catalogus librorum à Doctoribus Tigurinis editorum. Ita non male opuscula diversis vulgata annis conjungi potuissent, forte non plane absque fructu & usu lectorum. De quo tamen quid futurum sit, ἔσῃ ἐν γένεσθαι κείται. Sed & de generali saepe cogitavi conscribendo indice, qui majorem & ubertatem materiae ostenderet, & varietatem, quàm quae cuilibet obvia esse posset Lectori. Sed alius haec ortij opera est. Sufficiat hac occasione obiter tantum & tumultuarie indicasse eos, qui ex professo tractati a nobis sunt, locos communes. Potest ergo non paucorum sedes indicari 1. In Theologia
units.tr: I. Theological. Thus a single volume would present the Hodegeticum, with the Apology, various Disputations arranged according to common topics, and finally Orations on theological matters. II. Philological Dialectology, or Encyclopaedia of the Oriental Languages; so that whatever treats of languages, whether in general or in particular, whether Hebrew or Arabic or others too, would be brought together into one whole, such as Grammar, of Hebrew, Chaldee-Syriac, the harmony of four languages, Lexica, Technologies, etc. On the use of the Oriental languages. To these should afterwards be added the theologies of the Jews, Samaritans and Muslims, the juridical works, etc., and all the other things that pertain to Oriental history, whether sacred or profane. III. Universal Ecclesiastical History: Christian, Jewish, Muslim, Gentile, etc. IV. Pantoia [τὰ Πάντοια], or Swiss Mirror, in which are presented: (1) a method of reading Swiss histories; (2) a Swiss Irenicum; (3) a compendium of the natural, ecclesiastical, political and military history of Zurich. This work, written by me in the vernacular, is still unpublished [ἀνέκδοτον]. (4) A Zurich Herologium and Hierologium, or a fuller prosopography of men famous in the Church and in the Zurich School; (5) the Origins of the Zurich School; (6) the Zurich Library, or a catalogue of books published by the Zurich teachers. Thus small works published in different years could well have been joined together, perhaps not altogether without benefit and use to readers. What will become of this, however, lies in the future [ἐν γένεσθαι κείται]. I have also often thought of compiling a general index, which would show both the greater abundance of the material and a variety greater than any reader might easily find. But that is the work of another garden. It is enough, on this occasion, to have indicated in passing and in a hurried way the common topics treated by us, in their proper places. Thus the seats of not a few can be indicated. 1. In Christian theology, where A. Exegetical: 1. There is an explanation of several texts of the Pentateuch in Hebrew law, namely of all those places in the Law, from Leviticus chapter 20 onward, which are preceptive. 2. Of the more obscure passages in the various versions, in the Thesaurus Philologicus, the dissertation on the Heptapla, part of the Smegmata Orientalia, volume 3, 5, 6, 7, 8. 3. A defence of the passages which charge the Papists with corruption; Thesaurus Philologicus, page 147. 4. An illustration, from Hebrew writings, of the places of the New Testament, first Heidelberg disputation 3, 5; various Papist Hodegetica, part 1, chapter 7, page 168, and part 2, chapter 2, page 120. 6. The explanation of other places of Scripture here and there, especially in the antithesis between the Nabatean and Mosaic laws; Oriental History, book 1, chapter 8, page 197. 7. For other passages see the notes in the indices of the Thesaurus Philologicus, Analecta Iuris Hebraici, Oriental History, Smegmata 8. The creation in six days [κτίσις ἐξαπήμερος] is set forth in the order of Genesis chapter 1. Textual disputations: Deuteronomy 6:6–7, Nehemiah 7, Matthew 5.

units.la: N. Christiana, ubi A. Exegetica. 1. Habetur explicatio textuum aliquot Pentateuchi in jure Hebraeorum, omnium nempe eorum locorum, quae in Lege ad Levit: Cap. 20. praeceptiva sunt 2. Obscuriorum locorum in variis versionibus in Thes. philolog. Differt. de Heptap. Pars. Smeg. Orient. v. 3.5.6 7.8. 3. Vindiciae locorum, quae corruptionis Pontificij insimulant; Thes. philol. pag. 147. 4. Illustratio, ex scriptis Hebraicis, locorum Novi Testamenti primit. Heidelberg. Disp. 3.5. variae Pontificiae Hodeg. P.I.c.7.p.168. & P.II. c.2.p.120.6. Aliorum hinc inde Scripturae locorum explicatio, praesertim in antithesi legum Nabathaearum & Mosaicarum. Hist. Orient. 1. 1.c.8.p.197.7. Caetera loca vide notata in Indicibus Thes. phil. Anal. Iuris Heb. Hist. Orient. Smegmat. 8. κτίσις ἐξαπήμερος ordine Gen. c. 1. exhibet. Disputationes textuales, Deut. 6. v. 6. 7. Nehem. 7 Matth. 5.
units.tr: N. Christian, where A. Exegetical. 1. An explanation is given of some texts of the Pentateuch in the law of the Hebrews, namely of all those passages in the Law which are preceptive, in Leviticus chapter 20. 2. Of obscure passages in the various versions, in Thes. philolog., Diss. on the Heptaplar; Part Smeg. Orient., vol. 3, 5, 6, 7, 8. 3. Defences of passages which the Papists accuse of corruption; Thes. philol., p. 147. 4. Illustration, from Hebrew writings, of passages of the New Testament: Heidelberg Disp. 3, 5; various Papist Hodeg. P. I, c. 7, p. 168, and P. II, c. 2, p. 120. 6. Explanation of other passages of Scripture here and there, especially in antithesis to the laws of the Nabataeans and of Moses; Hist. Orient. 1, 1, c. 8, p. 197. 7. For other passages, see those noted in the Indexes of Thes. philol., Anal. Iuris Heb., Hist. Orient., Smegmat. 8. He presents the creation in six days [κτίσις ἐξαπήμερος] in the order of Genesis chapter 1. Textual disputations: Deut. 6:6–7; Nehem. 7; Matth. 5.

units.la: B. Historica. Tractatur enim in ijs I Historia Testamenti Veteris. a. Thes aur. philolog. ut ex Indice Historico patet: ubi compendium totius V. T. proponitur. b. Smegm. Orient. Cap 8. ubi ab initio Mundi ad tempora judicum Historia pertexitur. c. Historia Orient. ubi explicuimus תאריך בני אדם Genealogiam posterorum Adami. d. Disp. de Pseudep. V. T. & Melchised. 11. Novi Testamenti, quae generaliter & Historice tractatur toto Systemate nostro Historiae Ecclesiasticae. Specialiter & dogmati e circa quaedam loca Theologica, in Hodegetico tripartito. Confessione Cyrilli, Veterum Testimonijs munita.
units.tr: B. Historical. For in these works there is treated: 1. The history of the Old Testament. a. In the Thes. philolog., as is clear from the Historical Index, where a compendium of the whole Old Testament is set forth. b. Smegm. Orient., chapter 8, where the history is carried on from the beginning of the world to the time of the judges. c. Hist. Orient., where we have explained the genealogy of the posterity of Adam [תאריך בני אדם]. d. Disp. on the Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament and Melchisedek. 11. The New Testament, which is treated generally and historically throughout our whole System of Ecclesiastical History; and specially, with regard to certain theological passages and dogmas, in the three-part Hodegeticus, with the confession of Cyril, supported by the testimonies of the ancients.

units.la: C. Didactico Elenctica, N Generaliter in Systemate, & Gymnasio Theologico, duabus centuriis, Hodegetico, & Historiae Ecclesiasticae varijs capitibus, quae συμβίβασιν continent. Confessione Cyrilli Martyris: Disput. de usu Linguae Heb. contra Pontificios & Anabapt. Specialiter. I. Theologia, Gymnas. Theol. Disput. Ifagog. De Scriptura, a. ejus authoritate Hodeg. P. I. c. 1. Primit. Heid Disp, 2. 6. canone 16. c.3. Thesaur. pag. 110. Centur. Theol. cap. 2. Confess. Cyrill. pag 510. c. Perfectione, Hodeg. P. I. cap, 6. Confess, Cyrill, c. 2, d. Indice controversiarum, Hodeg. P. I. cap. 8. c. Authoe. Authoritate Patrum, Anal. centur. Theolog. l. 1. f. scriptis eorum supposititijs Anal P. 2. Ennead. Heidelb. 1. g. Modo explicandi literas sacras Heidelb. prim. Disp. I. Vindiciae Bibliorum Tigurinorum, in commercio Epistol. Helvetico Hodeg. P. I. c 5. pag. 134. ⌐ Nominibus eorum, qui Biblia vel Hebraicè vel Arabicè, vel Syriacè commentarijs illustrârunt, promtuar. sive Biblioth. Orient. i. Versionibus in Linguas vernaculas. Generaliter Anal. Ecc. Disp. 2. Hodeg. P. I. c. 5. De officio Interpretis, S. Sc. lectione, Interpretatione & Translatione specialiter Chaldaicis Syriacis, Arabicis. Hodeg. P. I. c. 5. Anal. P. I. Disp. 2. Thef. pag 251. Smeg. c 6. Fascic. Disp. Heidelb de Translat. II. De Deo, Hodeg P. II. c.
units.tr: C. Didactic and Elenctic. N. Generally, in the System and the Theological Gymnasium, in two centuries, in the Hodegeticus, and in various chapters of the Ecclesiastical History, which contain the reconciliation [συμβίβασιν]. The confession of Cyril the Martyr. Disputation on the use of the Hebrew language against the Papists and Anabaptists. Specially: I. Theology: Theological Gymnasium, Disputation Isagogicus. On Scripture: a. its authority, Hodeg. P. I, c. 1; Primit. Heid. Disp. 2, 6; canon 16, c. 3; Thesaur., p. 110; Centur. Theol., chap. 2; Confess. Cyrill., p. 510. c. Its perfection, Hodeg. P. I, chap. 6; Confess. Cyrill., c. 2. d. Index of controversies, Hodeg. P. I, chap. 8. e. Its author. Authority of the Fathers, Anal. centur. Theolog., l. 1. f. Their spurious writings, Anal. P. 2; Ennead. Heidelb. 1. g. The manner of explaining the sacred letters, Heidelb. prim. Disp. I. Defence of the Tigurine Bible, in the exchange of letters with Helvetia, Hodeg. P. I, c. 5, p. 134. Names of those who illustrated the Bible with commentaries in Hebrew, Arabic or Syriac, promtuar. or Bibliotheca Orientalis. i. Versions into vernacular languages. Generally, Anal. Ecc. Disp. 2; Hodeg. P. I, c. 5. On the office of the interpreter, the reading, interpretation and translation of Scripture; specially Chaldee, Syriac, Arabic: Hodeg. P. I, c. 5; Anal. P. I, Disp. 2; Thes., p. 251; Smeg. c. 6; Fascic. Disp. Heidelb. de Translat. II. On God, Hodeg P. II, c.

units.la: 1. Nominibus & attributis Dei Fascic. Disp. Heidelb. N 4 III. Decretis Dei, Confess. Cyrilli cap. 3 Meletem Iren. cap 6 7. IV. Creatione: totum opus ἐξαρτίσεως. Disp. de Paradiso. V. De Lege: Ius Hebraeorum, Epit. utriusque Iuris & Hodeg P. III c 1. de imaginibus. Sabbathismus, primit. Heidelb. Idolographia V. T. Ib. de invocatione sanctorum: Hodeg. P. II cap 2. VI De Christo: Melet. Iren. cap. 5. Confess. Cyrill 7. 8. Esse Messiam, Appen. Grammat. Chald. Syri. VII. De Ecclesia: Confess Cyrill. cap. 10. Notis Ecclesiae, Fasc 2. Histor. Orient. pag 275. Hist. Eccles. Sec. 12. pag 144. Pontificis Romani fallibilitate, Histor. Eccles. Sec. 15. Append. Confess. Cyrill. c 12. VIII. De Sacramento Baptismi & Coenae: Confess. Cyrill. cap. 7. Melet. Iren. c. 4 & Mantissa. 1. Subsid. Anal. Disp. de Baptismo & Coena I X. Apologia pro Ecclesia Reformata de necessitate Reformationis, Anal. P. I. Disp. 1. Hist Eccles. Sec. XVI. primit. Heidelb. Disp. 2. X. Ecclesia Orientali, Hist. Eccles. Sec. de Christianis, Topog. Eccles. in specie Graeca, Confess. Cyrill. Leo. Allat. XI. Iustificatione, ejusque appendicibus bonis operibus, indulgentijs, Purgatorio. Hodeg. P. IIII cap 2. Confess. Cyrill. cap. 13. Anal. P. I. Disp. 3 de Iubil. De resurrectione, Fasc c 1.
units.tr: 1. On the names and attributes of God, Fascic. Disp. Heidelb. N 4; III. On the decrees of God, Confess. Cyrilli cap. 3; Meletem Iren. cap. 6, 7. IV. On creation: the whole work of completion [ἐξαρτίσεως]. Disp. on Paradise. V. On the Law: Ius Hebraeorum, Epit. of both laws, and Hodeg. P. III, c. 1. On images, Sabbatarianism, primit. Heidelb., Idolography of the Old Testament, ib. On the invocation of saints: Hodeg. P. II, cap. 2. VI. On Christ: Melet. Iren. cap. 5. Confess. Cyrill. 7, 8. That he is the Messiah, Appen. Grammat. Chald. Syri. VII. On the Church: Confess. Cyrill. cap. 10. On the marks of the Church, Fasc. 2. Histor. Orient. p. 275; Hist. Eccles. Sec. 12, p. 144. On the fallibility of the Roman Pontiff, Histor. Eccles. Sec. 15; Append. Confess. Cyrill. c. 12. VIII. On the sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper: Confess. Cyrill. cap. 7; Melet. Iren. c. 4 and Mantissa 1; Subsid. Anal. Disp. on Baptism and the Lord's Supper. IX. Apology for the Reformed Church on the necessity of the Reformation, Anal. P. I, Disp. 1; Hist. Eccles. Sec. XVI; primit. Heidelb. Disp. 2. X. The Eastern Church: Hist. Eccles. Sec. on the Christians; Topog. Eccles. especially the Greek; Confess. Cyrill.; Leo Allat. XI. Justification and its appendices: good works, indulgences, purgatory. Hodeg. P. IIII, cap. 2; Confess. Cyrill. cap. 13; Anal. P. I, Disp. 3 on the Jubilee. On the resurrection, Fasc. c. 1.

units.la: ꝟ. IVDAICA, de qua Spartum in Historia Eccles. Sect. quae de Iudaismo agit ex professo distincte vero 1. Articuli fidei Iudaicae, Append Grammat. Syr Chald. Thef. phil. pag 79. Fusius Compend. Theol. Iud. 2. de origine & usu distinctionis Articulorum in fundamentalies &c Syst. Theol Loc. 1. SAMARITICA, Exercit. Anti Morini. Thef. philol. pag 44. Bibliothec. Orient. cap 4. Smeg. Orient. pag 442. Pseudeg. V. T. pag 20 ubi compendium Theologiae Samaritanae. MVHAMMEDICA: Hist. Eccles. Sect. de Muhammedismo, Hist. Orient. Compend. Theat. Sacr. GINGIS CHANICA: Hist. Eccles. secul 15. sect. 2. NABATHÆA, Thef. phil. pag 562. Hist. Orient. l. 1. c. 8. MAGICA Thef. phil p. 56. Bibl. Orient. cap 2. Classis. GENTILIS, Hist. Eccles. singulis seculis de Gentilismo quaedam occurrunt eâ praesertim sectione, quae Gentilismus inscribitur, & variae Muhammedismi sectae: Anal P. I Disp. 2. Hist. Orient. l. 2. cap 6. Bibliothec. Orient p. 205. Comp. Theat. Sacr. varia Iudaeorum Schismata: Thef. philol. l. 1, c. 1. Comp. Theol. Iud. Haereticorum Hist. N. T. sect. de falsa Ecclesia.
units.tr: 2. JUDAICA, of which Spartum speaks in the Hist. Eccles. Sect. which treats of Judaism expressly. Here, distinctly: 1. The articles of Jewish faith, Append. Grammat. Syr. Chald. Thef. phil. p. 79; more fully in Compend. Theol. Iud. 2. On the origin and use of the distinction of articles into fundamental and so on, Syst. Theol. Loc. 1. SAMARITAN: Exercit. Anti-Morini; Thef. philol. p. 44; Bibliothec. Orient. cap. 4; Smeg. Orient. p. 442; Pseudeg. V. T. p. 20, where there is a compendium of Samaritan theology. MUHAMMADAN: Hist. Eccles. Sect. on Muhammadanism; Hist. Orient.; Compend. Theat. Sacr. GENGHISKHANID: Hist. Eccles. century 15, sect. 2. NABATAEAN: Thef. phil. p. 562; Hist. Orient. l. 1, c. 8. MAGIC: Thef. phil. p. 56; Bibl. Orient. cap. 2. The GENTILE class: Hist. Eccles. in each century some matters on Gentilism occur, especially in the section entitled Gentilism, and the various sects of Muhammadanism; Anal. P. I, Disp. 2; Hist. Orient. l. 2, cap. 6; Bibliothec. Orient. p. 205; Comp. Theat. Sacr. The various schisms of the Jews: Thef. philol. l. 1, c. 1; Comp. Theol. Iud. Heretical History of the New Testament, section on the false Church.

units.la: II. In turis prudentia. Huc enim aliquid confert. 1. Ius Hebraeorum. 2. Bibliothecae theca orientalis, ubi ex Hebraeorum (p. 36.) & Arabum (p. 175) scriptis tantum eruimus, quantum satis est ad notitiam titulorum: praesertim in Arabica Bibliotheca. Adde Disput. de usu Linguae Arab. in jure & Comp. utriusque juris.
units.tr: II. On prudence in law. For this contributes something: 1. Ius Hebraeorum. 2. The Bibliotheca orientalis, where from the writings of the Hebrews (p. 36) and the Arabs (p. 175) we extract only as much as suffices for knowledge of the titles, especially in the Arabic bibliography. Add the Disputation on the use of the Arabic language in law, and the Comp. of both laws.

units.la: III. Ad Medicinae suppellectilem aliquid confert tum Bibliotheca, tum Disput. 2. Anal. P. I. ubi non pauca occurrunt, quae Medicinam spectant.
units.tr: III. For the stock of medicine, both the Bibliotheca and Disp. 2, Anal. P. I contribute something, where not a few things concerning medicine occur.

units.la: IV. philosophiae inservit 1. Specimen philosophiae Historicae, ubi de vario Philosophiae usu & abusu 2. Specimen analyseos sacrae: primit. Heidelb. Disp. I. & explicatio Verborum Coenae. 3. κτίσις ἐξαπίμερος, est Physica Christiana. 4. Disp. de Terrae motibus. Anal. P. I. Disp. 4. 5. Bibliotheca Orient. ubi de Philosophis Hebraeorum, Syrorum, Arabum. 6. Anal. P. I. Disp. de usu Linguae Arabicae in Philosophia.
units.tr: IV. Serving philosophy: 1. Specimen philosophiae Historicae, where it treats of the varied use and abuse of philosophy. 2. Specimen analyseos sacrae: primit. Heidelb. Disp. I, and the explanation of the words of the Supper. 3. The κτίσις ἐξαρτίσμένη is Christian physics. 4. Disp. on earthquakes, Anal. P. I, Disp. 4. 5. Bibliotheca Orient., where it treats of the philosophers of the Hebrews, Syrians and Arabs. 6. Anal. P. I, Disp. on the use of the Arabic language in philosophy.

units.la: V. Ad PHILOLOGIAM pertinent tum superiora pleraque, tum cumprimis opuscula. a. Grammatica Hebraea: Chaldaeo Syriaca: Hebraea, Chaldaea, Syriaca, Arabica. b. Technologica. Technologia Theologico-Historica Arabum. c. Lexica. Cujusmodi sunt, quae tum ex aliis, tum Arabica cumprimis Lingua, ad perfectionem Lexici Hebraici eruuntur, Anal. P. I. Disp. 2. Smeg. Orient. c. 7. & Lexic. Harmonicum. d. Historica, Nempe I. Historia Hebraeorum, Hist. Eccles. singulis seculis Sect. de Iudaismo. II. Saracenorum, ib Sect. de Muhammedismo; Hist Orient. III. Tartarorum, Hist. Eccles. seculo 15. Sect. 2. IV. Samaritanorum: Tbef. Philolog. Exercitationes Anti-Mor. Pseudep. V. Gentilium, Hist. Eccles. de Gentilismo. VI. Naturalis, Sect. 1. Hist. Eccles. VII Helvetiorum, Anal. P. I. Irenic Helvet. & Method. legendi Hist. Helv. e. Prosopographia I. Melchisedec. Disput. II. Patriarcharum. Smegm. Orient. pag. 206. &c. Rabbinorum; Hist. N.T Sect. de Iudaeis. IV. Patrum, ib. Sect. de Christ. V. Scholasticorum Theologorum, ib. VI Imperatorum Christianorum, ib. VII. Muhammedanorum; ib. Sect. de Muhammedismo. VIII. Tamerlanis; Hist. Eccles. S. XV. S. 2. IX. Paparum, ib. de Christ. X. Reliquorum Eruditorum Occidentis, ib. & Symbib. Orientis vero Heb. Syr. Arab. Aegypt. Abysinorum &c. Bibliothec. Oriental. Anal P. I. Disput. 2. f. De Cippis, nummis, mensuris, ponderibus, inscriptionibus Orientis tractatu peculiari.
units.tr: V. To PHILOLOGY belong both most of the above and especially the smaller works. a. Hebrew grammar; Chaldean, Syriac; Hebrew, Chaldean, Syriac, Arabic. b. Technology. Theological-historical technology of the Arabs. c. Lexica: such as are drawn out both from others and especially from the Arabic language for the perfecting of the Hebrew lexicon, Anal. P. I, Disp. 2; Smeg. Orient. c. 7; and Lexicon Harmonicum. d. Historical works, namely: I. History of the Hebrews, Hist. Eccles. in each century, section on Judaism. II. Of the Saracens, ib., section on Muhammadanism; Hist. Orient. III. Of the Tartars, Hist. Eccles. century 15, sect. 2. IV. Of the Samaritans: Thef. Philolog., Exercitationes Anti-Morini; Pseudep. V. Of the Gentiles, Hist. Eccles. on Gentilism. VI. Natural history, Sect. 1, Hist. Eccles. VII. Of the Swiss, Anal. P. I; Irenic. Helvet. and Method. legendi Hist. Helv. e. Prosopography: I. Melchisedec, Disp. II. Of the patriarchs, Smegm. Orient. p. 206 etc. Of the rabbis: Hist. N.T. Sect. on the Jews. IV. Of the Fathers, ib., section on Christians. V. Of the scholastic theologians, ib. VI. Of the Christian emperors, ib. VII. Of the Muhammadans, ib., section on Muhammadanism. VIII. Of Tamerlane, Hist. Eccles. S. XV, S. 2. IX. Of the popes, ib., on Christians. X. Of the other learned men of the West, ib.; and Symbib. Of the East: Hebrew, Syriac, Arabic, Egyptian, Abyssinian etc., Bibliothec. Oriental. Anal. P. I, Disp. 2. f. On cippi, coins, measures, weights and inscriptions of the East, in a separate treatise.

units.la: Huldricus Henricus, Iacobi, viri & doctissimi, & in agendis rebus dexterrimi, Professoris Carolini Rhetoro Logici ab an Chr. 1576. ad 1605. filius; Scholae Carolinae ab an. Chr. 1611. Moderator, Professor Graecus 1625. ad 1610 quo die 19 April. aetat 55. mens 3. Obijt. Scripsit & edidit nonnulla tam Latina, quam Graeca, in Scholae potissimum nostrae trivialis usum, ut sunt libellus precum Graeco Latinarum; Nomenclatura, Grammatica Graeca, Latina, Rhetorica revisa. Prodijt etiam Bibliotheca ejus nova, Tigurinorum publico-privata, selectiorum variarum Linguarum artium & scientiarum, librorum, ex liberalitate & munificentia bonorum utriusque tam Politici, quam Ecclesiastici ordinis, in usum Reipubl. literariae collecta; ubi de causis maxime agitur Bibliothecæ novæ. Tig.1629. Latin. & Germ. Sed & carmina ejus extant plura, Oratio præterea ejus de Patria, magnisque Dei in eam beneficijs, alibi à me est commendata. Hæc tamen ἀνέκδοτος est, cum alijs, quibusdam opusculis, ut sunt, variæ notæ Philologicæ, Philosophicæ, Historicæ in vitam Alexandri Magni, Iulij Cæsaris, Homeri Iliad. Prosodia Græca, Orat. de Græcæ Linguæ præstantia; Comœdiæ nonnullæ, præcepta de servanda sanitate.
units.tr: Huldricus Henricus, son of Jacob, a man most learned and most skilled in public affairs, Professor of Rhetoric and Logic at Carolinum, from 1576 to 1605; Moderator of the Schola Carolina from 1611, Professor of Greek 1625 to 1610, on which day, 19 April, aged 55 years and 3 months, he died. He wrote and published several works, both Latin and Greek, chiefly for the use of our public school: such as a little book of Greek and Latin prayers; a nomenclature; a Greek grammar, a Latin grammar, and a revised rhetoric. There also appeared his new Library, the public-private library of the Zurichers, a collection of selected books in various languages, arts and sciences, gathered for the use of the literary republic from the generosity and munificence of good men of both the civil and the ecclesiastical orders; in which the causes of the new Library are chiefly discussed. Zurich 1629, Latin and German. But several of his poems also survive; moreover his oration on the homeland and the great benefits of God toward it, which I have commended elsewhere. This however remains unpublished, together with other small works, such as various philological, philosophical and historical notes, on the life of Alexander the Great, of Julius Caesar, on Homer's Iliad, a Greek prosody, an oration on the excellence of the Greek language, several comedies, and precepts for keeping health.

units.la: Huldricus Iob. Henricus, Iacobi filius, Henrici superioris ex fratre nepos. Vir eruditus, & verè πολύγλωττος. Peregrinatione literariâ quinquennali absoluta (Genevæ primùm postea, Bremæ, tandem in Bohemia & Moravia substitit) Ecclesiæ ad Sp. S. Minister, ab an. Chr. 1620. ad 1625. quo, in ipso flore ætatis, obijt, die 28. Martij. Dedit disputationes quasdam tum Theologicas, de Hæreticis & contumacibus Ecclesiarum turbatoribus, in qua de officio Christianorum Pastorum, & Magistratuum in coercendis hæreticis agitur; item de Sanctorum invocatione, tum Philosophicam &c. Carmina præterea, tam Latina, ad calcem opusculorum aliquot D. Parentis, de Religione Græcorum; &c. quàm Græca, cujusmodi est μονωδία ἐπικήδειος εἰς τὴν ἐν ὁσιβεστάτῳ καὶ ἐπιφανεστάτῳ ἀνδρὸς, Βουρκάρδῳ λημμάνῳ, ἐκ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, τῆς πυρρόνθ' ἐπισκόπου ἀκριβοτάτης, πλοῦτον; aliud item præfixit disputationi de sanctorum defunctorum invocatione. Trium linguarum Hebraicæ, Græcæ, & Latinæ documentum non contemnendum subjecit oratori D. Parentis seculari de Reformatione Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Eximium ipsius καλλιγραφίας studium tum Acta Synodi Dordracenæ commendant, magnam partem ab eo descripta; tum alia quædam tam Græcæ, quàm Syriacæ scriptionis affabrè facta specimina probant.
units.tr: Huldricus Johannes Henricus, son of Jacob, nephew through his brother of the earlier Henry. A learned man, and truly polyglot. Having completed a five-year literary journey (first at Geneva, afterwards at Bremen, and finally settling in Bohemia and Moravia), he was minister of the Church of the Holy Spirit from 1620 to 1625, when he died in the very flower of his age, on 28 March. He gave certain disputations, both theological, on heretics and obstinate disturbers of the Churches, in which the duty of Christian ministers and magistrates in restraining heretics is discussed; likewise on the invocation of the saints; and philosophical ones, etc. Moreover, poems, both Latin, appended to the end of some works of our father on the religion of the Greeks, etc., and Greek, such as the funeral monody on the most pious and most illustrious man, Burkhard Lemmann, [μονωδία ἐπικήδειος εἰς τὴν ἐν ὁσιβεστάτῳ καὶ ἐπιφανεστάτῳ ἀνδρὸς, Βουρκάρδῳ λημμάνῳ, ἐκ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, τῆς πυρρόνθ' ἐπισκόπου ἀκριβοτάτης, πλοῦτον]; he also prefixed another to the disputation on the invocation of the departed saints. He appended to the oration of our father, the secular one on the Reformation of the Zurich Church, a not contemptible proof of three languages, Hebrew, Greek and Latin. The exquisite skill of his own fine penmanship is commended both by the Acts of the Synod of Dort, a large part of which he copied out, and by other specimens of his work, well made in Greek and Syriac script alike.

units.la: Huldricus, Iohannes Iacobus, Iacobi filius, Henrici frater, L. A. M. Ecclesiæ & Scholæ Tigurinæ Minister ab anChr 1592. ad 1618. quo (cùm Plebanus ante fuisset ad an. Chr. 1611. & P. Græcus S. S. Theologiæ Professor, & Collegij Carolini Præpositus, piè decessit, ætat. 70. Vir solidè doctus, antiquitatis studiosus, & masculo dicendi genere pollens. Scripsit tractatus aliquot doctos, disputationes etiam & carmina, (quorum nonnulla ipse opusculorum suorum limini præfixit) cujusmodi sunt. 1. Vindiciae pro Bibliorum Translatione Tigurina, adversus Iacobi Gretseri Iesuitæ admonitionem noviter ad exteros, proterva crimination emissam, Tigur. 1616. Id ipsum scriptum per Metathesin literarum Lychardi quoque Neocomensis nomine prodijt. Scripsit Gretserus causæ suæ admonitionis ad Exteros defensionem, cui Huldricus, responsum paraturus, distributionem operis sequentem observavit, quæ tamen hactenus non prodijt: Elenchus defensionis Gretseriana fraudulenta, pro vindicijs Translationis S. Bibliorum Tigurinæ. Defensio admonitionis protervæ, à Gretsero Iesuita, vindicijs nostris pro S. Bibliorum Translatione Tigurinâ, opposita concontexta est ex quatruplici fraude. 1. Praetermissione fucata Cardinalium hujus negotii Argumentorum. 2. Assumptione rationum nostrarum sophistica, mutila & manca. 3. Infarsione alienorum & ad praesentem causam minimè spectantium. 4. Convitiorum denique foedissimorum vomitu lesuitico. Primae fraudis exempla quaenam hujus negotii argumenta, Gretserus sile ntio praetermiserit. 1. Admonui Gretserum, ut unicam vocem seu phrasin mala fide ab Interpretibus Tigurinis translatam, in medium proferret. Resp. Nulla.
units.tr: Huldricus, John James (Iohannes Iacobus), son of James and brother of Henry, Master of Liberal Arts, minister of the Church and School of Zurich from 1592 to 1618, when he died piously at the age of 70. He had first been plebanus until 1611, and was Greek professor of sacred theology and provost of the Carolinum college. He was a man of solid learning, devoted to antiquity, and strong in a manly style of speaking. He wrote several learned treatises, disputations and poems, some of which he prefixed to his own small works. Among them are: 1. A defence of the Zurich translation of the Bible against the James Gretser, Jesuit, admonition to foreigners, a recently published shameless accusation, Zurich 1616. The same work also came out under the name Lychardus Neocomensis, by a transposition of the letters. Gretser wrote a defence of his admonition to foreigners. Huldricus, preparing a reply, drew up the following plan of the work, which has not appeared so far: Refutation of Gretser's fraudulent defence, in defence of our vindications of the Zurich translation of the Holy Bible. The defence of the shameless admonition, which Gretser the Jesuit set against our vindications of the Zurich translation of the Holy Bible, is woven together from a fourfold fraud. (1) The concealment, by a pretence, of the principal arguments of this matter. (2) The sophistical, maimed and defective handling of our reasons. (3) The insertion of foreign matter that does not bear on the present case at all. (4) Finally, a vomit of the most foul insults in the Jesuit manner. Examples of the first fraud, that is, which arguments of this matter Gretser passed over in silence: 1. I urged Gretser to bring forward a single word or phrase which the Zurich translators had rendered in bad faith. Reply: none.

units.la: 2. Accusavi ipsum fraudis impiae, qua Clypei Venetiani Encomium illustrè, Pastoribus Tigurinis tributum, truncatè allegavit. Resp. N. 3. Asserui tantam lucis Evangelicae vim esse, ut si libera librorum Orthodoxorum copia fieret exteris, Venetianis, Italis, Hispanis &c. universi Papatus superstitiones facile corruiturae sint. Resp. N. 4. Enarravi historicè consilium, modum, finem & usum Translationis sacrae, à Theologis Tigurinis susceptae & absolutae. Resp. N. 5. Demonstravi versiones S. Bibliorum, ex lingua Nativa in Latinam, sive in aliam tritam & vernaculam, liberas in Ecclesia Christianâ, antiquitus fuisse. Resp. N. 6. Contendi, decretum Synodi Viennensis in Gallia de Linguarum Orientalium studio instaurando, ad fidem Christianam inter Saracenos propagandam, futurae Reformationi viam stravisse. Resp. N. 7. Allegavi insigne testimonium & encomium Iacobi Augustini Thuani, Praesidis Parisini, hominis Pontificii, nostratum Theologorum scriptis tributum. Resp. N. 8. Ad luculentum testimonium à D. Luthero, ante certaminis Sacramentarij æstum, Helveticarum Ecclesiarum Confessioni tributum. Resp N. 9. Ad integrum Caput de Translatione Bibliorum Tigurina, à Roberto Stephano Parisiensi Regio Typographo edita; &c. Resp. N. 10. Ad objectionem de Indice expurgatorio, decreto Synodi Tridentinae concinnato, in quo monumenta Patrum Historiae, Annales Ecclesiastici, scripta authorum recentiorum, nefaria fraude truncantur, Resp. N. 11. Ad rationem nostram, de prisca fide primorum Martyrum Tigurinorum, S. Felicis & Regulae, quoad capita doctrinae coelestis fundamentalis, Resp. N. 12. Sacramentariae haereseos crimen immeritò nostratibus intentari, qui de Sacramentorum essentiâ, forma, proprietatibus, fine, usu & effectis, cum Canone S. Scripturae & Orthodoxa Antiquitate, haectenus consentaneè docuerunt, Resp N. 13. Asserui firmis rationibus, honoratissimum Episcoporum elogion, & Hispano Theologo Ferdinando de Escalante Ecclesiae Tigurinae pastoribus jure tributum esse, &c. Resp. N. 14. Commonefeci Gretserum Huldr. Zuinglium ineptè & calumniosè Baalim Turregiensem nominari à Iesuitis; & longè verius Antibaalim & Baalimastiga nuncupandum esse, &c. Resp N. 15. Vindicavi, salvâ conscientiae fide, honestissimam Leonis Iudę familiam, à parentibus avisq; non Iudęam, sed Christianam fidem in Alsatia professis: ejusque obitum placidissimum & beatissimum, &c. Resp. N. 16. Ad vindicationem Carminis Gualtheriani argumenta fingu-
units.tr: 2. I accused him of the impious fraud by which he cited, in truncated form, the illustrious encomium of the Venetian Shield, paid to the Zurich ministers. Reply: none. 3. I asserted that the power of the Gospel light is so great that, if foreigners, Venetians, Italians, Spaniards and others, were given free access to the orthodox books, all the superstitions of the whole Papacy would easily collapse. Reply: none. 4. I related historically the purpose, method, end and use of the Holy Translation undertaken and completed by the Zurich theologians. Reply: none. 5. I showed that translations of the Holy Bible from the native language into Latin, or into another common and vernacular tongue, were free in the Christian Church from ancient times. Reply: none. 6. I contended that the decree of the Council of Vienne in Gaul, on reviving the study of the Oriental languages for the propagation of the Christian faith among the Saracens, paved the way for the Reformation to come. Reply: none. 7. I cited the notable testimony and encomium of Jacques-Auguste de Thou, president of Paris, a man of the Papist party, paid to the writings of our theologians. Reply: none. 8. To the clear testimony of Dr Luther, given before the heat of the Sacramentarian conflict, paid to the Helvetic Confession of the Churches. Reply: none. 9. To the whole chapter on the Zurich translation of the Bible, published by Robert Estienne, royal printer of Paris, etc. Reply: none. 10. To the objection concerning the expurgatory Index, drawn up by the decree of the Council of Trent, in which the monuments of the Fathers, the Church histories, the Annals and the writings of recent authors are mutilated by a wicked fraud. Reply: none. 11. To our argument concerning the ancient faith of the first Zurich martyrs, Saints Felix and Regula, as to the chief points of the fundamental heavenly doctrine. Reply: none. 12. That the charge of Sacramentarian heresy is unjustly brought against our people, who have hitherto taught consistently with Scripture and orthodox antiquity concerning the essence, form, properties, end, use and effects of the sacraments. Reply: none. 13. I asserted, on firm grounds, that the most honourable elogium of bishops is rightly paid to the ministers of the Zurich Church, and to the Spanish theologian Ferdinand de Escalante, etc. Reply: none. 14. I reminded Gretser that Huldrych Zwingli is foolishly and slanderously called "Baal of Zurich" by the Jesuits, and that he ought much more truly to be named Antibaal and Baalimastix, etc. Reply: none. 15. I vindicated, with a clear conscience, the most honourable family of Leo Jud, whose parents and grandparents professed not the Jewish but the Christian faith in Alsace, and his most peaceful and blessed death, etc. Reply: none. 16. In defence of Gualther's poem, the arguments of the individual chapters of Scripture gathered together, and the description of the Roman Antichrist by the example of the community of the orders of the empire. Reply: none.

units.la: {1} Praetermissione fucata Cardinalium — ms. marginal reference marks as in text. singulorum S. Scripturæ capitum complexi: & ad descriptionem Romani Antichristi exemplo ordinum imperij communitatem, Resp. N. 17. Ad Demonstrationem Logicam, pro elogio Christianismi & Catholicismi, Ecclesijs per omnia Europæa regna Reformatis, jure convenientis, Responsio nulla data fuit.
units.tr: {1} The concealment, by a pretence, of the principal arguments. Marginal reference marks as in the text. 17. To the logical demonstration, in praise of Christianity and Catholicism, rightly belonging to the churches reformed throughout all the kingdoms of Europe: no reply was ever given.

units.la: SECVNDAE fraudis Gretserianæ exempla, Assumptio rationum nostrarum Sophistica, mutila & manca. 1. Nomen & antiquitatem Pagi Tigurini, inter Helvetios primarij, olim à Iulio Cæsare ob virtutem bellicam magnificè celebrati, noftratibus invidiosè à Gretsero abjudicari. 2. Gravissima injuriarum onera recensui Historicè ex libris fide dignis, quæ Veneta Respublica Serenissima, jure pridem à Pontifice Romano sustinuerit: Gretserus duobus prioribus prætermissis, tertium duntaxat de Iesuitarum opulentia ventilavit. 3. Illustre encomium Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Pastoribus in Clypeo Venetiano tributum, ab Hispano Theologo ex ignoratione Civitatis Tigurinæ profectum esse, falsò contendit Gretserus. 4. Fidem Protomartyrum Tigurinorum cum nostrate Evangelica doctrinâ consentientem fuisse, multiplici sophismate & fallacia Gretserus oppugnato.
units.tr: The SECOND examples of Gretser's fraud: the sophistical, maimed and defective assumption of our reasons. 1. The name and antiquity of the Pagus Tigurinus, first among the Helvetii, once magnificently celebrated by Julius Caesar for its martial courage: Gretser falsely denies it to our people, out of envy. 2. I recounted historically the most grievous burdens of injuries which the most Serene Venetian Republic had long since rightly endured from the Roman Pontiff, from trustworthy books. Gretser, passing over the first two, touched only the third, on the wealth of the Jesuits. 3. Gretser falsely maintains that the illustrious encomium paid to the ministers of the Zurich Church in the Venetian Shield came from a Spanish theologian through ignorance of the city of Zurich. 4. That the faith of the Zurich protomartyrs agreed with our Evangelical doctrine, Gretser attacked with manifold sophistry and fallacy.

units.la: TERTIAE Fraudis Gretserianæ Exempla. Infarsio alienorum & ad præsentem causam minimè spectantium. 1. Donatio Ludovici Germanici, & Ludovici Pii Regum Franciæ, facta Part henoni Sanctimonialium urbis Tigurinæ, à se condito. 2. Factum Illustrissimi Ducis Saxoniæ Augusti, Biblia Tigurina Germanica Sacello suo removeri jubentis. 3. Quæstio heterogenea: An Christiani Doctores verum & genuinum Hebraici textus sensum in Veteri Testamento, salva conscientia, ex Rabbinorum libris depromere posint? 4. Invectiva digressio in clarissimum sacræ linguæ Professorem Ioh. Drusium, ejusque, filium jam placidè defunctum. 5. Sebastiani Castalionis, Immanuelis Tremellij, Francisci Iunij, versiones S. Bibliorum, nobis à Gretsero objectæ. 6. Priscæ constitutiones quædam Caroli Magni, & Ludovici Germanici, Regum Franciæ, contra Sacerdotum, Monachorum, Monialium &c. thorum matrimonialem. 7. Descriptio viri hæretici ex Epiphanio, Isidoro, Tertulliano, Theodoreto &c. adducta. 8. Vellicatio calumniosa & aculeata Melchioris Goldasti, &c.
units.tr: The THIRD examples of Gretser's fraud: the insertion of foreign matters which do not bear at all on the present case. 1. The gift of Louis the German and Louis the Pious, kings of France, made to the Parthenon, the nunnery of the city of Zurich, founded by himself. 2. The deed of the most illustrious Duke of Saxony, Augustus, who ordered the German Zurich Bible to be removed from his chapel. 3. A heterogeneous question: whether Christian teachers may, with a clear conscience, draw the true and genuine sense of the Hebrew text of the Old Testament from the books of the rabbis? 4. An invective digression against the most famous professor of the sacred language, John Drusius, and against his son, now peacefully deceased. 5. The versions of the Holy Bible by Sebastian Castellio, Immanuel Tremellius and Francis Junius, objected to us by Gretser. 6. Certain ancient constitutions of Charlemagne and Louis the German, kings of France, against the marriage bed of priests, monks, nuns, etc. 7. A description of a heretical man, cited from Epiphanius, Isidore, Tertullian, Theodoret, etc. 8. The slanderous and stinging sneer of Melchior Goldast, etc.

units.la: QVARTAE fraudis Gretserianæ Exempla. Convitia virulenta testimonijs Capitalium Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ hostium excusata, &c. 1. Condemnatio doctrinæ Zuinglianæ, à D.
