Luthero immoderato æstu abrepto facta. 2. Crimen falsatæ Translationis Novi Testamenti Germanicæ, à Conrado Schlüsselburgio Tigurinis intentatum. 3. Testimonium Iohannis Fabri, vicarij Constantiensis de ingenio Zuinglij. 4. Narratio calumniosa Christophori Harthmanni, Historici Eremitani, de moribus & actionibus Zuinglij, Leonis Iudæ, Sacerdotum in Eremo. 5. Fabula anilis de Moyse, Iudæo quodam Vitodurano, Zuinglij Zuinglij Magistro & informatore in literis Hebraicis. 6. Mendacium impudentissimum, de cineribus S. Felicis & Regulae, hortatu Zuinglij in praeterlabentem Limagum effusis, &c. Quae singula breviuscule, moderate & solide dilatabo. Placuit haec ex ipsius authoris autographo hoc loco adspergere. 2. De religione antiqua & Catholica S. Felicis, & S. Regulae Proto-Martyrum Tigurinorum, reliquorum item Legionis Thebaeae Sociorum, Historia succincta, & veritate monumentorum Ecclesiasticorum consentanea. Tig. 1628. Prodijt etiam Germanice. Epitomen ejus Oratione Panegyrica recensuit die 12. Septembr. 1627. 3. De Ecclesia Electorum Dei, inter medium praeteritorum saeculorum Papatum ὑπόστασις seu existentia, & conservatione perpetua, Tig. 1627. 4. De religione Ecclesiarum Graecanicarum tum veteris, tum hodierna, disquisitio Theologica & Historica, Tig. 1621. 5. Orationes duae, quarum altera secularis, commemorans Reformationis Ecclesiae Tigurinae annis ab hinc centenis elapsis, institutae beneficium divinum; posterior paraenetica, suggerens remedia, quae gravi dissidiorum scandalo, in Ecclesiis Reformatis leniendo, pie adhiberi possunt. Tig. 1629. 6. Oratio de Statu Ecclesiarum Reformatarum hodierno tristi & calamitoso, Tig. 1625. habita. 7. Diatribe de Sacramentis in genere, & specie, qua capita Confessionis Helveticae 19. 20 & 21. circa quaestiones controversas certis aphorismis comprehenduntur. Disputatio fuit synodalis 1629. 8. Elenchus errorum, quibus Orthodoxia Ecclesiarum Reformatarum de S. Eucharistia, a Pontificijs impetitur, de praesentia & manducatione Christi corporali; de Transsubstantiatione, de communione sub una specie, de sacrificio Missae propitiatorio. Tiguri 1630. 9. Vindicatio Capitis 17. Confessionis Helveticae, de Ecclesia Christi Catholica, adversus praecipuas Iesuitarum Hypotheses, Tig. 1628. Docta, & temporibus nostris feliciter accommodata disputatio. 10. Fidelis paraenesis ad Anabaptistas Schismaticos; qua status Ecclesiae Helveticae describitur, & ab adversariorum civillis vindicatur. Tig. 1615. Germ. 11. De certitudine salutis, ex Ioh. X. Tigur. 1617. ad Generos. V. Vilhelmum, Rupae Dominum, S. C. Majest. Consiliarium, & Camerarium &c. qui filium, Iohannem Henricum, ab Ecclesia Bremensi commendatum, praeceptorem domesticum, per biennium, & cum fructu filio Ottoni destinavit, & cum laude dimisit. Praeterea, quae jam recensuimus edita, ἀνέκδοτα quaedam sunt, magni judicij, eximiaeque eruditionis sacrae & profanae, monumenta; cujusmodi sunt. 1. Tractatus de Helvetia, ejus initio, progressu, rebus gestis, causis dissidiorum, eorumque remediis. 2. Confessionis Helveticae explicatio, praemissa narratione causarum & occasionis scripti illius editi; cujus & Celeberrimus D. Gernlerus noster meminit Disp. 2. de Confessione Helvetica. 3. Examen & confutatio Fundamentorum, quibus Neoburgicus Princeps, falsò vanèque innixus à Reformata Evangelicorum Ecclesia ad Papisticam superstitionem defecit 1615.
units.tr: The FOURTH examples of Gretser's fraud: virulent insults, excused by the testimonies of the chief enemies of the Zurich Church, etc. 1. The condemnation of Zwinglian doctrine, made by Dr Luther, carried away by immoderate heat. 2. The charge of a falsified translation of the German New Testament, brought against the Zurich people by Conrad Schlüsselburg. 3. The testimony of John Faber, vicar of Constance, concerning the character of Zwingli. 4. The slanderous narrative of Christopher Hartmann, an Eremite historian, concerning the morals and actions of Zwingli, of Leo Jud, and of the priests in the hermitage. 5. An old wives' tale about Moses, a certain Jew of Winterthur, who was Zwingli's teacher and instructor in Hebrew letters. 6. The most shameless lie, about the ashes of Saints Felix and Regula, poured into the passing Limmat at Zwingli's urging, etc. I shall expand each of these items briefly, moderately and soundly. It has pleased me to set these down here from the author's own autograph. 2. On the ancient and Catholic religion of Saint Felix and Saint Regula, the first Zurich martyrs, and likewise of the companions of the Theban Legion, a succinct history, consistent with the truth of ecclesiastical monuments. Zurich 1628. It also appeared in German. He reviewed its epitome in a panegyric oration on 12 September 1627. 3. On the Church of God's elect, its hypostasis or existence and perpetual preservation amid the Papacy of the intervening centuries, Zurich 1627. 4. On the religion of the Greek churches, both ancient and present, a theological and historical inquiry, Zurich 1621. 5. Two orations, one secular, recalling the divine benefit of the institution of the Reformation of the Zurich Church, a hundred years having elapsed since then; the other paraenetic, suggesting remedies which may be piously applied to soften the grave scandal of dissensions in the Reformed Churches. Zurich 1629. 6. An oration on the present sad and calamitous state of the Reformed Churches, delivered at Zurich 1625. 7. A diatribe on the sacraments in general and in particular, in which the 19th, 20th and 21st chapters of the Helvetic Confession are summarised in certain aphorisms on the controverted questions. It was a synodal disputation, 1629. 8. A refutation of the errors with which the orthodoxy of the Reformed Churches concerning the Holy Eucharist is assailed by the Papists: concerning the corporeal presence and manducation of Christ, concerning transubstantiation, communion under one kind, and the propitiatory sacrifice of the Mass. Zurich 1630. 9. Vindication of the 17th chapter of the Helvetic Confession, on the Catholic Church of Christ, against the chief hypotheses of the Jesuits, Zurich 1628. A learned disputation, happily adapted to our times. 10. A faithful exhortation to the schismatic Anabaptists, in which the state of the Helvetic Church is described and defended against the civil charges of its adversaries. Zurich 1615; also in German. 11. On the certainty of salvation, from John 10, Zurich 1617, addressed to the noble Wilhelm von Rupa, lord of Rupa, imperial councillor and chamberlain, etc., who entrusted his son, John Henry, commended by the Church of Bremen, as a domestic tutor for two years, to his son Otto, and dismissed him with praise. Besides these works already listed as published, there are certain unpublished monuments of great judgment and of exceptional sacred and profane learning, such as these: 1. A treatise on Helvetia, its beginnings, progress, events, the causes of its dissensions and the remedies for them. 2. An explanation of the Helvetic Confession, prefaced by a narrative of the causes and occasion of that published writing; of which our most celebrated Dr Gernler also makes mention, in his second disputation on the Helvetic Confession. 3. An examination and refutation of the foundations on which the Prince of Neuburg, falsely and vainly relying on them, defected in 1615 from the Reformed Church of the Evangelicals to Papist superstition.

units.la: Huldricus Iob. Iacobus, Henrici Professoris & Canonici Filius, ex Professore primum Historiarum, Diacono postea Abbatissano, & Ædis ad Sp. S. Pastore, Templi summi Antistes vigilantissimus, inter perpetuas, quibus publico nomine distringitur, curas, plurimas meditationes sacras & Politico-Historicas confripsit, Homilias in Genesin, Ruth, utrumque Samuelis, Esther, Ieremiam, in aliquot Danielis capita: In Matthæum, Marcum, ad Romanos, utramque ad Corinthios. Exercitationes in N.T. Varias Conciones Militares, Festales, Pænitentiales, Consulares &c. Sermones Synodales, & Scholasticos: Orationes publicas de notis Ecclesiæ, bonis Ecclesiasticis, Theologia Catechetica, de Studio Arithmetico Ethico, Historico, de rubo Mosis, militia moderna, Carolo Borromæo. Edita hactenus sunt, Additamentum ad tractat. Italic. de jubilæo, Letanie Christianæ contra il Turco, Rosario del Soldato Christiano Ital. & Germ. Fata Magni Gustavi in 4. Germ. De Vesuvio ignivomo, &c. Deus porrò sanctis ejus laboribus clementer benedicat.
units.tr: Huldrich Johann Jakob, son of Professor and Canon Heinrich. He was first professor of history, then deacon at Abbatissa, then minister of the church of the Holy Spirit, and finally the most vigilant chief minister of the Great Minster. Amid the constant cares that burden him in his public office, he has written many sacred and political-historical meditations: homilies on Genesis, Ruth, both books of Samuel, Esther, Jeremiah, and several chapters of Daniel; on Matthew, Mark, Romans, and both letters to the Corinthians; exercises on the New Testament; various sermons for soldiers, for feast days, for penitence, for the magistrates, and so on; synodal and scholastic sermons; and public orations on the marks of the Church, on church property, on catechetical theology, on the study of arithmetic, ethics and history, on the burning bush of Moses, on modern warfare, and on Charles Borromeo. Hitherto published are: an addition to his Italian treatise on the jubilee; Christian litanies against the Turk; The Christian Soldier's Rosary, in Italian and German; The Deeds of Gustavus the Great, in quarto, in German; On the Fire-Spewing Vesuvius, and so on. May God graciously bless his holy labours further.

units.la: Huserus Conradus, montis Hirzelani pastor ad an Chr. 1582. Tractatum de impostis & Ceremoniis Iudæorum nostri temporis antea Germanicè editum, Latinè vertit, vulgavitque Basil. 1575.
units.tr: Conrad Huser, minister at Hirzel mountain. In the year of Christ 1582 he translated into Latin, and published at Basel in 1575, a treatise on the superstitions and ceremonies of the Jews of our time, which had earlier appeared in German.

units.la: Huslinus Rodolphus, V. D. in agro Tigurino Minister, Gessneri Historiam avium in Linguam Germanicam transtulit.
units.tr: Rudolf Huslin, Minister of the Divine Word in the Zurich territory, translated Gesner's Natural History of Birds into German.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Irmingerus Iob. Iacobus, Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Minister in Æde primum Petrina ab a. Ch. 1620. postea Basilica ab an 1645 ad 1649 quo obijt. Solidus fuit Theologus, facundus Orator, doctus Poeta. Plurima ejus extant carmina Latina & Germanica, inter alia urbis Tigurinæ munimentum, & Musarum Tigurinarum monimentum, quo Amplissimo Viro D. Ioh. Rodolpho Rhanio de Consulatu fuit gratulatus an. Ch. 1644. d. 8. Octobris, Bivium Herculis, &c. Edidit præterea libellum Germanicum de tribus primariis, Christianismi articulis, de vera fide, resipiscentia, patientia in morte & afflictionibus, Tig. 1522.
units.tr: Johann Jakob Irminger, minister of the Church of Zurich: first at the church of St. Peter, from the year of Christ 1620, and afterwards at the Minster, from 1645 until 1649, when he died. He was a sound theologian, an eloquent orator, and a learned poet. Many of his Latin and German poems survive, among them "The Fortress of the City of Zurich" and "The Monument of the Muses of Zurich", with which he congratulated the most distinguished Johann Rudolf Rahn on his consulship in the year of Christ 1644, on 8 October; also "The Crossroads of Hercules", and so on. He also published a German booklet on three chief articles of Christianity: on true faith, repentance, and patience in death and affliction (Zurich, 1522).

units.la: Iudæ, Leo, Alsatus natione, Zuinglij in fano Eremitano primum successor, postea in Tigurina Ecclesia Collega, Templi ad D. Patrum Pastor ab a. Ch. 1522, ad 1542. quo die 18. Iunij Vir laboriosissimus, fuit defunctus. Ex ore Zuinglij Reformatoris annotationes in Genesin & Exodum, item in quatuor Evangelistas; Pasionis Dominicæ Historiam, ac in Epistolas Pauli ad Romanos, Cor. Philip. Colost. Thess. & in Iacobi Epistolam, Annotationes excepit, quæ in folio Tiguri denuò excusæ anno 1581. Præterea opus articulorum sive conclusionum Huldr. Zuinglij è Germanico Latinum reddidit: quod & cum reliquis Zuinglij operibus habetur, & seorsim Tiguri excusum est 1535. Catechismum majorem & minorem Germanicè scripsit, distributum in vices interrogandi & respondendi, impressos ibidem. Veteris Testamenti libros Hebraicos simplici & pură dictione, e sacra Hebræorum Lingua, consultis simul Orthodoxis interpretibus, in Latinam transtulit, fide & religione summa. Passim autem per tota Biblia annotationes, & variæ lectiones marginibus adjiciuntur: Froschouerus excudit Tig. An. 1543. De hac Editione, quæ Tigurina καθ' ἐξοχὴν dicitur, alibi prolixius egimus. Historiam passionis Domini nostri ex quatuor Evangelistis conjunctam, clara & simplici expositione Germanicè scripsit, impressam Tiguri. Def. Erasmi paraphrases in Novum Testamentum, in Germanicum sermonem vertit, adjecta declaratione in Apocalypsin Iohannis, per D. Contradum Pellicanum: ibidem excusas. Antea quoque tota Biblia Germanicè reddiderat, ad Hebraicam veritatem, cum Iudæo quodam diligenter collata, quæ irid Tigur. edita sunt. Claruit apud Tigurinos an. 1540. scripsit etiam Germanicè de sepultura, resurrectione & ascensione Christi, & missione Spiritus Sancti. Zuinglij Antibolon contra Empserum, de vera & falsa religione, providentia, ad Christianum Regem in Germanicam Linguam convertit. Bullingeri librum contra Anabaptistas Latinitate donavit.
units.tr: Leo Jud, an Alsatian by birth, first successor of Zwingli at the Hermitage church, and afterwards colleague of Zwingli in the Zurich Church, minister of the church of St. Peter from the year of Christ 1522 until 1542, when this most industrious man died on 18 June. From the mouth of Zwingli the Reformer he took down notes on Genesis and Exodus, likewise on the four Evangelists, on the history of the Lord's Passion, and on Paul's letters to the Romans, Corinthians, Philippians, Colossians and Thessalonians, and on the letter of James. These notes were printed again in folio at Zurich in 1581. He also translated into Latin the work of Huldrich Zwingli on the articles or conclusions, from German; this is found with Zwingli's other works and was also printed separately at Zurich in 1535. He wrote a larger and a smaller Catechism in German, arranged in questions and answers, printed in the same place. He translated the Hebrew books of the Old Testament into Latin, in a plain and pure style, from the sacred Hebrew language, consulting at the same time orthodox interpreters, with the greatest faithfulness and piety. Throughout the whole Bible, annotations and variant readings are added in the margins; Froschauer printed it at Zurich in the year 1543. This edition, called Tigurina [the Zurich edition] par excellence [καθ' ἐξοχὴν], we have discussed at greater length elsewhere. He wrote in German, in a clear and simple exposition, the history of the Passion of our Lord, harmonized from the four Evangelists; it was printed at Zurich. He translated into German the paraphrases of Erasmus on the New Testament, with an explanation of the Apocalypse of John by Dr. Conrad Pellican added; these were printed in the same place. Earlier he had also rendered the whole Bible into German, carefully collated with a certain Jew for the Hebrew truth; these were published at Zurich. He flourished among the Zurich people in the year 1540. He also wrote in German on the burial, resurrection and ascension of Christ, and on the mission of the Holy Spirit. He turned into German Zwingli's Antibolon against Emser, on true and false religion and on providence, addressed to the Christian King. He gave a Latin dress to Bullinger's book against the Anabaptists.

units.la: K.
units.tr: K.

units.la: Kolerus, Iacobus, L.A.M. Ecclesiæ Elcovianæ Minister, an Chr. 1591. Vicinarumque inspector 1599 ad 1611, quo obijt. Genevæ Auditor fuit Bezæ, post-ea Marpurgi Magisterij gradum consecutus domum redijt. Edidit tractatum de animæ propagatione, sitne ex traduce, an immediatè à Deo inspiretur? Conciones VI. de ultimo judicio German. Habeo plura ejus Msc. præsertim practica.
units.tr: Jakob Koler, Master of Liberal Arts, minister of the church at Elgg, from the year of Christ 1591; inspector of the neighbouring churches from 1599 until 1611, when he died. At Geneva he was a hearer of Beza; afterwards, having obtained the degree of Master at Marburg, he returned home. He published a treatise on the propagation of the soul: whether it comes by traduction, or is breathed in immediately by God? Six sermons on the Last Judgment, in German. I have several of his manuscripts, especially practical ones.

units.la: Kolerus Felix, Iacobi F. Pastor Muranus ad lacum Gryphæum ab a.Ch. 1621. ad 1635. Vir diligentissimus & felix analyticus. Meletemata edidit quædam in Psalm. 8. Prima institutionis elementaris fundamenta candidissimo Viro, grato animo, fero accepta.
units.tr: Felix Koler, son of Jakob, minister at Mur on Lake Greifen from the year of Christ 1621 until 1635: a most diligent man and a gifted analyst. He published some meditations on Psalm 8. To the most candid man, I received the first foundations of elementary instruction with a grateful and receptive mind.

units.la: Kufen Iodocus, Verbi inagro Tigurino primum Minister, Professor deinde Artium Logicarum in Collegio Humanitatis; Professor denique Carolinus ad an. Chr. 1630. quo, dum Scholarchæ administraret provinciam, decessit, vulgavit Orationem de vita & obitu celeberrimi Ecclesiæ & Scholæ nostræ Theologi, D. Ioh. Caspari VVaseri.
units.tr: Jodocus Kufen, first minister of the Word in the Zurich territory, then professor of the liberal arts of logic in the College of Humanity, and finally Carolinian professor, until the year of Christ 1630, when he died while administering the office of scholarch. He published an oration on the life and death of Dr. Johann Caspar Waser, most celebrated theologian of our Church and School.

units.la: Kriegius Iohannes, antiquissimus Tigurinorum Historicus, Annales conscripsit, quorum Stumpfius meminit pag. 480. b. & Bulling. de reb. Tigurin. l. 8.
units.tr: Johannes Kriegius, the oldest historian of the Zurich people, wrote annals, which Stumpf mentions on page 480, b., and Bullinger, On the Affairs of Zurich, book 8.

units.la: L.
units.tr: L.

units.la: Landebergius Rodolphus V.D. in agro Tigurino Minister, vertit ex Latina in Germanicam Linguam Evonymi Philiatri Thesaurum
units.tr: Landebergius Rodolphus V.D., minister in the Zurich countryside, translated into the German language the Thesaurus of Evonymus Philiatros from Latin.

units.la: Lavaterus Ioh. Casparus, Professor in Collegio Carolino ab an. Chr. 1623. ad 1637. Extant pro laurea suprema quæstiones Medicæ Cardinales quatuor.
units.tr: Lavaterus Ioh. Casparus, professor at the Carolinum from 1623 to 1637. There are extant four cardinal medical questions for his highest degree.

units.la: Lavaterus Henricus, Medicinæ Doctor, Professor Physicus & Collegij Carolini Præpositus ab an.Chr. 1601. usque ad 1623. scripsit Epitomen Philosophiæ Naturalis. Disputationem de Terræ motu.
units.tr: Lavaterus Henricus, Doctor of Medicine, professor of physics and provost of the Carolinum from 1601 to 1623. He wrote an epitome of natural philosophy and a disputation on the motion of the earth.

units.la: Lavaterus Iob.Henricus, Medicinæ Doctor, & publicus in Collegio Carolino Professor, Collega honorandus, superioris filius, dedit disputationem de Arthritide, & Paradoxis chirurgicis.
units.tr: Lavaterus Iob. Henricus, Doctor of Medicine and public professor at the Carolinum, a colleague to be honoured, son of the above, published a disputation on arthritis and surgical paradoxes.

units.la: Lavater Ludovicus, Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Archi Diaconus 1550. Antistes 1585. Obijt 1586. Vtilissimis suis scriptis, Exegeticis præsertim, magnam sibi nominis conciliavit famam. Et primo quidem Henrici Bullingeri, Soceri sui sermones de Cœna Domini duos ex GermanicaLingua in Latinam transtulit, quos Froschouerus excudit Tiguri an.Domini 1553. Idem Procopij commentaria Græca in libros Regum 1.2. & 4. item in primum Paralipomenon Latinitate donavit, cum reliquis Procopij commentarijs, excusa à Gessneris fratribus. Scripsit insuper de ritibus & institutis Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ libellum, excusum in 8. Historiam de origine & progressu controversiæ Sacramentariæ de Cœna Domini, ab anno D. 1524. usque ad annum 1563. deductam, Latinè, apud Froschouerum in 4. Eadem Historia locupletior prodijt Germanicè, Iob. Stumpfio interprete, in 8. De Spectris, Lemuribus, & magnis atque insolitis fragoribus variisque præsagitionibus, quæ plerunque obitum hominum, magnas clades, mutationesque imperiorum præcedunt: lib. Germ. editum Tig. apud Froschouerum, & Latinè Genevæ apud Ioh. Crispinum. Idem liber conversus est in Linguam quoque Gallicam & Italicam. Nuper demum in Belgio prodijt. Cometarum Catalogum, excusum Tig. apud Gessnerum. De pestilentia Conciones 2. inquibus ostenditur, unde sit pestis, & quare immittatur, item quo pacto se gerere debeant, qui illo morbo corripiuntur. Germ. Accesit Cypriani sermo de mortalitate vel peste in Linguam Germanicam ab eodem conversus. De caritate annonæ & fame Conciones 3. quæ & Germanicè editæ sunt, & in Latinam Linguam conversæ, & commentarijs in Ezechielem insertæ, sed ordine aliquantum mutato. Commentarios in Proverbia Salomonis, excusos à Froschouero in quarto & in folio. Commentarios in librum Iosuæ ab eod. excus. in 4. & in folio. Homilias sive commentarios in Ezechielem Prophetam, Genevæ apud Ioh.Crispinum, in folio. In primum & secundum librum Paralipomenon commentaria, additis tabulis Genealogiarum. Tiguri, 1572. in folio.Henrici Bullingeri Homilias in Apocalypsin in Linguam Germanicam convertit, excusas in folio & in 8. It. tractatum Bullingeri super hæc verba 14. Cap Iohannis, In domo patris mei mansiones multæ sunt &c. Scripsit ad hæc Conciones de fide Iobi, quæ Germanicè excusa est, Tiguri in 8. Aliam de patientia ex 5. capite Epistolæ, quæ ibidem est impressa. Vitam Henrici Bullingeri Germanicè evulgavit, cui addita est Refutatio Iosiæ Simleri calumniarum Iacobi Andreæ, contra responsionem ministrorum Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ editarum, à Lavatero conversa in Linguam Germanicam. Explicationem in octo postrema capita commentarijs Petri Martyris in Genesin additam. Ejusdem in Iobum 141. homiliæ; Germanicè in folio publicè extant. Apologiam ministrorum Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ contra Iacobum Smidelinum ex Latina in Germanicam Linguam convertit. Vitam Conradi Pellicani edidit in sol. ut operibus adjungi posset. Librum Ruth 28. homiliis expo fuit, quæ in Linguam Italicam conversa sunt, àIohanne Martio. Librum Hester 47. homilijs expositum edidit Germanicè, omnia impressa sunt apud Froschouerum Tigari. Habeo ejusdem Compendium Historicum, propria ejus manu scriptum, inde à tempore Reformationis, & Epistolas nonnullas ἀνεκδότας.
units.tr: Lavater Ludovicus, archdeacon of the Tigurine Church from 1550, chief minister from 1585, died 1586. By his very useful writings, especially his exegetical ones, he won for himself a great reputation. First, he translated into Latin two sermons on the Lord's Supper by Heinrich Bullinger, his father-in-law, which Froschauer printed at Zurich in 1553. He also turned into Latin the Greek commentaries of Procopius on the books of Kings 1, 2 and 4, and likewise on the first book of Chronicles, which were printed together with Procopius's other commentaries by the Gessner brothers. He further wrote a little book on the rites and institutions of the Tigurine Church, printed in octavo; a history of the origin and progress of the sacramentarian controversy on the Lord's Supper, covering the years 1524 to 1563, in Latin, printed by Froschauer in quarto. The same history appeared in a fuller German version, translated by Iob. Stumpfius, in octavo. On spectres, ghosts, great and unusual noises and various omens, which usually go before the deaths of men, great disasters and changes of empires: this was published in German at Zurich by Froschauer, and in Latin at Geneva by Jean Crespin. The same book was also turned into French and Italian, and lately it has appeared in the Netherlands. A catalogue of comets, printed at Zurich by Gessner. Two sermons on the plague, in which it is shown whence the plague comes and why it is sent, and likewise how those who are seized by that disease ought to conduct themselves; in German. To these is added a sermon on mortality or plague by Cyprian, translated into German by the same man. Three sermons on the dearth of grain and famine, which were both published in German and translated into Latin, and inserted into his commentaries on Ezekiel, though in a somewhat altered order. Commentaries on the Proverbs of Solomon, printed by Froschauer in quarto and folio. Commentaries on the book of Joshua, printed by the same in quarto and folio. Homilies or commentaries on the prophet Ezekiel, at Geneva by Jean Crespin, in folio. Commentaries on the first and second books of Chronicles, with genealogical tables added; at Zurich, 1572, in folio. He translated into German Heinrich Bullinger's homilies on the Apocalypse, printed in folio and octavo. Also a treatise of Bullinger on these words of John chapter 14, In my Father's house are many mansions, etc. Besides these, he wrote sermons on the faith of Job, which were published in German at Zurich in octavo, and another on patience from the fifth chapter of the Epistle, printed there too. He published Bullinger's life in German, to which was added a refutation by Josias Simler of the calumnies of Jacob Andreae, against the reply of the ministers of the Tigurine Church, translated by Lavater into German. An explanation of the last eight chapters, added to Peter Martyr's commentaries on Genesis. Also 141 homilies of the same on Job; these exist publicly in German in folio. He translated from Latin into German the apology of the ministers of the Tigurine Church against Iacobus Schmidelin. He published the life of Conrad Pellican in folio, so that it could be added to his works. He expounded the book of Ruth in 28 homilies, which were translated into Italian by Johann Martius. He published in German the book of Esther, expounded in 47 homilies; all were printed by Froschauer at Zurich. I have his historical compendium, written in his own hand from the time of the Reformation, and some letters unpublished [ἀνεκδότας].

units.la: Lavaterus Ioh. Rodolphus, Tigurinus, Gymnasij Hanovien sis Rector vocatus inde ad Professionem Rhetoricam Logicam in Collegio Humanitatis 1611. ad eandem artium Professionem publicam in Collegio Carolino 1612. ad 1615. quo obijt. Edita ab eo sunt Anti-Socinus, hoc est, solida & exacta confutatio omnium & singulorum errorum, quos olim Arriani, Ebionitæ, Samosatenia ni, Pelagiani, & Trithetitæ, horribili audacia propugnârunt, & nuper demum Servetus, Ochinus, Blandrata, F Davidis, Socinus, Christoph. Ostorodus, eorumque complices ab inferis revocarunt, cum solida & Orthodoxa assertione Deitatis Iesu Christi & Sp. S. & imputationis meriti Christi pro peccatis nostris, &c. cum innumeris aliis. Omnia jam primum ex doctissimorum ævi nostri Theologorum scriptis erut a, & boni publici causa conjunctim edita, Francofurti 1612. cum Rod. Lavateri præfatione, in qua monet, pleraque ex Paræi Commentarijs, & Simleri tractatu desumta &c. Jacobi Chynæi, Abarnage, Scoti Analysis & Scholia in Aristotel. XIV. libros, de prima seu divina Philosophia, editio nova emendata, & notis aucta, opera & studio Ioh. Rod. Lavateri, Hanov. 1607. Defensio Medicorum Galenicorum, adversus Calumnias Angeli Salæ, operarij Chymici, in qua superba ejus censura examinatur & confutatur, per Henricum Lavaterum, D. Hanoviæ 1610. Καταβασις εις ἅδης, hoc est, de descensu Iesu Christi ad inferos tractatus Scholasticus & Theologicus in duos libros tributus, Fran. 1610. Quæstio, ubi vera & Catholica Iesu Christi Ecclesia invenienda sit, abs Andrea Dudithio, Oratore Cæsareo, olim Iohanni VVolfio, & Theodoro Bezæ per Epistolam propositæ, & horum ad eandem solidissimæ responsiones, quarum illa de novo prodiit, hæc emendationes, studio Ioh. Rodolphi Lavateri, Hanov. 1610. Ejusdem prodiunt disquisitiones Philosophicæ: Disput. Logic. de termino vocis: De natura Systematis Physici: De miscell. quæstionibus Philosophicis: De præcipuis benè stabiliendæ Reipublicæ mediis. Oratio denique ejus, de Canonisatione Ignatij Lojolæ, & Francisci Xaverii cum notis. Leemannus, Burkhardus, Tigurinus, Scholae aliquandiu Schafhusianae, postea Ecclesiae Tigurinae tum in Abbatissana, tum Carolina Aede pastor, cum antea etiam ad Sp.S. Zuinglio junioři successisset. Mortuus est an. Chr. 1613. Antistes, ad quod officium an. Chr. 1584. designatus erat. Scripsit brevissimam, Methodicam, & ad quatuor capita reductam institutionem religionis Christianae, Germanicè 1583. Epigramma in Psalterij Paraphrasin Rodolphi Leemanni. Habeo ἀνέκδοτα ejus scripta tum Apologetica contra Phil. Nicolai scriptum virulentum, tum Historica, varia veterum authorum iudicia, de Antichristo.
units.tr: Lavaterus Ioh. Rodolphus, of Zurich, rector of the Hanau gymnasium, was then called to the professorship of rhetoric and logic at the Collegium Humanitatis in 1611, and to the same public professorship of the arts at the Carolinum from 1612 until 1615, when he died. There were published by him: Anti-Socinus, that is, a solid and exact refutation of all and each of the errors which the Arians, Ebionites, Samosatenes, Pelagians and Tritheists once defended with dreadful audacity, and which Servetus, Ochino, Blandrata, Francis David, Socinus, Christoph Ostorodt and their accomplices have lately recalled from the dead, together with a solid and orthodox assertion of the deity of Jesus Christ and of the Holy Spirit, and of the imputation of Christ's merit for our sins, etc., along with countless others. All of these, drawn from the writings of the most learned theologians of our age, were first brought together and published for the public good at Frankfurt in 1612, with a preface by Rudolf Lavater, in which he notes that many things are taken from the commentaries of Paraeus and the treatise of Simler, etc. Jacobus Chynaeus, Abarnagius, Scotus: Analysis and Scholia on Aristotle's fourteen books on first or divine philosophy, a new edition, corrected and enlarged with notes, by the work and care of Johann Rudolf Lavater, Hanau 1607. Defence of the Galenic Physicians against the calumnies of Angelus Sala, the chemical workman, in which his arrogant censure is examined and refuted, by Heinrich Lavater, Doctor, Hanau 1610. Katabasis eis Hades [Καταβασις εις ἅδης], that is, a scholastic and theological treatise on the descent of Jesus Christ into hell, in two books, Frankfurt 1610. The question where the true and Catholic Church of Jesus Christ is to be found, proposed by letter by Andreas Dudith, imperial envoy, formerly to John Wolf and Theodore Beza, and the very solid replies of these to the same; the former appeared anew, the latter with corrections, by the care of Johann Rudolf Lavater, Hanau 1610. There also appear his philosophical inquiries: a logical disputation on the term of a word; on the nature of a physical system; on miscellaneous philosophical questions; on the chief means of establishing a commonwealth well. Lastly, his oration on the canonisation of Ignatius Loyola and Francis Xavier, with notes. Leemann, Burkhard, of Zurich, for some time schoolmaster at Schaffhausen, afterwards minister of the Tigurine Church, both at the Abbey church and at the Carolinum, having previously succeeded Zwingli the younger in the Holy Spirit church. He died in the year of Christ 1613. He had been designated chief minister in 1584 for that office. He wrote a very brief, methodical institution of the Christian religion, reduced to four chapters, in German, 1583. An epigram on the paraphrase of the Psalter by Rudolf Leemann. I have his unpublished writings, both apologetic ones against the virulent writing of Philip Nicolai, and historical ones, various judgments of ancient authors on Antichrist.

units.la: Leemannus, Ioh. Rodolphus, Tigurinus, Imbriacensis Ecclesiae Minister simulque poëta (cui faciles fluebant Camoenae) sanctus & ingeniosus. Scripsit tria epitaphia in obitum D. Bullingeri. Impressa Tiguri cum narratione Ioh. Simleri de vita & obitu ejusdem, anno 1575. in 4. Carmen item, in obitum Iosiae Simleri excusum, Tiguri in 4. anno D. 1577. cum vita ejusdem à D. Stuckio descripta. Querelam in praematuram mortem Rodolphi Gualtheri F. ad R. Gualtherum P. editam ibid. omnium Psalmorum Davidis paraphrasin poeticam, perpetuis hendecasyllabis suavissimis reddidit. Epigramma venustissimum praefixit augmento Bibliothecae Alphabeticae, à Ioan. Iacobo Frisio, edito an. 1583.
units.tr: Leemann, Johann Rudolf, of Zurich, minister of the church at Immensee and at the same time a poet (to whom the Muses came easily), holy and gifted. He wrote three epitaphs on the death of Dr Bullinger, printed at Zurich with a narrative by Johann Simler on his life and death, in quarto, in 1575. Likewise a poem on the death of Josias Simler, printed at Zurich in quarto in the year 1577, with the life of the same described by Dr Stucki. A lament on the untimely death of Rudolf Gwalther the son, addressed to R. Gwalther the father, was published there too. He rendered the whole paraphrase of the Psalms of David into poetry, in most sweet, continuous hendecasyllables. He prefixed a most charming epigram to the enlarged Alphabetical Library of Johann Jakob Frisius, published in 1583.

units.la: Leuu, Iohannis Tigurini libri duo de peste Germanicè manuscripti extabant apud Casparum VVolphium Medicum.
units.tr: Leuu, Johannes of Zurich: two books on the plague in German remained in manuscript with Caspar Wolf, physician.

units.la: Malleolus, Felix, Civis, Cantor & Canonicus Tigurinus: Claruit a. Chr. 1454. Vir, pro ratione aetatis illius, satis eruditus, Magnatum gratiâ florens, apertus, & παρρησιαστής. Extat operum quorundam ejus editorum Catalogus in Bibliotheca Gessneriana; sed multò perfectior est, qui in antiquo pergameno, ipsa nisi vehementer fallar, Malleoli manu, exaratus ita habet: At ego Felix Hemmerli (patricia Tigurinorum, eáque antiqua satis familia fuit, jam enim 1342. Vlricus Hemmerli Tribunus plebis reperitur) Praepositus Solodurensis, & Cantor Thuricensis Ecclesiarum, Decretorum, de Matris almae studiorum gremio Bononiensis Doctor minimus; & in dignitatis officio successor licet inutilissimus, Excellentis, multumque venerabilis, & periti viri, Magistri Conradi de Mure, primi hujus Thuricensis Ecclesiae Cantoris, qui floruit tempore Generosi Comitis, Rodolfi de Habspurg, in Regem Romanorum, de anno Domini 1263. ultima Septembris concorditer electi. Et licet ego felix non sim dignus, ut solvam corrigiam calceamentorum prædicti Domini Cantoris, qui obyt anno Domini 1281. III. Cal. Aprilis. sepultus in Capella Beatissimae Virginis sitae juxta ambitum jam dictae Ecclesiae Thuricensis, & inibi lapide pide suorum eleganter elevato ad Altaris sinistram majoris: Qui tot, prout hic in principio & fine præsenti Codicis compendio patet, gloriosa complevit librorum volumina, per me quandoq; solerter ruminata. Sed quòd post ipsum primum Cantorem nō experior in nostro Collegio fuisse Prælatum Canonicum, aut Clericum, qui confecerit librorum aliquod opusculum, denominatione famatum, nisi quantum tantillus ego excoxi; sed non quasi argentum electum, de camino paupertatis, Jef. 41. per Augustissimorum quoque Principum Divorum Sigismundi I. & Friderici III. Romanorum Regum & Imperatorum tempora, exiliter, exiguáque dictavi quædam collationum condimenta, inferius specialiter, ea intentionis motione, qua ipse Dominus Cantor primus movebatur, & nominatim designata, ad omnipotentis Dei, sanctorúmque nostrorum, Felicis & Regulæ, totiúsque Curiæ cælestis laudem gloriam & honorem. Fluxerunt autem 179. ab Electionis tempore prædicti Rudolfi, qui fuit Pater & propago Illustrissimæ domus modernæ Ducum Austriæ, usque ad jam dicti Friderici, ejusdem domus Alumni, Coronationem, Romæ per Nicolaum Papam V. de anno Domini 1452. Dominica, in medio quadragesimæ celebratam gloriosissimè: suáque sibi pro tunc uxore matrimonialiter, per eundem solennissimè conjuncta, quæ fuit Regis Portugaliæ filia, corpore speciosissima. Et ego pro tunc Felix fueram Canonicus Thuricensis 40. Præpositus Solodurensis 31. Et Doctor 26, Cantor Thuricensis 24. annorum, & ætatis 63. permissione miseratonis divinæ, competenter compos mentis, nec non corpore constitutus. Est autem principalior de meis libris unus de nobilitate, ad Gloriosissimum Principem Albertum, Ducem Austriæ, per 34. Capitula copiosè distincta.
units.tr: Malleolus, Felix, citizen, cantor and canon of Zurich, flourished in the year of Christ 1454. For the standard of his age he was a man of considerable learning, prosperous through the favour of great men, frank, and a parrhesiastes [παρρησιαστής]. A catalogue of some of his published works is in the Gessner library, but a much more complete one, written on old parchment in what I am fairly sure is Malleolus's own hand, reads as follows: But I, Felix Hemmerli (a patrician family of Zurich, and a fairly ancient one, since Ulrich Hemmerli is already found as tribune of the plebs in 1342), provost of Solothurn and cantor of the churches of Zurich, the very least doctor of decretals from the bosom of the nurturing mother of studies at Bologna, and, though most useless, successor in the office of that excellent, much venerated and skilled man, Master Conrad of Mure, first cantor of this church of Zurich, who flourished in the time of the noble Count Rudolf of Habsburg, elected by common consent as King of the Romans on the last day of September in the year of the Lord 1263. And although I, Felix, am not worthy to loosen the thong of the shoes of the aforesaid lord cantor, who died in the year of the Lord 1281 on the third day before the Kalends of April, and was buried in the chapel of the Most Blessed Virgin, situated near the cloister of the aforesaid church of Zurich, and there, with a stone elegantly raised at the left of the high altar of the greater church... He, as is clear here at the beginning and end of the present summary of the codex, completed a glorious number of volumes, which I have at times diligently chewed over. But I do not find that after this first cantor there was in our college any provost, canon or cleric who composed some little work famous by name, except as much as I, so small a man, have refined; yet not as chosen silver from the furnace of poverty (Jef. 41). Through the times of the most august princes, the divine Sigismund I and Frederick III, Kings and Emperors of the Romans, I have dictated, meagrely and in small measure, certain seasonings of collations, specified below, with the same intention that moved the lord cantor himself, and designated by name, to the praise, glory and honour of almighty God, of our saints Felix and Regula, and of the whole heavenly court. Then 179 years passed from the election of the aforesaid Rudolf, who was the father and offspring of the most illustrious present house of the Dukes of Austria, until the coronation of the aforesaid Frederick, a nursling of the same house, celebrated most gloriously at Rome by Pope Nicholas V in the year of the Lord 1452, on a Sunday in the middle of Lent; and his wife, who was then joined to him in matrimony by the same pope most solemnly, the daughter of the King of Portugal, most beautiful in body. And at that time I, Felix, had been a canon of Zurich for 40 years, provost of Solothurn for 31, doctor for 26, and cantor of Zurich for 24, and I was 63 years of age, by the permission of divine mercy competent in mind and likewise in body. The chief of my books is one on nobility, addressed to the most glorious prince Albert, Duke of Austria, copiously divided into 34 chapters.

units.la: 2. Item processus judiciarius coram omnipotenti Deo habitus inter Nobiles & Suitenses rusticos, vivos & defunctos, ad modernum Fridericum III. 3. Largum utriusque juris repertorium. 4. Contra validos mendicantes, videl. Beghardos &c. Collectio compendiosa. 5. Recapitulatio contra eosdem. 6. Contra Anachoritas, i.e. Beghardos Silvestres. 7. Glossa cujusdam bullæ per eosdem impetratæ.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, a judicial process held before almighty God between noble and rustic Swiss, living and dead, addressed to the present Frederick III. 3. A broad repertory of both laws. 4. Against strong beggars, namely the Beghards etc., a concise collection. 5. A recapitulation against the same. 6. Against the Anchorites, that is, the Silvestrine Beghards. 7. A gloss on a certain bull obtained by the same.

units.la: §. Epistola de cœlis missa, contra negligentes cultum divinum & juratum 9. Tractatulus contra iniquos judices, Prælato meo causam inculcante. 10. Iniquè suppressorum consolatio. 11. De novis officijs & beneficijs, & diebus festivis non instituendis collatio. 12. De negotio Monachorum, ad requisitionem D. Abbatis de Mulbrun, tractatulus compilatus. 13. Doctoratus in stultitia. 14. Tractatulus de contractibus qui vulgariter Gysel dicuntur, & Latinè obstagium, 15. De Exorcismis & Adjurationibus. 16. De aurâ & tempestatum benedictionibus. 17. De Assisinis, in mortem Principis tendentibus & machinantibus. 18. De furto miraculoso, de reliquijs, in loco Heremitarum beatissimæ Virginis perpetrato. 19. De arbore torculari, in die Festo de loco ad locum transferendo. 20. De anno jubilæo & Indulgentijs ejus. 21. Recapitulatio super illo. 22. De oblatis & solutis pecunijs, pro prabenda & beneficio in Ecclesijs & Monasterijs obtinendo. 23. De balneis naturalibus hic & alibi constitutis. 24. De libertate Ecclesiastica ad requisitionem Domini Vicarij Constantiensis tractatus largiter compositus. 25. Appellatio generalis contra Cardinales, beneficia in Germania petentes. 26. De aëris distemperatione, propter quorundam hominum cadavera non ritè sepulta proveniente. 27. De plebanis & religiosis mendicantibus, in prædicationis opera & Confessione discrepantibus. 28. Contra quendam superbum Clericum Epistola Curialis. Extant præterea ejusdem Pasionale, de matrimonio seu sponsalibus: Pasionale Virginum nobilium nondum nuptarum cum mundo degentium. Tractatus de misericordia, captivis & defunctis impendenda. De religiosis proprietarijs: Lamentatio duorum Sacerdotum captivorum: Regiftrum querelæ; de emptione & venditione unius pro 20. quos posteriores in captivitate composuit, ἀνέκδοτα pleraque, & inter monumenta mea Helvetica asservata. Multa sæpe eximia habet, quæ ex inficeti illius seculi sordibus eruta, rem literariam non uno modo juvant. Inter Canonistas non obscuri nominis author est: nomen tamen ejus frequentius, quàm libros citare solent eruditi. Caspar Hedion in Appendice Chronicorum Abbatis Vrspergensis citat librum de Nobilitate ad Albertum Ducem Austriæ; de Balneis naturalibus Beatus Rhenanus, & Gesnerus, lib. de thermis. Priorem ego nunquam vidi, nec, etsi serio inquisiverim, investigare potui; habeo tamen fragmenta quædam & excerpta ex illo. Celeb. Rivet. Cathol. Orthod, Tract. 3. pag. 20. pag. 179. Tractat 1. de Exorcismis citat, lepidàmque castrationis porcorum narrationem ex eo subijcit. Bonus vester exorcista, Felix Malleolus, nos docet, quòd illi, qui equos aut asinos, aut porcos castrant, id est, testiculos enervant, in nomine Domini, invocant S. Antonium, ut suo praesidio praestet sanctus animalibus sanitatis auxilium: Item sape videtur compertum, quòd illi, qui offendunt porcos S. Antonij donatione fideliter applicatos, fore punitos. Item videmus, ejusmodi porcos campanella signatos, in domus priores nunquam revertentes. Plura de hoc Malleolo, forte non ingrata, commemorari a nobis possent: Quia vero Indicem tantum scribimus librorum, non vero Historiam, brevitatis habenda est ratio. Illud sibi tribuit, quòd inter Clericos singulares, Constantiensis Dioecesfeos, Bibliothecam tum habuerit instructissimam. Ita enim in suo Passionali: Sciat pietatis tua curialitas, quod inter Clericos singulares Dioecesfeos Constantienfis pro nunc non est copiosior libris, licet fortasse aliquis habeat volumina pretij cariores: Nam mihi sunt, praeter praedictos (tum suos, tum Conradi de Mare) libellos, ultra 500. libri, libelli, tractatuli, vel volumina notabiliter registrata, & in studiorio meo regulariter tabulata: Et super hoc ad copiosum numerum, hinc inde ab Ecclesijs & Monasterijs antiquissimi libri liberaliter accommodati: & omnes isti super ingenij modulum, de diversis scientiarum & Artium & disciplinarum facultatibus abundanter referti. Tandem hic Malleolus ab Episcopo Constantiensi in carcerem fuit compactus, deinde captivitate (quae initium sumpsit an. Chr. 1454. die Mercurii, mens. Feb.) ejusque causis prolixè agit in Registro querelae, quae, alia occasione, curioso lectori non invidebimus.
units.tr: §. Letter sent from the heavens, against those who neglect the divine and sworn worship. 9. A little treatise against unjust judges, my provost urging the case. 10. Consolation of those unjustly suppressed. 11. A collation on new offices and benefices, and on festival days not to be instituted. 12. A treatise compiled on the affair of the Monks, at the request of the Lord Abbot of Maulbronn. 13. Doctorate in foolishness. 14. A little treatise on contracts which are commonly called Gysel, and in Latin obstagium. 15. On Exorcisms and Adjurations. 16. On the blessings of the air and of storms. 17. On the Assassins, who aim and plot at the death of a prince. 18. On a miraculous theft of relics, committed in the hermitage of the Most Blessed Virgin. 19. On the wine-press tree, to be moved from place to place on a festival day. 20. On the Jubilee year and its indulgences. 21. A recapitulation on that. 22. On money offered and paid in order to obtain a prebend and benefice in churches and monasteries. 23. On the natural baths situated here and elsewhere. 24. On ecclesiastical liberty, a treatise composed at length at the request of the Lord Vicar of Constance. 25. A general appeal against cardinals seeking benefices in Germany. 26. On the disturbance of the air arising from the corpses of certain men not buried in the proper way. 27. On parish priests and mendicant religious who disagree in the work of preaching and in confession. 28. A letter of a curialist against a certain proud cleric. Besides these, the same author's Pasionale, on marriage or betrothals; Pasionale of noble virgins not yet married, living in the world; a treatise on mercy to be bestowed on captives and the dead; on religious who hold property; a lamentation of two captive priests; a register of complaint; on the buying and selling of one for twenty, which he composed later in captivity; most of them unpublished [ἀνέκδοτα], and preserved among my Swiss monuments. He often has many outstanding things, which, dug out from the filth of that unpolished age, help literary matters in more than one way. Among the canonists he is an author of no obscure name; yet his name is cited more often than his books are cited by scholars. Caspar Hedio, in the appendix to the Chronicle of the Abbot of Ursperg, cites his book on nobility addressed to Duke Albert of Austria; Beatus Rhenanus and Gesner, in their book on thermal waters, cite the one on natural baths. I have never seen the former, nor, though I have seriously searched, have I been able to find it; yet I have certain fragments and excerpts from it. The celebrated Rivet, in his Catholic Orthodox, tract 3, pp. 20 and 179, cites Tract 1 on Exorcisms, and adds from it the witty story of the castration of pigs: Your good exorcist, Felix Malleolus, teaches us that those who castrate horses or asses or pigs, that is, weaken their testicles, invoke in the name of the Lord St. Anthony, so that the saint may by his protection grant the help of health to the animals. Likewise it is often seen to have been ascertained that those who harm pigs faithfully dedicated to St. Anthony by donation will be punished. Likewise we see such pigs marked with little bells never returning to their former homes. Many more things about this Malleolus, perhaps not unwelcome, could be recalled by us; but since we are writing only an index of books and not a history, regard must be had for brevity. He claimed for himself that among the outstanding clerics of the diocese of Constance he had then the best-stocked library. For thus he writes in his Passionale: Let your piety's courtesy know that among the outstanding clerics of the diocese of Constance at present there is no richer in books, although perhaps someone has volumes more precious in price; for I have, besides the aforesaid little books (both his own and those of Conrad of Mure), more than 500 books, booklets, treatises, or volumes, notably registered and regularly shelved in my study; and in addition to this a considerable number of very old books have been lent to me freely from here and there by churches and monasteries; and all these, beyond the measure of my ability, are abundantly filled with the various faculties of the sciences, arts and disciplines. Finally, this Malleolus was thrown into prison by the Bishop of Constance, and then into captivity (which began in the year of Christ 1454, on a Wednesday, in the month of February); and he treats its causes at length in the Register of complaint, which, on another occasion, we shall not begrudge the curious reader.

units.la: Mangoltus Gregorius, Tigurinus scripsit librum de piscibus, qui in lacu Acronio inprimis, aliisque lacubus & fluvijs capiuntur, Tiguri apud Gesnerōs: Annales, urbis Constantiensis; Descriptionem oppugnatae ab Hispanis urbis Germanicam, Chronologiam ab initio Mundi, quae MS. omnia sunt.
units.tr: Mangoltus Gregorius, of Zurich, wrote a book on the fish caught especially in Lake Constance and in other lakes and rivers, printed at Zurich by the Gessners. He also wrote the Annals of the city of Constance, a description of the German city besieged by the Spaniards, and a chronology from the beginning of the world. All of these are in manuscript.

units.la: Mantzius Iohannes, V.I.D. Canonicus & Collegij Carolini Praepositus, ab an. Chr. 1495. ad 1519. Nihil quidem, quod sciam, edere voluit, typis, quo rem literariam promoveret: adeo tamen multa & varia sub ipsius nomine extant documenta, citationum, concessionum, dispensationum, ordinationum, specialium delegationum, &c. ut dignus mihi visus fuerit, qui huic Catalogo inseretur.
units.tr: Mantzius Iohannes, Doctor of Both Laws, canon and provost of the Carolinum college, lived from 1495 to 1519. As far as I know, he never wished to publish anything in print to advance learning. Nevertheless, many and varied documents survive under his name: citations, grants, dispensations, ordinances, special commissions, and so on. For that reason he seemed to me worthy of a place in this catalogue.

units.la: Martyr Petrus Vermilius, Florentinus, sacras literas magna cum laude Argentorati docuit & Oxonij in Anglia, & postremo Tiguri. Scripsit plurima, e quibus hæc ab ipso edita sunt. Catechismus, sive symboli expositio, Italicè: libellus impressus apud Oporinum. Commentarij doctissimi in Epistolam primam D. Pauli ad Corinthios, excusi Tiguri à Froschouero, anno Domini 1551. in quarta forma, & in sol. Commentarij in librum Iudicum, ab eodem excusi in sol. & in 8. Defensio doctrinæ veteris & Apostolicæ de sacrosancto Eucharistiæ Sacramento, adversus Stephani Gardineri librum, quem ille primùm sub nomine Antonij Constantij, deinde proprio suo ipsius nomine appositò evulgavit: opus longè accuratissimum, in quo quicquid de Eucharistia, in sacris literis, Patrum Conciliorumque monumentis proditum est, accuratè & copiosè tractatur. Tiguri excus. anno Domini 1559 in sol. Disputatio de Eucharistiæ Sacramento, habita in celeberrima universitate Oxoniensi, de eadem retractatio, ibidem habita. Hi duo libri primùm in Anglica excusi sunt, & postea apud Andream Gessnerum, & Rodolphum VVyflenbach, An. D. 1552. in 8. & postremo à Froschouero, unà cum defensione doctrinæ de Eucharistia, &c. in sol. Defensio ad Richardi Smythæi Angli, olim Theologiæ Professoris Oxoniensis, duos libellos, de cælibatu, Sacerdotum, & votis monasticis, Basileæ apud Pet. Pernam, anno 1559. in 8. Porrò post obitum ipsius sequentes libri editi sunt, Commentarij in duos libros Samuelis, Tiguri, anno D. 1554 in sol. Commentarij in primum librum Melachim, sive Regum, & posterioris libri undecim prima capita. Ibidem anno 1556. Commentarij in primum librum Mosis. Ibidem. Commentarij in primum & secundum, & tertij libri Ethicorum Nicomachicorum Aristotelis, initium. Ibid in 16. Precum, ex Psalmis, libellus in 4. Epitome Defensionis adversus Stephanum Gardinerum. Confessio de Cœna Domini, exhibita Senatui Argentoratensi. Sententia de præsentia corporis Christi in Eucharistia, propositia in colloquio Poissiaco, Epistola de causa Eucharistiæ, ad virum quendam magni nominis. Hæc simul cum Oratione Simleri de vita Martyris impressa sunt anno 1561. in quarto. Ejusdem Loci communes, ex variis ipsius authoris scriptis in unum librum collecti, & in quatuor Classes distributi sunt. Accesserunt huic editioni ab ipso authore P. Martyre scripti, nec antea publicati, Loci, de libero arbitrio, providentia Dei, prædestinatione, & causa peccati. Ad hæc Orationes sive Conciones, nec non quæstiones aliquot & responsa: Epistolæ item partim Theologicæ, quibus varii loci explicantur, partim familiares: cum Præfatione Domini Rodolphi Gualtheri Tigurini, de usu & utilitate Locorum communium & de Concionibus formandis: Indice præterea rerum ac verborum copiosissimo. In sol. Tiguri excudebat Christophorus Froschouerus, anno 1580. Præterea Commentarij ejusdem in Exodum, in Prophetas aliquot minores, Epistolæ item & Orationes, aliàque nonnulla manuscripta, servabantur à Iulio Terentiano. Obijt Tiguri anno 1562. Accesserunt non ita pridem, opera D. Rodolphi Stuckij, Comment. in Threnos & c. Habeo Epistolas ab hac dum ejus aliquot ἀνεκδότως, & judicium Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ ab ipso, in cau sazanchij, conceptum.
units.tr: Martyr Petrus Vermilius, of Florence, taught Holy Scripture with great distinction at Strasbourg, at Oxford in England, and finally at Zurich. He wrote a great deal, of which the following were published by him. Catechismus, or an exposition of the creed, in Italian: a little book printed by Oporinus. Commentarij doctissimi in Epistolam primam D. Pauli ad Corinthios, printed at Zurich by Froschauer in 1551, in quarto and in folio. Commentarij in librum Iudicum, printed by the same in folio and in octavo. Defensio doctrinæ veteris & Apostolicæ de sacrosancto Eucharistiæ Sacramento, against the book of Stephen Gardiner, which he first put out under the name of Antonius Constantius and then openly under his own name: a far more careful work, in which whatever is handed down about the Eucharist in Holy Scripture and in the writings of the Fathers and Councils is treated carefully and fully. Printed at Zurich in folio in 1559. A disputation on the sacrament of the Eucharist, held at the famous university of Oxford, and a revision of it, likewise held there. These two books were first printed in English, and afterwards by Andreas Gessner and Rudolf Wyssenbach in 1552 in octavo, and finally by Froschauer, together with the defence of the doctrine of the Eucharist, in folio. A Defensio against the two little books of Richard Smyth, an Englishman, formerly professor of theology at Oxford, on celibacy, on the priests, and on monastic vows, printed at Basel by Peter Perna in 1559 in octavo. Furthermore, after his death the following books were published: Commentarij on the two books of Samuel, at Zurich in folio in 1554. Commentaries on the first book of Melachim, that is, Kings, and the first eleven chapters of the second book. Printed there in 1556. Commentaries on the first book of Moses, printed there. Commentaries on the first, second and third books of the Nicomachean Ethics of Aristotle, the beginning only, printed there in octavo. A little book of Prayers, drawn from the Psalms, in quarto. An epitome of the Defence against Stephen Gardiner. The confession on the Lord's Supper, presented to the Senate of Strasbourg. The opinion on the presence of the body of Christ in the Eucharist, put forward at the colloquy of Poissy. A letter on the question of the Eucharist, to a certain man of great name. These were printed together with Simler's oration on the life of Martyr in quarto in 1561. His Loci communes, collected from various writings of the same author into one book and divided into four classes, were also published. To this edition were added the Loci written by Peter Martyr himself, which had not been published before, on free will, the providence of God, predestination, and the cause of sin. In addition there are his orations or sermons, as well as some questions and replies; also letters, partly theological, in which various topics are explained, and partly familiar; with a preface by Rudolf Gwalther of Zurich, on the use and benefit of common places and on the making of sermons; and besides, a very full index of things and words. In folio. Printed at Zurich by Christoph Froschauer in 1580. Also his commentaries on Exodus, on some of the minor Prophets, letters, orations, and some other unpublished writings were kept by Julius Terentianus. He died at Zurich in 1562. Not long ago there were added, through the work of Rudolf Stuck, commentaries on the Lamentations, etc. I have letters from him, some of them unpublished, and the judgement of the Church of Zurich composed by him concerning the Canzanchi affair.

units.la: Megander (Germ. Grat s anus) Caspar, Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ & Bernensis Minister, ab initio statim Reformationis, scripsit Commentaria in Epistolam Pauli ad Galatas, Tiguri 1553. Ad Ephesios, Basil. apud Henricum Petri, a D. 1534. In Epistolas tres ad Timotheum & Titum, Basil 1536. Collegit etiam farraginem annotationum in Genesin ex ore Zuinglij, impress. Tiguri 1527. Item in Exodum ex ore ejusdem, Tiguri eodem anno. In Epistolam ad Hebræos, & priorem Iohannis Canonicam, Tiguri 1539. Et denuò 1581. cum annotationibus in Evangelia, & aliquot Pauli Epistolas. Scripsit etiam Catechismum in gratiam juventutis Bernensis, & Commentaria in Acta Apostolorum. Obiit Tiguri 1545. Archidiaconus.
units.tr: Megander (in German, Grat s anus), Caspar, minister of the Church of Zurich and of Bern, from the very beginning of the Reformation, wrote commentaries on Paul's Epistle to the Galatians, printed at Zurich in 1553; on the Ephesians, at Basel by Henry Petri, in 1534; on the three Epistles to Timothy and Titus, at Basel in 1536. He also gathered a collection of annotations on Genesis from the lectures of Zwingli, printed at Zurich in 1527, and likewise on Exodus from the same source, at Zurich in the same year. On the Epistle to the Hebrews and the First Epistle of John, at Zurich in 1539, and again in 1581, with annotations on the Gospels and some of Paul's Epistles. He also wrote a catechism for the youth of Bern, and commentaries on the Acts of the Apostles. He died at Zurich in 1545, as archdeacon.

units.la: Murerus Christophorus, vir ordinis Politici, Mathematum tamen & Poëseos studiosus, edidit Comœdiam de Scipione Africano, Germanic. ut Iosua Murerus aliam de Esthera.
units.tr: Murer, Christoph, a man of the civil service but devoted to mathematics and poetry, published a comedy on Scipio Africanus in German, as Josua Murer did another on Esther.

units.la: Murerus, Iohannes Iacobus, Pastor Lithopolitanus ad an. Chr. 1595. dedit Epilogismum trium Eclipseon solaris 1. & 11. Lunarium Anno MDVC. futurarum, typis illustratum, Tiguri 1595.
units.tr: Murer, Johann Jakob, minister at Lithopolis, in the year of Christ 1595 published an epilogism on three eclipses, one solar and two lunar, to occur in the year 1605, illustrated with printed diagrams, at Zurich in 1595.

units.la: De Mure, Conradus, Canonicus, primúsque Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Cantor, floruit an. D. 1273. Obiit 1281. 3. Calend. April. De quo plura in vita Felicis Malleoli, & originib. Schol. Carolin. Scripsit Fabularium, id est, de diversis Poëtarum Fabulis, qui liber adhuc, Petri Numagen Trevirensis, Sacellani Tigurini, manu, an. Chr. 1502. descriptus, in Bibliotheca Carolina asservatur. Descopo, & studio juvandi Studiosos, ipsum in præfatione audire placet Conradum de Mure. Ita autem habet: In nomine Domini Amen. Incipit Fabularium à Magistro Conrado, Cantore Ecclesiæ Thuricensis Præpositura Constantiensis Diœceseos, secundum ordinem Alphabethi, cum aliquali diligentia compilatus, & tandem completus an. D. 1273. in vigilia assumtionis Beatæ Mariæ Virginis. Cùm in Ovidianis & metricis aliorum Poëtarum figmentis, non solùm quædam propriorum nominum diversa raritas, rara diversitas & varietas patronymicorum seu nominum habentium formam eorundem, verùm etiam actiones seu operationes ipsis propriis nominibus & vocabulis attributa parvulis studentibus difficilem perplexitatem, perplexam difficultatem multoties generent & inducant; Ego Magister Conradus, Canonicus Thuricensis, dictus de Mure, nec valens, nec volens ignavia inertis otij torpere; sed communi parvulorum utilitati cupiens deservire, post labores novi Græcis in per ejusdem correctionem à me habitos, post libellum de naturis animalium metricè compositum, post sudores libelli de septem Sacramentis, ad instantem quorundam sodalium meorum petitionem, antiquo iterum lado inclusus (videtur ergo in gratiam studiosæ tum juventutis, cui præerat, scriptum illud adornâsse, antequam ordinarius in Collegio Carolino erat Scholasticus) Fabularium simplicem, & cui de integumento vel expositione Fabularum nihil sit additum, propter parvulos, & annexum proposui compilandum &c. Meminit hujus scripti Felix Malleolus, in suo Pasionali: Sic similiter eximius Poeta Laureatus, videlicet M. Conradus de Mure, Cantor Ecclesiæ nostræ Thuricensis, primus in Capella Beatissimæ Virginis ibidem ad sinistram majoris altaris sepultus, cujus Epitaphij cultus his diebus per me fuit renovatus, & ibidem in pariete conscriptus de anno D. 1281. Cal 3. April. Hic multum gloriosa matrice composuit volumina, quorum omnium per ordinem numerum & nomina conscripsit, & in principio & in fine libri sui, qui dicitur Fabularius, qui solus inter sua volumina fuit prosaicus, & magnæ subtilitatis decore redimitus, & fuit duodecimus. Initio autem libri compendium exhibet Historiæ V. T. profanum, collatum cum Synchronismo Biblico. Subjicit deinde origines Idololatriæ Gentilis, Idolorum nomina, carmine, ut non male Theogonia metrica appellari posset. Tum demum accedit ad Fabularium Alphabethicum, sive Lexicon eorum nominum propriorum, quæ apud Poetas potissimum occurrunt. Prolixus satis est, non tam in explicandis Etymologijs, quàm in enarrandis rebus gestis. In Ecclesiasticis, quæ rarius adspergit, Apocrypha nonnunquam admiscuit. Videamus Methodi, quam observat, unum & alterum exemplum. Primum sit petitum ex Nomenclatura Ecclesiastica in voce Pilatus. Pilatus, inquit, cognomine Pontius à Ponto Insula, sicut quidam liber Ovidij dicitur de Ponto, quia ipsum Ovidius composuit in Ponto Insula, relegatus. Quædam tamen hic Apocrypha, quædam Historica comprobantur. Quidam Rex Moguntiæ Athus nomine, peritus Astronomiæ, quadam die ex venatione cum suis in sero ad hospitium villani cujusdam declinavit, ubi, dum inspectis sideribus ad suos dixisset: Mulier, quæ in nocte mecum dormiverit, & concubuerit, pariet filium magni nominis: Unde cùm reginam uxorem non posset habere, de consilio Sociorum, filium hospitis nomine Pilam, sibi fornicariè appositam cognoscens impraegnavit. Hæc Pila pariens filium, qui nomine composito ex matre Pila, & patre Atho, Pilatus nominatur. Hunc Rex cum reliquis in aula mandat nutriri, qui factus adolescens, filium Regis Athi, suum scilicet fornicariè fratrem, occidit; quo maleficio, seu fratricidio comperto Pilatus Romam in obstagium exilio deputatur, ubi filium Regis Anglorum etiam obsidem satis nequiter jugulavit. Unde à Cæsare in Pontum Insulam, ubi sunt crudeles homines, & inhumani, pro Præfecto & Procuratore mittitur, ut ibidem per crudeles incolas deperiret: Sed quia illic multa strenuè gessit, Herodes, Præfectus Judææ, audita strenuitate, vocat & assumit eum, in regni consortium & laboris, quoquo, Regi Herodi incipit contrarius esse, immemor beneficiorum exhibitorum; & à Tiberio, Cæsare Augusto, & Romanis mittitur Judææ Procurator. Unde dissensio inter Herodem oritur & Pilatum: Tamen hæc dissensio secundum Scholasticam Historiam orta fuit ex eo, quòd Pilatus quosdam Galilæos occiderat, qui erant de Herodis dominio, & districtu, & hæc dissensio in morte Jesu sopitur, sub isto Pilato Præside, qui sicut pramissum est, creditur fuisse natione Teutonicus, Judæi Jesum Christum decreverunt crucifigendum. Sed post Domini mortem Vespasianus & filius suus Titus imperium habent, Vespasianus in Occidente, Titus in Oriente; neuter tamen corpore sanus. Nam Titus leprosus; nasus quoque Vespasiani plenus erat Vespis, studiòque frequenter inani vexârant medicos. Isti mittunt ad Pilatum, ut eis mittat Jesum, de quo fama fuit, quod diversos indifferenter curaret languores; quo audito nuncios mittit ad Cæsares cum muneribus, qui, vento contrario in Hispanos portus pulsi, veniunt ad Vespasianum ibidem, & ei indicant de morte Jesu. Vespasianus verò dum per nasum jurâssset, se mortem Jesu vindicaturum, statim à nasi languore liberatur: Igitur, de consilio filij Titi, Jerusalem mittuntur nuncij ad Pilatum, quid morte Christi vel vita perquirant, quibus quadam die in urbe deambulantibus & spatiantibus mulier.
units.tr: De Mure, Conrad, canon and the first cantor of the Church of Zurich, flourished in the year of the Lord 1273. He died in 1281, on the third day before the Kalends of April. More about him may be found in the life of Felix Malleolus and in the origins of the Carolinum school. He wrote a Fabularium, that is, a book on the various fables of the poets. This book, copied out in 1502 by Peter Numagen of Trier, chaplain at Zurich, is still preserved in the Carolinum library. It is worth hearing Conrad de Mure himself in the preface, on the purpose and aim of helping students. It reads as follows: In the name of the Lord, Amen. Here begins the Fabularium by Master Conrad, cantor of the Church of Zurich in the diocese of Constance, compiled with some care in alphabetical order, and finished in the year of the Lord 1273, on the eve of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Since in the Ovidian and metrical fictions of other poets, not only the diverse rarity of certain proper names and the variety of derivative names having the same form, but also the actions or operations attributed to those proper names and words, often create and bring about a difficult perplexity for little students; I, Master Conrad, canon of Zurich, called de Mure, neither able nor willing to grow torpid in the sloth of idle leisure, but desiring to serve the common benefit of the little ones, after my labours on the Greek ..., after my labours on the correction of the same, after the little book on the natures of animals composed in verse, after the sweat of the little book on the seven Sacraments, at the urging of some of my comrades, enclosed once more in an old ... (it seems, then, that he prepared that work for the benefit of the studious youth over whom he presided, before he was ordinary schoolmaster at the Carolinum college). I have proposed to compile a simple Fabularium, to which nothing has been added about the allegorical covering or explanation of the fables, for the sake of the little ones, and annexed &c. Felix Malleolus mentions this work in his Pasionalis: Likewise the distinguished laureate poet, namely Master Conrad de Mure, cantor of our Church of Zurich, was buried first in the chapel of the Most Blessed Virgin there, to the left of the high altar; his epitaph, which I have renewed these days, was written on the wall there with the date of the Lord 1281, the third day before the Kalends of April. He composed many volumes of great learning, the whole number and titles of which he listed in order at the beginning and end of his book called the Fabularius, which alone among his volumes was in prose, adorned with the grace of great subtlety, and it was his twelfth. At the beginning of the book he gives a compendium of the history of the Old Testament, profane, compared with the biblical synchronism. He then sets out the origins of heathen idolatry and the names of the idols, in verse, so that it might not badly be called a metrical Theogony. Then at last he comes to the alphabetical Fabularium, or lexicon of those proper names that occur chiefly in the poets. It is rather long, not so much in explaining etymologies as in narrating deeds. In ecclesiastical matters, which he touches on rarely, he has sometimes mixed in apocryphal material. Let us look at one or two examples of his method. The first is taken from the ecclesiastical nomenclature under the word Pilatus. Pilate, he says, with the surname Pontius, from the island of Pontus, just as a certain book of Ovid is called On the Pontus, because Ovid composed it while exiled on the island of Pontus. Some things here are proved apocryphal, some historical. A certain king of Mainz named Athus, skilled in astronomy, one day coming back from the hunt with his men in the evening, turned aside to the lodging of a certain farmer, where, after looking at the stars, he said to his men: "The woman who sleeps with me tonight and lies with me will bear a son of great name." Since he could not have his queen as wife, on the advice of his companions he got with child the host's son's wife, Pila, whom he knew by fornication. This Pila, bearing a son, who by a compound name from the mother Pila and the father Athus is called Pilatus. The king orders him to be raised in the court with the rest; when he grew up he killed the son of King Athus, his own half-brother by fornication. When this crime, or fratricide, was discovered, Pilate was sent to Rome to be held as a hostage in exile, where he wickedly slew the son of the King of the English, also a hostage. Therefore Caesar sent him to the island of Pontus, where there are cruel and inhuman men, as prefect and procurator, so that he might perish there at the hands of the cruel inhabitants. But because he there acted with much vigour, Herod, prefect of Judea, having heard of his vigour, summoned and took him into partnership in the kingdom and the labour; but he began to be hostile to King Herod, forgetful of the benefits shown him; and he was sent by Tiberius Caesar Augustus and the Romans as procurator of Judea. Hence a quarrel arose between Herod and Pilate. Yet this quarrel, according to the scholastic history, arose because Pilate had killed certain Galileans who were under the rule and jurisdiction of Herod; and this quarrel was settled at the death of Jesus, under this Pilate as governor, who, as has been said, is believed to have been a German by birth, when the Jews decided to crucify Jesus Christ. But after the Lord's death Vespasian and his son Titus held the empire, Vespasian in the West, Titus in the East; yet neither was sound in body. For Titus was a leper, and Vespasian's nose was full of wasps, and they had often tormented doctors with useless study. They send to Pilate, asking him to send them Jesus, of whom the rumour was that he healed diverse diseases without distinction; on hearing this he sends messengers to the Caesars with gifts, who, driven by contrary winds to the ports of Spain, come to Vespasian there and tell him of the death of Jesus. Vespasian, however, having sworn by his nose that he would avenge the death of Jesus, was at once freed from the disease of his nose. Therefore, on the advice of Titus's son, messengers are sent to Pilate at Jerusalem to ask what they might gain from the death or life of Christ; as they walked and strolled one day in the city, a woman.

units.la: U mulier, nomine Veronica, de morte Jesu indicat, & imaginem Jesu sudario impressam, quam ipsi mulieri Jesus dederat, assumunt, & cum ejusdem nuntijs Romam festinat, ubi Titus, inspecta imagine Jesu à lepra mundatur. Vespasianus etiam superveniens de consilio Titi citant Pilatum, qui audita citatione, conscius criminis, se ipsum jugulat cultello, cujus cadaver in Rodanum prope Viennam precipitatur, & in eodem precipitationis loco Rodanus efficitur nautis valde periculosus: unde Viennenses novitate mali stupefacti, Lugdunum veniunt, causam perquirere facti, unde cadaver Pilati in profundo Rodani inventum & extractum transmittunt in alpes prope montem septimum (mons est Rhæticus, de quo Tschudius, in descript. Alp. Rhætic. ut mirer Conradum de Mure, Lucernensium vicinum, montis Pilati, prope Lucernam, non meminisse: Forte superstitio, quæ paulatim postea radices egit, de eo nondum in valuit, publicè nuper profligata à cujato Lucernensi, in descriptione lacus Civitatum Sylvestrium) ubi adhuc ejusdem Pilati memoria horribilis & terribilis memoratur. Nam sicut dicitur, Pilato nominato seu vocato, magna fit ibi concussio, cum horrore strepitus & tumultus. Alterum exemplum sit ex Historia profana, de Merlino Anglorum vate. Merlinus, secundum Britannicam Historiam taliter nascitur. Tempore Vortegirni, Regis Britonum, filia Regis urbis Demeciæ, in Ecclesia Sancti Petri, in eadem urbe, inter Monachas degens, per quoddam Daemonium, de genere incuborum corrupta & impregnata genuit Merlinum, qui summè ingeniosus, Magus & Vates, multa de futuris, modo per ambages, modo certis verbis prædicebat. Isto Vortegirno, secundum Prophetiam Merlini, in turri conclusò & combusto, Pascentius filius Vortegirni, per quendam, nomine Copam, in habitu Monachi, & specie Medici, & pro Confessione Medici procuravit Regem Aurelium toxicari. Sed frater Aurelij Uterpendragon, quod Lingua Britannica sonat caput Draconis, in Regem sublimatus Hirgirnam uxorem Gorlois Ducis Cornubiæ tam vehementer amavit, quod fere extabuit. Tandem Merlinus per artes Magicas ipsum Uterpendragon in speciem mutavit Gorloys, Ulfin vero familiarem ejus in quendam, nomine Jordanum, se ipsum vero etiam transmutavit, & sic Uterpendragon in specie mariti cognovit Hirgirnam & impregnavit. Et eadem nocte concepit illum celeberrimum Arthurum. Itaque dum iste Uterpendragon, bibens de fonte ex industria toxicato, mortuus esset, praedictus filius ejus Arthurus in Regem consecratur. Iste Arthurus inaudita virtutis, hospitalitatis largissima, in beneficijs conferendis quasi alter Titus, summe ingeniosus, strenuissimus bellator, victoriosissimus pugnator, regni sui magnificus dilatator, in convivijs & festivitatibus suae curiae incredibilis Dominus & administrator. Post multa mirifica & incredibilia, post multos Principes & magnates cum suis provincijs & urbibus debellatis, in publico conflictu, multis Regibus, Ducibus, Baronibus, militibus, popularibus, plebejis amissis, lataliter vulneratus diem clausit extremum. Et nota, quod iste Arthurus Christianissimus nostrae fidei exaltator, non est de foro praesentium operum, ubi tantum tangi debent Poetica figmenta; sed ideo fit, ut de Merlino, scil. homine tanti nominis habeatur mentio aliqualis.
units.tr: A woman named Veronica reports the death of Jesus, and they take the image of Jesus impressed on a cloth, which Jesus had given to this woman. Together with the messengers, they hasten to Rome, where Titus, on looking at the image of Jesus, is cleansed of leprosy. Vespasian also arrives, and on Titus's advice they summon Pilate. When Pilate hears the summons, conscious of his crime, he cuts his own throat with a knife. His corpse is thrown into the Rhône near Vienne, and at the place where it was thrown in the Rhône becomes very dangerous for sailors. Therefore the people of Vienne, astonished at this new evil, come to Lyons to inquire into the cause of the event, and from there they send Pilate's corpse, found and drawn out of the deep water of the Rhône, into the Alps near Mount Septimus. (This is a mountain of Rhaetia, concerning which Tschudi, in his description of the Rhaetian Alps, I wonder that Conrad von Mure, a neighbour of the people of Lucerne, does not mention in relation to Mount Pilatus near Lucerne. Perhaps the superstition, which later gradually took root, had not yet prevailed concerning it; it was lately refuted in public by Cysat of Lucerne, in his description of the lake of the Civitates Sylvestres.) Where the memory of this same Pilate is still recalled as dreadful and terrifying. For, as it is said, when Pilate is named or called, a great commotion arises there, with a horrible noise and tumult. A second example is taken from profane history, concerning Merlin, the bard of the English. According to the British History, Merlin was born in the following way. In the time of Vortigern, king of the Britons, the daughter of the king of the city of Demetia, living among the nuns in the church of St Peter in the same city, was corrupted and made pregnant by a certain demon of the kind of incubi, and bore Merlin, who, extraordinarily clever, a magician and a seer, foretold many things about the future, sometimes in riddles, sometimes in plain words. When Vortigern had been shut up in a tower and burned, according to Merlin's prophecy, Pascentius, son of Vortigern, through a certain man named Copa, dressed as a monk and in the guise of a physician, and under pretext of a physician's confession, arranged for King Aurelius to be poisoned. But Aurelius's brother Uther Pendragon, which in the British tongue means the head of the dragon, was raised to the kingship and loved Igerna, wife of Gorlois, Duke of Cornwall, so vehemently that he nearly wasted away. At last Merlin, by magic arts, changed Uther Pendragon into the likeness of Gorlois, and changed Ulfin, his companion, into a certain man named Jordan; and he also transformed himself, and so Uther, in the form of the husband, knew Igerna and made her pregnant. And on that same night she conceived that most famous Arthur. Then, when this Uther, drinking from a spring deliberately poisoned, had died, his aforesaid son Arthur was consecrated king. This Arthur, of unheard-of virtue, most generous in hospitality, in bestowing benefits like another Titus, extremely clever, a most vigorous warrior, a most victorious fighter, a magnificent extender of his kingdom, was an incredible lord and manager in the feasts and celebrations of his court. After many wonderful and incredible deeds, after many princes and magnates had been defeated together with their provinces and cities, in a public battle, with many kings, dukes, barons, knights, commoners and plebeians lost, he was mortally wounded and closed his final day. And note that this Arthur, most Christian exalter of our faith, is not within the scope of the present work, where only poetic fictions ought to be touched; but it happens here that some mention is made of Merlin, a man of such great name.

units.la: Tertium denique exemplum sit vocabulum Philosophia. Philosophia est Secretorum Naturae vera apprehensio. Vel Philosophia est eorum, quae sunt & non videntur: Et eorum quae sunt, & videntur, vera comprehensio, & diversis respectibus subscripta: Subsunt eidem septem liberales artes. Prima Grammatica, puerilis formae, habens in dextera palmarium vel ferulam seu scuticam, id est, flagellum de vibicibus vel de corrigijs compositum. Ovid. Epist.
