In a whole volume of various poems he has amply shown that the German language lacks nothing for the turning of verses. A third edition has lately appeared, greatly enlarged by an appendix.

units.la: Sprunglinus Hartmannus, Ecclesiæ VVilensis in agro Rafzensi, Minister, Capituli Reginoburgici Decanus ad an. Chr. 1614. felix scriptorum Theologicorum interpres. Transtulit Homilias 5. de Cæna Dominica Conradi Vlmeri 1600. Pro ut Lavateri Homiliarum Germanicarum diligens interpres Latinus habetur. Ejusdem est liber belli Papistici de Sacramento extremæ unctionis. Tig. 1613. Hæresium pars 1. & 2. complectens tum indicem verarum & præcipuarum hæresium, quibus in genere ferè totus Papatus infectus est, tum illarum hæresium, quibus Pontifics Romani in specie dedit; sunt, opposita singulis hæresibus Orthodoxa doctrina & fide, Oppenhemij 1617.
units.tr: Sprunglinus Hartmannus, minister of the church of Wil in the Rafz district, dean of the chapter of Regensburg, until the year of Christ 1614, a happy translator of theological writers. He translated five homilies on the Lord's Supper by Konrad Ulmer, 1600, just as he is regarded as the diligent Latin translator of Lavater's German homilies. His is also a book against the Papistical sacrament of extreme unction, Zurich 1613. Parts 1 and 2 of a work on heresies, comprising both an index of the true and principal heresies with which almost the whole papacy is in general infected, and those heresies with which the Roman Pontiffs in particular are tainted; set against each heresy is the orthodox doctrine and faith. Oppenheim, 1617.

units.la: Strubius Henricus, Arithmeticus, Arithmeticam scripsit vernaculam, Tiguri editam 1588.
units.tr: Strubius Henricus, an arithmetician, who wrote an arithmetic in the vernacular, published at Zurich in 1588.

units.la: Stuckius Iohannes Guilelmus, Tigurinus, ex nobili & antiqua Stuckiorum familia natus, Iacobi Ammiani Professoris Rhetoro Logici aliquandiu Parastates, postea Theologiæ Professor ordinarius ab an. Chr. 1571. ad 1607. Comes etiam fuit Petri Martyris ad colloquium Possiacenum, de quo nonnulla habeo ipsius manu ex Gallia Tigurum scripta. Lucubrationibus suis magnum apud eruditos acquisivit nomen. Scripsit autem varia I. Theologica. Habeo ejus commentaria in Zachariam Msc. Orationes duas de munere Ecclesiastico. De Angelis Angelicoque praesidio atque custodia hominum meditatio pia &c. Inserta nonnulla ex Chrysostomi Homiliis manuscriptis. Tig. 1595. Scripsit etiam tractatum Lingua vernacula de Coena Domini. In refutando Huberianimo praeclara & eximia ejus fuit opera, ut postea in Stumpfio nonnulla monebimus. II. Philologica. De Sacris & Sacrificijs Gentilium. Antiquitatum convivialium lib. tres: In quibus Hebraeorum, Graecorum, Romanorum, aliarumque Nationum antiqua conviviorum genera, necnon mores, consuetudines, ritus, Ceremoniaeque conviviales, atque etiam aliae explicantur, & cum ijs, quae hodie cum apud Christianos, tum apud alias gentes a Christiano nomine alienas in usu sunt, conferuntur, multa Grammatica, Physica, Medica, Ethica, Oeconomica, Politica, Philosophica denique atque Historica cognitu jucunda simul & utilia tractantur plurima Sacrorum prophanorum que auctorum veterum loca obscura illustrantur, corrupta emendantur, deniique desperatus deploratusque nostrorum temporum luxus atque luxuria gravi censura damnatur: Tig. 1582. III. philosophica, Geographica, praesertim & Astronomica, ut sunt Scholia in Ariani Historici & Philosophi Ponti Euxini & maris Erythraei periplum, quae luculentam regionum, gentium, insularum, Oppidorum, fluminum, mercium, caeterarumque rerum memorabilium utriusque Peripli descriptionem continent, ex accurata veterum & recentiorum authorum collatione: addita (praeter loca, quae solers Lusitanorum penetravit navigatio,) omnium cum oppidorum, quae Danubius irrigat, tum fluviorum, qui in eum devolvuntur, diligenti & jucunda observatione: Ipsum etiam authorem e Graeco sermone in Latinum vertit, plurimisque mendis repurgavit, Lugd. 1577. Ejusdem Prognosticon de an Chr. 1588. & ijs, qui sequuntur ad magnum diem ultimi judicij. Sed & Carmina Epistolae, Orationes Prosopographicae ejusdem multa extant, ut sunt Carolus Magnus redivivus i. e. Caroli M. cum Henrico M. Gallorum Rege comparatio 1592. Oratio funebris in obitum Bullingeri 1575. Descripsit vitam Iosiae Simleri 1577. Epistolam dedit ad Georgium Comitem Labiscanum gratulatoriam, quae impressa est cum Panegyrica Oratione Labiscani. Ejusdem Irene Gallica, Henrici IV. auspicijs sancita gratulatio ad Gallos, Tig. prodiit & Basileae. Ejusdem habeo aliquot Epistolas Msc. de variis thematibus.
units.tr: Stuckius Iohannes Guilelmus, of Zurich, born of the noble and ancient Stuck family, for some time assistant to Jakob Ammann, professor of rhetoric and logic, afterwards ordinary professor of theology from the year of Christ 1571 to 1607. He also accompanied Peter Martyr to the colloquy at Poissy, and I have some letters in his own hand written from France to Zurich. By his studies he gained a great name among the learned. He wrote various works. I. Theological. I have his commentaries on Zechariah in manuscript; two orations on the ecclesiastical office; On the angels and the angelic protection and guardianship of men, a devout meditation, etc., with some passages taken from the manuscript homilies of Chrysostom. Zurich, 1595. He also wrote a treatise in the vernacular on the Lord's Supper. In refuting Huberianism his work was outstanding and distinguished, as we shall later note in Stumpf. II. Philological. On the sacred rites and sacrifices of the Gentiles. Three books on banquet antiquities, in which are explained the ancient kinds of feasts among the Hebrews, Greeks, Romans and other nations, as well as their customs, usages, rites and convivial ceremonies, and these are compared with those which are today in use both among Christians and among other peoples foreign to the Christian name; many matters that are grammatical, physical, medical, ethical, economic, political, philosophical and finally historical, pleasant and useful to know, are treated; many obscure passages of sacred and profane ancient authors are illuminated, corrupt ones are emended; and lastly the desperate and deplorable luxury and extravagance of our times is condemned with severe censure. Zurich, 1582. III. Philosophical, geographical, especially astronomical, such as the scholia on Arrian, historian and philosopher, on the periplus of the Euxine Sea and the Erythraean Sea, which contain a lucid description of the regions, peoples, islands, towns, rivers, merchandise and other memorable things of both voyages, drawn from a careful comparison of ancient and recent authors; added (besides the places which the skilful navigation of the Portuguese has penetrated) is a careful and pleasant observation of all the towns that the Danube waters, and of the rivers that flow into it. He also translated the author himself from Greek into Latin and cleansed him of very many faults. Leiden, 1577. His Prognostication for the year 1588, and for those who look forward to the great day of the last judgment. There also exist many of his poems, letters and prosopographical orations, such as Charlemagne Reborn, that is, a comparison of Charlemagne with Henry IV, King of the French, 1592; a funeral oration on the death of Bullinger, 1575; he wrote the life of Josias Simler, 1577. He gave a letter of congratulation to Count Georg of Labiscan, which was printed along with the Panegyric Oration of Labiscanus. His Gallic Irene, a congratulation to the French sanctioned under the auspices of Henry IV, appeared at Zurich and at Basel. I have some of his manuscript letters on various themes.

units.la: Stuckius, Iob. Rodolphus, Ecclesiae Abbatissanae Minister 1626. Artium Rhetoro. Logicarum Professor publicus 1632. Theologus 1639. Scholarcha perpetuus & Bibliothecarius ad an. Chr. 1661. quo diem obijt, familiae nobilissimae sigillum. Fuit superioris ex fratre nepos, Theologus Φερωνυμος, doctus, solidus, placidus, & ad varios obeundos labores aptus natus. Plura scripsit quam edidit. Edidit tamen Comment. Petri Martyris in Threnos. Varias disputationes Theologicas, cujusmodi sunt. 1. Examen Dialogi cujusdam de religione. VVilhelmus mus Gothardus, Solodurensis sacrificulus, virulento scripto doctrinam Reformatam impudenter allatravit, cui eruditas aliquot disputationes Synodales opposuit, quæ Tractatum constituunt contra Pontificios non contemnendum.
units.tr: Stuckius, Johann Rudolf, minister of the church at Abbatissana, 1626; public professor of rhetoric and logic, 1632; theologian, 1639; perpetual scholarch and librarian until he died in the year of Christ 1661, a member of a most noble family. He was the nephew, through a brother, of the older man of the same name, a learned, solid and gentle theologian, born fit for many kinds of labour. He wrote more than he published. He did publish a commentary on Peter Martyr's Lamentations, and various theological disputations, of which the following are examples: (1) an Examination of a certain Dialogue on Religion. Wilhelm Gotthard, a Solothurn priest, bitterly attacked the Reformed doctrine in a venomous piece of writing, and Stuckius answered him with several learned synodal disputations, which together make up a not contemptible treatise against the Papists.

units.la: 2. Brevis Διδασκαλία de phrasibus ad unionem Christi hypostaticam pertinentibus 1653. 3. Declaratio brevis argumentorum de Pædo-baptismo 1658. 4. Theoremata Theologica de Sacra Domini Cæna, 1659. 5. Theses Theologicæ de Festis Christianorum 1658. 6. Iudicium Orthodoxum & æquum de refponfionibus Parochi cujusdam (Badensis) quas ipse Apocrifes appellat, ad probationes, quas ex thesibus de Missa, Tiguri primo Maij, an. Chr. 1556. editis, collegit 1657. 7. Heptas Thesium de Missa, 1656. 8. Addi possunt Responsiones Orthodoxæ ad XII. Iesuitæ Keddij postulata. 9. Difput. de peccato originali. 10. Prædicamenta Mosis. 11. An cætus hodiernus sub Pontifice Romano mereatur Ecclesiæ nomen, & Christi sit Ecclesia. 12. Eodem Præside ventilata fuit disputatio de Iejunio. 13. De Baptismo. 14. Pædobaptismo. 15. An infantes sine Baptismo morientes, vitâ æternâ sint excludendi. 16. De præsentia & communione Corporis Christi in S. Cæna. 17. Diascepsis de resipiscentia. 18 De Resurrectione mortuorum, Methodi specimen. 19. Dulce, triennium, sive de Concordia VVittebergensi. Doctissimis insuper commentarijs illustravit Synopsin Theologicam Breitingeri. Cui & erudite parentavit. Sed & plures ejus sunt Orationes, propositiones, carmina, consilia, quæ celeberrimi Theologi, Præceptoris, Compatris & Collegæ Ἐφυίαν, μάθησιν, καὶ ἄσκησιν abunde probant.
units.tr: (2) A brief Instruction [Διδασκαλία] on the phrases pertaining to the hypostatic union of Christ, 1653; (3) a brief declaration of the arguments concerning infant baptism, 1658; (4) theological theses on the Holy Supper of the Lord, 1659; (5) theological theses on the feasts of the Christians, 1658; (6) a sound and fair judgment on the replies of a certain (Baden) parish priest, which he himself calls Apocryphal, gathered against the proofs drawn from the theses on the Mass published at Zurich on 1 May 1556, 1657; (7) a Heptad of Theses on the Mass, 1656; (8) to these may be added his Orthodox Responses to the twelve demands of the Jesuit Keddi; (9) a disputation on original sin; (10) the Precepts of Moses; (11) whether the present assembly under the Roman Pontiff deserves the name of Church, and whether it is the Church of Christ; (12) under the same presidency a disputation on fasting was debated; (13) on baptism; (14) on infant baptism; (15) whether infants dying without baptism are to be excluded from eternal life; (16) on the presence and communion of the body of Christ in the Holy Supper; (17) a discussion of repentance; (18) on the resurrection of the dead, a specimen of method; (19) Dulce triennium, or on the Concord of Wittenberg. He also illustrated the Theological Synopsis of Breitinger with most learned commentaries, and wrote an erudite funeral oration for him. There are also many of his orations, propositions, poems and counsels, which abundantly prove the nature, learning and practice [Ἐφυΐαν, μάθησιν, καὶ ἄσκησιν] of that most celebrated theologian, his teacher, godfather and colleague.

units.la: Stumpfius Iohannes, Ecclesiæ in agro Tigurino Minister, Bubikonæ primum; postea Stamhemij 1543. Capituli Lithopolitani Decanus, Theologus & Historicus insignis. Vernaculo sermone scripsit Concilium Constantiense 1541. Historiam Helveticam; quæ aliquoties prodiit; ultimo Celeberrimi VVaseri cura castigatam & auctam 1606 Breviter contra malevolos eam vindicavimus, Forerum præsertim Iesuitam, Hist. Eccles. Sec. 9. pag. 623. Analect. P. II. p. 217. Idem Historiæ suæ epitomen edidit 1554. Plura ejus MSS. extant in Bibliotheca nostra Civica, unde non pauca transcribenda curavi. Ejusdem est Historia Henrici Imperatoris IV. vernaculè. Libellus de ultimo judicio; Translatio Historiæ Sacramentariæ, Lud. Lavateri.
units.tr: Stumpf, Johann, minister of the Church in the Zurich countryside, first at Bubikon, then at Stammheim from 1543; dean of the chapter of Embrach (Lithopolis), a distinguished theologian and historian. In the vernacular he wrote on the Council of Constance, 1541, and a Swiss History, which appeared several times and last, revised and enlarged under the care of the most celebrated Waser, 1606. We have briefly defended it against its ill-wishers, especially the Jesuit Forer, in our Church History, sec. 9, p. 623, and Analecta II, p. 217. He also published an epitome of his history, 1554. Many of his manuscripts survive in our civic library, and I have arranged for not a few of them to be copied. His is also the History of the Emperor Henry IV, in the vernacular; a little book on the Last Judgment; and a translation of Ludwig Lavater's History of the Sacramentarians.

units.la: Stumpfius Rodolphus F. Kilchbergensis primum, postea ad Prædicatores in urbe Minister 1584. Antistes denique, Lavateri Successor, ab an. Chr. 1586. ad 1592. Historiam Helveticam auxit. Magno præterea studio acta sui temporis Ecclesiastica conscripsit. Extat adhuc in Archivo Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Tomus, quo Acta Huberiana diligentissimè ab eo collecta exhibentur. Inter alia etiam continetur Raphaelis Eglini de Oratione Alberianis judicium, & errorum ejus confutatio. Varia Huberi scripta Elenctica, Historica, &c. De instaurato Huberiano & Tubingensi certamine 1590. adversus Bezam & Musculum. Scriptum, ptum, in quo tractantur. 1. Paraleipomena de inhærente justitia. 2. De injustitia & corruptione naturali pravus error. 3. De Iustitia Dei, quam Alberius ex Essentia Dei derivat, unde dependeat necessario a. Ofiandrismus. b. Eutychianismus. c. Nestorianismus. d. Vbiquitas, ex communicatione proprietatis divinæ naturæ &c. 4. Successio Cathedralis, Episcopi, Romani, in Petri primatum: Quibus omnibus breviter indicatis & refutatis veritas ipsa opponitur. Guil. Stuckij judicium de Controversiis Alberianis & Huberianis tollendis. Cætera Historiam belli Sabaudiei cum Genevensibus & Gallici intestini describunt.
units.tr: Stumpf, Rudolf, son of Franz, first minister at Kilchberg, then from 1584 minister to the preachers in the city; finally antistes, successor of Lavater, from 1586 to 1592. He enlarged the Swiss History. Besides this, with great diligence he wrote down the ecclesiastical events of his own time. There still survives in the archive of the Zurich Church a volume in which the Acts of Huber, most diligently collected by him, are presented. Among other things it also contains Raphael Egli's judgment on Alberus's Oration and his refutation of its errors. Huber's various polemical and historical writings, etc., and On the Renewed Huberian and Tübingen Controversy, 1590, against Beza and Musculus. A writing in which the following are treated: (1) Paraleipomena on inherent righteousness; (2) on injustice and natural corruption, a perverse error; (3) on the justice of God, which Alberus derives from the essence of God, and from which it depends of necessity: a. Osiandrism, b. Eutychianism, c. Nestorianism, d. ubiquity, from the communication of the properties of the divine nature, etc.; (4) the cathedral succession of the Roman bishops to the primacy of Peter. All these matters, briefly indicated and refuted, are set over against the truth itself. Wilhelm Stuck's judgment on removing the Alberian and Huberian controversies. The rest describe the war of Savoy with the Genevans and the French civil strife.

units.la: Suterus, Iob. Caspar, Scholæ primùm Classicæ apud Tigurinos Collaborator, Collegii postea Parthenici Inspector, Ecclesiæ tandem Collegiatæ Archidiaconus vigilantissimus ab an. Chr. 1638. ad 1655. quo, inter preces nostras, animam reddidit. Catechesin Tigurinam & analysi & testimoniis Scripturæ vestitam, Catechumenorum captui feliciter accommodavit. Ejusdem varia extant carmina Latina & Germanica.
units.tr: Suter, Johann Kaspar, first collaborator at the Classical School among the Zurich people, afterwards inspector of the Parthenian college, and finally a most watchful archdeacon of the collegiate church from 1638 to 1655, when he gave up his soul among our prayers. He skilfully adapted the Zurich Catechism, clothed in analysis and the testimonies of Scripture, to the understanding of catechumens. Various poems of his in Latin and German survive.

units.la: Schwarzenbachius Iob. Rodolphus, Verbi Minister Grunenbaci in Algoja; Neftenbaci in agro Tigurino; Ecclesiæ, tandem Abbatissanæ Diaconus 1616. & Pastor 1626. ad 1646. Compendium dedit Historiæ Iobi, Tiguri.
units.tr: Schwarzenbach, Johann Rudolf, minister of the Word at Grüningen in Aargau and at Nänikon in the Zurich countryside; deacon of the church at Abbatissana in 1616 and pastor from 1626 to 1646. He gave a compendium of the History of Job, at Zurich.

units.la: Suicerus, Iob. Caspar, Professor Linguarum Græcæ & Hebraicæ in Collegio Carolino meritissimus, Græcæ literaturæ promotor indefessus, dedit hactenus rationem Syntaxeos Græcæ, Syllogen vocum N. T. Græcam: ἐμπυρόμ- ματα varia, Sacra & profana; soluta & ligata. Næper Frisii Dictionarium multo & emendatius dedit, & auctius. Comenij etiam Vestibulum, Scholarum usibus felicius accommodavit. Sed plura proximè ab eo expectamus, Hesychij præsertim, scriptoris doctissimi, sed pessimè hactenus tractati editionem, & authore, & sæculo nostro dignam. Lexicon præterea Patrum colligere pridem cœpit, magnóque jam incremento aliquo usque perduxit, eximium facturus operæ pretium, ubi colophonem ei aliquando, quod serió optamus, impo-suerit.
units.tr: Suicer, Johann Kaspar, most deserving professor of Greek and Hebrew at the Carolinum, tireless promoter of Greek literature. Hitherto he has given an account of Greek syntax, a Greek collection of the words of the New Testament, and various Empyromata [ἐμπυρώματα], sacred and profane, in prose and verse. Not long ago he gave a much improved and enlarged dictionary of Frisius, and he has adapted Comenius's Vestibulum more happily to the use of schools. But we expect more from him soon, especially an edition of Hesychius, a most learned writer who has so far been very badly handled, worthy both of its author and of our age. He has also long since begun to gather a lexicon of the Fathers and has brought it by now to a considerable size, and he will do an excellent service when at last he sets the finishing touch to it, as we earnestly hope he will.

units.la: Suicerus Iob. Henricus, Ecclesiæ, in agro Tigurino, Rixenbacensis Pastor ab an. Chr. 1594. ad 1612. scripsit compendium Historiæ Helveticæ, Latinè; ad an. Chr. 1607. Annales Helvetiæ, vernaculè; MS. Ex quibus in meum transscripta sunt, quæ de bellis Transalpinis agunt. Vt perfectiorem daret Historiam, exteros etiam consuluit Historicos, Guicciardinum cumprimis & Paulum Iovium.
units.tr: Suicer, Johann Heinrich, minister at Rixenbach in the Zurich countryside from 1594 to 1612. He wrote a compendium of Swiss History in Latin, down to the year of Christ 1607, and Swiss Annals in the vernacular, in manuscript. From these have been copied for me the passages dealing with the Transalpine wars. In order to give a more complete history, he also consulted foreign historians, above all Guicciardini and Paolo Giovio.

units.la: T.
units.tr: T.

units.la: Tomannus, Petrus, Tigurinus, Ecclesiæ Nicroviensis in Archi Palatinatu Pastor; Scholæ postmodum Tigurinæ in Collegio Humanitatis, tandem in Collegio Carolino, Professor Græco Hebræus ab a. Ch. 1636. Theologus ad 1652. Vir Linguarum callentissimus, Philologus, & Antiquarius insignis. Sed pauca scripsit. Prodierunt ejus aliquot disputationes Synodales, cujusmodi sunt, de Praedestinatione, de reatu primi peccati, de libero arbitrio: de Sacramentis N. T. de Baptismo, Orthodoxas consensus de Baptismate parvulorum: de justificatione. Habeo ejusdem quasdam observationes Philologicas in Epistolam ad Philemonem, eruditas, & antiquitatis studio refertas.
units.tr: Tomannus, Petrus, of Zurich, was minister of the church at Nicrovia in the Upper Palatinate. He later became teacher in the Zurich school in the College of Humanity and finally professor of Greek and Hebrew in the Carolinum College from 1636, and was a theologian until 1652. He was a man very learned in languages, a philologist and an outstanding antiquary. He wrote little, however. Several of his synodal disputations were published, such as those on predestination, on the guilt of the first sin, on free will, on the sacraments of the New Testament, on baptism, the Orthodox consensus on the baptism of infants, and on justification. I have some of his philological observations on the Epistle to Philemon, learned and full of antiquarian study.

units.la: Tomannus Sadrachus, Caspari Consulis Tigurini ex fratre nepos, Graecarum literarum callentissimus. Vicariam in lectionibus publicis aliquandiu praestitit operam. Extant Epitaphia ejus in obitum Bullingeri 1575. Simleri, Gualtheri F. Epigrammata in antiquitates conviviales Stuckij, Graeco-Latina. Praeterea ex omnibus Graecis authoribus Classicis veteribus & recentioribus ingens opus collegit Lexico-Philologicum, ex quibus, quicquid vel phraseos habent, vel sententiae ad certos redegit Locos communes. Ultimam expoliendi operis limam expectabamus à D. Petro Tomano, in cujus Bibliotheca me MSS. illa videre memini. Ego, ut opinor phraseologiam ejus Homericam habeo, vix tamen ejus propria manu scriptam, absoluta libris VII. I. πεὶ οἰκονομίας, cujus caput α. est πεὶ οἰκιας, καὶ τ αὐτὰ μερῶν. β. πεὶ γονέων, καὶ τέκνων. γ. πεὶ ἡλικίας. δ. πεὶ τῆς πατρίδος. ε. πεὶ ἐαυτῆ ... εἰμάτων. ς. πεὶ ἐργασίας. ζ. πεὶ γά-μα. η. πεὶ τῆς ... ζωάμα ... ἐπιμελείας. θ. πεὶ ... ἰζειν ... ἐξεοῖς. ι. πεὶ τὴν τροφὴν. ια. πεὶ παιδιῶν. ιβ. ὑπνῳ, καὶ τὰ πεὶ τὸν αὐτὸν. ιγ. γάνα ... καὶ τὰ μετ᾽ αὐτὸν.
units.tr: Tomannus Sadrachus, nephew through a brother of Caspar, Zurich magistrate, was very learned in Greek literature. For some time he served as a deputy in the public lectures. His epitaphs on the death of Bullinger (1575) survive, as do Simler's and Gualther's epigrams, Greek and Latin, on Stucki's antiquities of the table. Besides this, he collected from all the Greek authors, classical, ancient and more recent, a huge lexicon-philological work, in which whatever phrases or sayings he found he arranged under certain common topics. We were expecting the final polishing of this work from Master Peter Tomannus, in whose library I remember seeing those manuscripts. I think I have his Homeric phraseology, though hardly in his own hand, completed in seven books. I. On economy [περὶ οἰκονομίας], whose first chapter is on the house and its parts [περὶ οἴκιας, καὶ τῶν αὐτῆς μερῶν]. II. On parents and children [περὶ γονέων, καὶ τέκνων]. III. On age [περὶ ἡλικίας]. IV. On the fatherland [περὶ τῆς πατρίδος]. V. On garments [περὶ ἐσθήτων]. VI. On work [περὶ ἐργασίας]. VII. On marriage [περὶ γάμου]. VIII. On the care of life [περὶ τῆς ζωῆς ἐπιμελείας]. IX. On sitting and ... [περὶ ... ἱζειν ...]. X. On food [περὶ τὴν τροφὴν]. XI. On play [περὶ παιδιῶν]. XII. On sleep, and the matters connected with it [ὕπνου, καὶ τὰ περὶ τὸν αὐτὸν]. XIII. On old age, and what follows it [περὶ γήρως, καὶ τὰ μετ᾽ αὐτὸν].

units.la: Liber II.
units.tr: Book II.

units.la: τὰ πολιτικά. c. α. ἐπίθετα καὶ Φαρίσεις πεὶ πόλεως. β. ἐπίθετα ἀρχόντων καὶ Βασιλέων, καὶ Φαρίσεις ἐ ἀνάστασιν. γ. πεὶ τῆς ἀγορᾶς.
units.tr: Political matters [τὰ πολιτικά]. Chapter 1: Concerning the city [περὶ πόλεως], and the Pharisees. Chapter 2: Concerning rulers and kings, and the Pharisees concerning the resurrection. Chapter 3: Concerning the marketplace [περὶ τῆς ἀγορᾶς].

units.la: Liber III.
units.tr: Book III.

units.la: Continet τὰ ἀγεικά, ζῷα ἄλογα, τὰς ἐ ἀερ-ώσεις. c. a. πεὶ χθονὸς, καὶ τ αὐτῆς μερῶν, χώρων &c. β. οἰκήματα ἀγεικά καὶ σεῖμοί. γ. Βίος ἀγεικὸς, ἐ ἀλοζύνη γεωργικά. δ. Φυτὰ-σις, ἄρος, θερισμὸς, καὶ ἄλλα γεωργικά. ε. ξυλοτομία, ἐ καταφλέξις τ ξύλων. ς. ποιμενικὴ. τ. πεὶ κυνῶν, ἐ κυνηγεσίας, πεὶ ἡρῶν, ἐ ἥρως. η. ἱπποζύνη. θ. ἑρπετὰ. ι. πτηνὰ. ια. μετέωρα, αἴτε τὰ ἀέρ-ω κρίσεις ποιοῦσι.
units.tr: Contains the things pertaining to the fields, irrational animals, and the predictions from the air [τὰ ἀγρικά, ζῷα ἄλογα, τὰς ἐξ ἀέρος ἀποφάσεις]. c. a. concerning the earth, and its parts, regions [περὶ χθονὸς, καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς μερῶν, χώρων] &c. β. farm buildings and huts [οἰκήματα ἀγροικικὰ καὶ σκηνοί]. γ. Rural life, and the labours of farming [Βίος ἀγροικικὸς, καὶ πόνοι γεωργικά]. δ. Planting, ploughing, harvesting, and other farm work [Φυτεία, ἄροσις, θερισμὸς, καὶ ἄλλα γεωργικά]. ε. Woodcutting, and the burning of wood [ξυλοτομία, καὶ καταφλέξις τῶν ξύλων]. ς. Herding [ποιμενικὴ]. τ. Concerning dogs, hunting, concerning heroes, and the hero [περὶ κυνῶν, καὶ κυνηγεσίας, περὶ ἡρώων, καὶ ἥρως]. η. Horse-keeping [ἱπποτροφία]. θ. Creeping things [ἑρπετὰ]. ι. Birds [πτηνὰ]. ια. Things in the heights, that is, the things in the air that make predictions [μετέωρα, αἳ τὰ ἀέρια κρίσεις ποιοῦσι].

units.la: Liber IV.
units.tr: Book IV.

units.la: Θαλάσσεια, ναυτικά. Cap. α. Συνώνυμα, ἐπίθετα, καὶ Φαρίσεις τῆς θαλάσσης, τ αἰγιαλῶν, τ λιμένων, καὶ πολιμῶν, εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐ-βολῶν καὶ τ ἄλλων τ ποιήτων πλεννήσεων. β. πεὶ νεῶν, καὶ τ αὐτῶν μερῶν. γ. Ναῦται καὶ κυβερνῆται. δ. ἀφαρπαγὴ ἐ ψόλος, καὶ Φαρίσεις ἐ ἀνάγειν. ε. ψόλης καὶ τὰ πεὶ αὐτόν. ς. Φαρίσεις ἐ καταγειν, καὶ ἀπικέλσαι, ἐ ἀσπορ-μίζειν τινὶ τόπῳ, ἐ ὁρμεῖν καὶ καθελκεῖν τὴν νῆα, ἐ ἀποκοσμῆσαι τὰ τ νηὸς ἔνδεια, ἐ τ ἄλλων τ τοιῶν. τ. Συμβεβηκότα τὰ μὲν τῆς θαλάσσης, τὰ δὲ ἐ ψόλος. η. Φαρίσεις ἐ νήχεσθαι, καὶ ἰχθυᾶν, καὶ πεὶ τ ἰχθύων.
units.tr: Maritime and nautical matters. Chap. 1. Synonyms, epithets and phrases concerning the sea, the shores, the harbours and the storms, concerning the casting of things into the sea, and other poetic expressions. 2. Concerning ships and their parts. 3. Sailors and pilots. 4. Seizing and sinking, and putting in or sailing to a place. 5. Storms and what pertains to them. 6. Phrases for running aground, landing, mooring at a place, anchoring and launching the ship, and for fitting out the ship's equipment, and other such things. 7. Things that happen partly to the sea and partly through storms. 8. Phrases for swimming, fishing, and concerning fish.

units.la: Liber V. exhibet πολεμικὰ. C. a. ἐπἰθεῖα, ζυνώνυμα, καὶ Φαάσεις. β. ὥδασκλὴ πολεμικὴ ἡ καθόλου πάντα περὶ τ μάχης, ἡ πολιορκίας γενομένα. γ. ὁπλα. δ. τὰ ἐξ πολέμυ ἡ μάχης ζυμβεβηκότα. ε. Διαθέσεις ἡ ζυμπτώματα τ μαχαιωτῶν. ς. τὰ μέρη τ μαχῶν προηγέμενα. τ. τὰ τῆς μάχης μέρη δἰ τέρφ, ἢ μέσα. η. μαχῆτης ὁ μὲν καλὸς, ὁ δὲ κακὸς. θ. μάχη. ι. τὰ τῆς μάχης μέρη τελευτὴ, θεαύματα, Φωναὶ, ἡ τὰ περὶ αὐτὰ πάντα. ια. τὰ τῆ μάχη ἑπόμενα. ιβ. ἱππομαχία, ναυμαχία. ιγ. πολιορκία. ιδ. πορθήσεις, ἁλώσεις πόλεων. Liber V. περὶ ἐξ ἀνθρώπου. ζ.α. ζυνώνυμα, ἐπἰθεῖα, ἡ Φεάσεις περὶ ἀνθρώπου, ἡ τ αὐτὸ μερῶν προηγούντων τῆς ψυχῆς δηλαδὴ ἐξ ζώματος, ἡ κοιναὶ ἐννοιαι περὶ αὐτῶν. β. ποιότης ἀνθρώπου καθολικὴ ἡ ζωμαλικὴ. γ. ποιεῖν καὶ πάσχειν. δ. περὶ Φθόγγων, λεξυγῆς, ἰωῆς, Φωνῆς, λόγων, ἐπέων, μύθων. ε. περὶ τ τῆς ψυχῆς ἐξεων, ἡ τ τῆς αὐτῆς ἐνεργῶν, ἡ πραξεων ἁπασῶν. ς. τὰ τῆς ψυχῆς μικ]α, ἡ πρακτικὰ, καὶ ἀῶλα πάθη. Liber VI. τὰ ἔξω ζυμβεβηκότα ἀνθρώπω ζα. θρησκεία. β. περὶ δυτυχίας, καὶ δυσυχίας, καθολικῶς. γ. δὐτυχία, δυσυχία μερικὴ. δ. τόπω, χρόνω, καὶ ἄλλαι πεισάσεις.
units.tr: Book V. presents military matters. Chap. 1. Epithets, synonyms and phrases. 2. A treatise on the art of war, or everything generally concerning battle or siege. 3. Arms. 4. Things that befall in war or battle. 5. The dispositions or misfortunes of combatants. 6. The preliminary parts of battles. 7. The parts of battle in the middle. 8. The warrior, the good and the bad. 9. Battle. 10. The final parts of battle: its ends, spectacles, cries and everything about them. 11. What follows battle. 12. Cavalry battle, naval battle. 13. Siege. 14. The sacking and capture of cities. Book V. concerning man. Chap. 1. Synonyms, epithets and phrases concerning man, or of the parts that precede the soul, namely the body, or common notions about them. 2. The general and bodily quality of man. 3. Doing and suffering. 4. Concerning sounds, speech, voice, words, utterances, verses and fables. 5. Concerning the habits of the soul, or its activities, or all its actions. 6. The affections of the soul, the practical and the passive. Book VI. external accidents befalling man. Chap. 1. Religion. 2. Good and bad fortune in general. 3. Particular good and bad fortune. 4. Place, time, and other circumstances.

units.la: Truebius Felix, Senatoris Tigurini nonagenarii filius, Vir & prudentia singulari, & etiam eruditione, Ecclesiæ & Scholæ Minister: Nam & Linguam Hebræam publicè docuit, & Archidiaconus tandem fuit Ecclesiæ Collegiatæ ab an. Chr. 1586. ad 1594. ætat 51. quo obiit, peste inopinata: Carmina quædam scripsit, in obitum D. Bullingeri, Gesneri, Simleri & alia.
units.tr: Truebius Felix, son of Senator Tigurinus, who lived to ninety, a man of singular prudence and also of learning, minister of the Church and of the school. For he taught the Hebrew language publicly, and at length was archdeacon of the collegiate church from 1586 to 1594. He died of an unexpected plague at the age of 51. He wrote some poems on the death of Master Bullinger, Gesner, Simler and others.

units.la: Torinus Albanus, Vitoduranus Medicus, Græcarum literarum peritissimus, Pauli Æginetæ Enchiridion Latinè vertit, cum annotationibus, quibus translationis suæ rationem reddidit. Vertit etiam Philareti librum de pulsibus, & Theophili de urinis Basil. 1533. Polybi antiquissimi Medici, de seminis humani natura, Bas. 1544. Epiphanij Episcopi, de Prophetarum vita & interitu commentarium, qui cum textu Græco prodiit Basil. 1529. Dioclis Caristii de tuenda sanitate ad Antigonum Regem libellum aureum. Agapeti Diaconi de officio Regis ad Iustinianum Cæsarem. Iohannis Damascenì, Medici de exquisita febrium curatione compendiosum diegema, & aphorismos ejusdem ex barbara translatione elegantiore paraphrasi illustravit, Basil. 1542. Emanuelis Chrysoloræ Epitomen Grammatices Latinam fecit, Bas. 1528. Cælij Apitij, de re culinaria lib. 22. partim suo marte, partim ad vetustum exemplar castigatos edidit, anno 1541. una cum Platinæ libris de honesta voluptate & obsoniis. Alexandri Tralliani libros interpretatus est. Præterea paulò ante mortem Latinitate donavit Philathei Medici commentarios Græcos, in Aphorismos Græcos. Basileæ obiit 1550.
units.tr: Torinus Albanus, a physician of Winterthur and most expert in Greek literature, translated Paul of Aegina's Handbook into Latin, with annotations in which he explained the reasons for his translation. He also translated Philaretus's book on pulses and Theophilus's on urines (Basel, 1533); the work on the nature of human seed by Polybus, a very ancient physician (Basel, 1544); the commentary of Bishop Epiphanius on the life and death of the prophets, which appeared with the Greek text (Basel, 1529); the little golden book of Diocles of Carystus on the preservation of health, addressed to King Antigonus; the book of Agapetus the Deacon on the duty of a king, addressed to the Emperor Justinian; and the short treatise of John Damascene the physician on the exact cure of fevers, together with his aphorisms, which he illuminated with a more elegant paraphrase made from a barbarous translation (Basel, 1542). He made a Latin version of Manuel Chrysoloras's Epitome of Grammar (Basel, 1528). He published, partly by his own labour and partly by collation with an old copy, the twenty-two books of Caelius Apicius on cookery, in 1541, together with Platina's books on honest pleasure and on delicacies. He translated the books of Alexander of Tralles. Moreover, shortly before his death he rendered into Latin the Greek commentaries of the physician Philathius on the Greek Aphorisms. He died at Basel in 1550.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Vinslerus, Iosua, Tigurinus, Biennensis Ecclesiae Minister carmen scripsit in obitum Bullingeri. Habeo Epistolas ejus aliquot MS.
units.tr: Vinslerus, Josua, a Tigurine, minister of the church at Biel, wrote a poem on the death of Bullinger. I have several of his letters in manuscript.

units.la: Vitoduranus, Iohannes, Ita καὶ ἐξοχὴν vocatur Franciscanus quidam Monachus, patria Vitoduranus, qui Historiam scripsit ab an Chr. 1215. ad 1348. Autographum extat in Bibliotheca nostra Civica; Apographo pridem meam instruxi Bibliothecam, quod multa haberet author, quae ubique obvia non sunt, & quae non patriae tantum sive Helveticae, sed & Ecclesiasticae Historiae magnam afferunt lucem.
units.tr: Vitoduranus, John, thus called by way of eminence [καὶ ἐξοχήν], was a Franciscan monk, a native of Winterthur (Vitoduranus), who wrote a history from 1215 to 1348. The autograph exists in our civic library. Long ago I furnished my own library with a copy, because the author has much that is not found everywhere, and which sheds great light not only on the history of our homeland or Helvetia, but also on Church history.

units.la: Vollenweiderus Iacobus, in agro primum Turgae, postea Tigurino Vadis villae 1615. & Plachae 1647. Minister: Scripsit Theologica nonnulla, Elenctica potissimum; contra Wilhelmum Gothardum, & Danielem Martinum Apostatam Bearnensem, Lingua vernacula 1647. Examen novitatum cujusdam Levi Christiani, Sacerdotis secundum ordinem Melchisedeci, 1622.
units.tr: Vollenweider, Jakob, first in the district of Thurgau, later a minister in the Zurich village of Wädenswil (Vadis) from 1615 and at Plachae from 1647. He wrote several theological works, chiefly polemical: against Wilhelm Gotthard and Daniel Martin, the apostate from Béarn, in the vernacular, 1647; and An Examination of the Novelties of a Certain Levi Christianus, Priest According to the Order of Melchizedek, 1622.

units.la: Vtingerus, Henricus, Ecclesiae Collegiatae Canonicus, & Custos Collegii ante Reformationem. Circa & post Reformationem Zuinglii & Bullingeri fidus Paraštates. Non Ecclesia modo, sed & Respublica ejus saepe usa est opera, ubi ad Exteros, Reges, Principes &c. scribendum fuit. Eidem tribuitur Historia de origine, progressu, & Reformatione Collegii Carolini, quae in Archivo Collegii adhuc asservatur. Habeo ejusdem manuscripta non pauca.
units.tr: Utinger, Heinrich, canon of the collegiate church and custodian of the college before the Reformation. Around and after the Reformation of Zwingli and Bullinger he was their faithful assistant [παραστάτης]. Not only the Church but also the commonwealth often used his services, whenever letters had to be written to foreigners, kings, princes and others. To him is attributed the history of the origin, progress and reformation of the Carolinum college, which is still kept in the college archive. I have not a few of his manuscripts.

units.la: Vvaserus Caspar, Tigurinus, Simleri gener, Vir πολυλαωτος, Scholae & Ecclesiae nostrae Doctor, & Professor Graeco-Hebraeus ab an. Chr. 1607. postea ab an. Chr. 1611. Theologus ad 1625. d. 9. Septembris (qui emortualis illi fuit) meritissimus, & in quo hoc prae aliis observandum, quod lucubrationibus suis doctissimis amorem patriae conciliarit apud omnes promiscue eruditos, nulla religionis habita ratione. Placet Catalogum laborum ejus exhibere verbis, viri clarissimi, (cujus pietas & integritas apud nos non tantum est in memoria recentissima, sed etiam in veneratione) Iodoci a Kufen, quae ex Oratione ejus de vita & obitu Caspari Vvaseri pag. 17. ita habent:
units.tr: Wasser, Caspar, a Tigurine, son-in-law of Simler, a man of great renown [πολυλαώτος], doctor of our school and church, and professor of Greek and Hebrew from 1607, and afterwards theologian from 1611 until 9 September 1625, the day of his death, most deserving. In him one must observe beyond others that by his most learned labours he won for himself love for his homeland among all the learned, regardless of religion. I think it fitting to set out a catalogue of his labours in the words of that most distinguished man, whose piety and integrity are not only fresh in our memory but also held in veneration among us, Jodocus a Kuefen. In his oration on the life and death of Caspar Wasser, page 17, he writes as follows:

units.la: Nec vero tantum Ecclesiae profuit concionando, & Scholae profitendo, sed utrique etiam multum commodavit scribendo: ut evidentissime testantur praeclara ejus scripta memoriae prodita, quorum quaedam sunt Theologica, quaedam Philologica, & Historica, quaedam Scholastica. In numero monumentorum Theologicorum pono Evangelium Romanum, seu libros duos de remissione peccatorum contra Indulgentias Papales, ex sermone Gallico in Germanicum translatos: analysin Psalmi centesimi decimi, de Sacerdotio Christi secundum ordinem Melchisedec: Hieroglyphicum doctrinae Christianae: Consessionem fidei Iacobi I. Regis Magnae Britanniae, ex Anglico in Germanicum sermonem translatam: Tractatus aliquot Germanicos de Purgatorio: de Imaginibus; De Papa Romano, quod sit Antichristus; De Invocatione Sanctorum: rum: De Indulgentiis Pontificiorum: De Erroribus Schwenkfeldianorum: Archetypos homiliarum Gualtheri in Iesaiam, & Festalium, quos ex autographo correxit, notis illustravit, indice auxit: Conradi Grasseri Plagam regiam, sive commentarium in Apocalypsin B. Iohannis, quem interpolavit, edidit, eidemque Epistolam dedicatoriam ad Iacobum I. M. Britanniæ Regem præfixit. Inprimis vero ad opera Theologica pertinet opus veré aureum, Lexicon videlicet Biblicum, quod multos jam annos, multorum doctissimorum virorum rogatu incitatus, & commendatione confirmatus, magno studio, cura & labore collegit, in certas literas, juxta ordinem Alphabeticum, redegit, publicíque juris facere constituit, si vita diuturniori ipsi frui licuisset. In adornatione ejus pervenit ad literam T.adhæsitque ad vocem TRIBVLA, & TRIEVLATIO: quam licèt sæpius absolvere voluerit, nimia tamen tribulatione, & morbi ingravescentis vi oppressus, & præmatura morte sublatus, ad finem perducere non potuit. Dolendum sanè est, & quidem magnopere dolendum, non potuisse opus hoc tam præclarum, tam utile, tam necessarium absolvi, quod magnam utilitatem Ecclesiæ ministris in multis sacræ Scripturæ locis difficilioribus enodandis afferre poterat. Vtinam quis exstat, qui, quæ adhuc desiderantur, perficiat, qui operi colophonem addat, qui absolutum recognoscat, & in lucem ea dignitate edat, ac si ab authore ipso emendatum, recognitum & editum fuisset. Sed filios superstites pro singulari sua eruditione operam daturos speramus, ne hoc sacræ Scripturæ φωσφόρῳ Respublica literaria defraudetur, sed posthumus etiam suo tempore lucem aspiciat. Taceo nunc doctissimas Disputationes, quas ad singulas Synodos Maji adornavit, typis mandavit, publicè disputavit. Taceo alia scripta ejus Theologica ἀνέκδοτα, commentarios videlicet in Epistolas Pauli ad Romanos, ad Galatas, ad Colossenses, utramque ad Thessalonicenses, utramque ad Timotheum, ad Titum, ad Philemonem, & ad Hebræos; Orationes ejus Theologicas complures, Compendium sacræ Theologiæ Germanicum & Latinum.
units.tr: Nor did he serve the Church only by preaching and the School only by teaching, but he also greatly benefited both by writing, as his splendid writings, handed down to memory, most clearly attest. Some are theological, some philological and historical, some scholastic. Among his theological monuments I count the Roman Gospel, or two books on the remission of sins against papal indulgences, translated from French into German; an analysis of Psalm 110, on the priesthood of Christ according to the order of Melchizedek; the Hieroglyph of Christian doctrine; the Confession of Faith of James I, King of Great Britain, translated from English into German; several German treatises on Purgatory, on images, on the Roman Pope, that he is Antichrist, on the invocation of saints, on the indulgences of the Papists, and on the errors of the Schwenkfeldians; the archetypes of Gualther's homilies on Isaiah and on the festivals, which he corrected from the autograph, illustrated with notes and enlarged with an index; and Conrad Grasser's Royal Highway, or commentary on the Apocalypse of St John, which he edited after revising it, prefixing a dedicatory letter to James I, King of Great Britain. Above all, belonging to his theological works is the truly golden work, the Biblical Lexicon, which for many years he gathered with great zeal, care and labour, urged on by the request and confirmed by the recommendation of many very learned men. He arranged it in alphabetical order under the letters and resolved to make it public property, if a longer life had been granted him to enjoy it. In its preparation he came to the letter T, and stopped at the words TRIBULA and TRIBULATIO. Although he often meant to finish them, he was overcome by excessive tribulation and the force of a worsening illness, and carried off by an early death, so he could not bring it to completion. It is certainly to be lamented, and indeed greatly to be lamented, that so splendid, so useful and so necessary a work could not be finished, for it could bring great help to ministers in explaining many of the more difficult passages of Holy Scripture. Would that someone might exist who would complete what is still lacking, who would put the finishing touch on the work, who would revise the completed text and publish it in such dignity as if it had been emended, revised and published by the author himself. But we hope that his surviving sons will apply themselves with their singular learning, so that this light-bearer of Holy Scripture is not defrauded from the literary republic, but may also see the light in its own time, though posthumously. I now pass over his most learned disputations, which he prepared for each Synod in May, had printed, and publicly defended. I pass over his other theological writings, which remain unpublished: commentaries on the Epistles of Paul to the Romans, to the Galatians, to the Colossians, both to the Thessalonians, both to Timothy, to Titus, to Philemon and to the Hebrews; his several theological orations; and a compendium of sacred theology in German and Latin.

units.la: Non minorem vero commendationem merentur lucubrationes ejus Philologicæ & Historicæ. Cujusmodi sunt, Chronicon Stumpfii, quod summo studio, labore ac fide recensuit, & ab anno 1546. usque ad annum 1606. continuavit, addita descriptione tumultuum & bellorum Hungaricorum, Gallicorum, Belgicorum. Libri duo de antiquis Hebræorum, Chaldæorum & Syrorum numis, quorum S. Biblia & Rabbinorum scripta non raro meminerunt. Libri tres de antiquis mensuris Hebræorum, de quibus in sacra pagina mentio fit creberrima: quibus interspersæ sunt mensuræ Ægyptiorum, Arabum, Syrorum, Persarum, Græcorum & Romanorum. Mithridates Gesneri, quem recensuit & commentario illustravit. Descriptio vitæ & obitus Petri Martyris Vermilii Florentini, Theologi Tigurini, carmine Phalæcio comprehensa. Oratio panegyrica de ortu, vita & obitu clarissimi viri, Iohannis Guilielmi Stuckii, Theologi & antiquarii Tigurini, in Schola nostra anno 1608. recitata. Leonhardi Zubleri Tigurini opuscula Geometrica & Geodætica, à VVafero Latina civitate donata. Historia immanissimæ lanienæ & crudelitatis ab Hispanis, eorumque factioni addictis, per vallem Telinam anno 1620. mense Iulio patratæ. Epicedia, epitaphia, Epigrammata, Epithalamia, carminaque alia varia, in amicorum honores, gratulationem, συμπαθείας testificationem scripta, memoriæque prodita.
units.tr: His philological and historical labours deserve no less commendation. Of this kind are: Stumpf's Chronicle, which he revised with the greatest zeal, labour and fidelity, and continued from 1546 to 1606, adding a description of the Hungarian, French and Belgian tumults and wars; two books on the ancient coins of the Hebrews, Chaldeans and Syrians, which the Holy Scriptures and the writings of the rabbis not rarely mention; three books on the ancient measures of the Hebrews, which are very often mentioned in the sacred page, with the measures of the Egyptians, Arabs, Syrians, Persians, Greeks and Romans interspersed among them; Gesner's Mithridates, which he revised and illustrated with a commentary; a description of the life and death of Peter Martyr Vermigli of Florence, theologian of Zurich, comprised in Phalaecian verse; an oration in praise of the origin, life and death of that most distinguished man, John William Stuckius, theologian and antiquary of Zurich, delivered in our school in 1608; the geometrical and geodetic little works of Leonhard Zubler of Zurich, given Latin form by Wasser; a history of the most monstrous butchery and cruelty carried out by the Spaniards and those devoted to their faction through the Valtelline in July 1620; and epicedia, epitaphs, epigrams, epithalamia and various other poems, written in honour of friends, in congratulation, or as a testimony of sympathy, and handed down to memory.

units.la: Opuscula denique scholastica Scholæ nostræ reliquit & plurima, & utilissima. Inter quæ inprimis numerantur elementalia duo, alterum Hebraicum, Basileæ primum anno 1601. editum, & aliquoties Heydelbergæ recusum: Chaldaicum alterum, anno huius seculi undecimo in lucem emissum. Binæ Grammaticæ: Syra, quam primum edidit Lugduni Batavorum, anno millesimo quingentesimo nonagesimo tertio, & anno decimo nono seculi currentis recensuit, typisque ibidem secunda vice mandavit: Hebræa, anno millesimo sexcentesimo non tam ad lucem diurnam, quàm noctis lucernam composita. Institutiones Arithmeticæ, & tractatus de quadrato Geometrico cum figuris æneis. Monumenta ista omnia, documenta sunt evidentia, VVaserum fuisse singularis eruditionis, multæ lectionis, variæ variarum rerum cognitionis.
units.tr: Finally, he left our school many scholastic little works, and very useful ones. Among these are especially counted two elementary books, one in Hebrew, first published at Basel in 1601 and reprinted several times at Heidelberg, and the other in Chaldee, published in the eleventh year of this century. There are also two grammars: a Syriac one, which he first published at Leiden in 1593 and revised in 1619, having it printed a second time there; and a Hebrew one, composed in 1600, not so much for daylight as for the lamp of the night. He also wrote Arithmetical Institutions, and a treatise on the geometrical square with copper figures. All these monuments are clear evidence that Wasser was of singular learning, of wide reading, and of knowledge of many different subjects.

units.la: In disputationibus Synodalibus selectumferè instituit: Et ut antiquitatis Studiosissimus fuit, ita themata mixta, Historico-dogmatica elegit, cujusmodi sunt, de doctrina Catechetica; de versione Bibliorum in Linguas Vernaculas; Tetras Problematum de imaginibus; De Ecclesiæ ὑπαρξῆ, per omnia secula &c.
units.tr: In synodal disputations he generally arranged selected topics. And as he was most devoted to antiquity, so he chose mixed, historico-dogmatic theses, such as: on catechetical doctrine; on the translation of the Bible into the vernacular languages; a tetrad of problems on images; on the existence [ὑπαρξῆ] of the Church through all ages, and so on.

units.la: VVaserus, Caspar, Caspari nepos, Professor artium Rhetoro-Logicarum in Collegio Carolino clarissimus, Collega conjunctissimus, disputationes aliquot Philosophicas edidit, Isagogicas, tum mixtas etiam, qualis est de usu rationis in Theologia, &c.
units.tr: Wasser, Caspar, grandson of Caspar, a most distinguished professor of rhetoric and logic in the Carolinum college, and a very close colleague, published several philosophical disputations, introductory ones and also mixed ones, such as that on the use of reason in theology, and so on.

units.la: VVaserus, Iob. Henricus, Amplissimus Reipublicæ Tigurinæ Consul, rerum Helveticarum promus condus incomparabilis, βιβλιοθήκη εμψυχος. Nonnulla dedit antehac: Sed plura de Helvetia collegit volumina, Viri multis annis, publico nomine, occupatissimus, quàm multi alij, privati etiam & otiosi, legerint. Universæ Helvetiæ nomine optandum esset, ut vel primitias eorum, in consummatæ Historiæ domesticæ specimen, per concatenatas ejus curaspublicas habere possemus, quorum, si opus esset, locupletissima (loquor αὐτοπτης) ostendi possent horrea. Nec novum, nec præceps, nec tam meis, quàm publicis usibus hoc destinatum meum est votum!
units.tr: Wasser, John Henry, a most eminent consul of the Zurich commonwealth, an incomparable storehouse of Helvetian affairs, a living library [βιβλιοθήκη ἔμψυχος]. He has given out some things before, but he has gathered more volumes on Helvetia than many others, private and idle as well, have read, for he has been for many years occupied with public business on behalf of the state. For the whole of Helvetia it would be desirable that we might have at least the first fruits of these collections, as a specimen of a completed domestic history, linked together through his public care. If need were, I could show their very rich granaries (I speak as an eyewitness) [αὐτόπτης]. My wish is neither new nor rash, and it is intended not so much for my own uses as for public ones!

units.la: Verdmyllerus, Otto, Tigurinus Professor Ethices & Ecclesiæ Collegiatæ Archidiaconus ab an. Chr. 1547. ad 1551. quo vivere desijt. Scripsit de dignitate, usu & Methodo Philosophiæ moralis, quam Aristoteles ad Nicomachum scripsit lib.2.Basil.1545. Commentarium perquam eruditum in Orationem Ciceronis ad Equites Romanos, antequam iret in exilium: prodijt, sub nomine Myliandri Tigurini, Basil.1549. una cum aliorum lucubrationibus in omnes Orationes Ciceronis, & Parisijs seorsim 1540. Tiguri item ex recognitione auctoris & Basileæ 1553. Idem scripsit de officio concionatoris Christiani sermones. 3. De justificatione libros edidit. 4. Hoc profecto scripto obtinuisse videtur, ut alibi non immerito à nobis scholasticus Reformatus fuerit appellatus. Scripsit & Summam Christianæ fidei: Libellum de morte: de afflictionibus. Ejusdem est liber de similitudinibus ab animantibus desumtus, impressus Tiguri: Alius item de bonis operibus. 1551. Meminit & Frisius commentariorum ejus in Epistolam ad Galatas ἀνεκδότων. Habeo multas ejusdem Epistolas manuscriptas, & Aureoli partem Latinè translatum. Vir & laboriosus fuit, & judiciosus.
units.tr: Otto Verdmyller, Tigurine professor of ethics and archdeacon of the collegiate church, from 1547 until 1551, when he ceased to live. He wrote on the dignity, use and method of moral philosophy, which Aristotle addressed to Nicomachus, book 2, Basel 1545. He also wrote a very learned commentary on Cicero's oration to the Roman knights, delivered before he went into exile. It appeared under the name Myliander of Zürich, Basel 1549, together with other men's works on all of Cicero's orations, and separately at Paris in 1540, and also at Zürich, revised by the author, and at Basel in 1553. The same man wrote sermons on the office of the Christian preacher, three in number, and published books on justification, four in number. Indeed, by this writing he seems to have earned, not undeservedly, the title "Reformed scholastic" from us elsewhere. He also wrote a Summa of the Christian faith, a little book on death, and one on afflictions. Of his too is a book on similitudes drawn from animals, printed at Zürich, and another on good works, 1551. Frisius also mentions his unpublished [ἀνέκδοτα] commentaries on the Epistle to the Galatians. I have many of his letters in manuscript, and a part of Aureolus translated into Latin. He was also a hard-working and judicious man.

units.la: VVirzius Iohannes, Ecclesiæ & Scholæ Tigurinæ Minister meritissimus: Ex Collegij Abbatissani Inspectore Gregi Vitodurano præficitur, indeque domum revocatus in Collegio Carolino Spartam Rhetorologici ab an. Ch. 1639. Theologi vero 1652. ad 1659. magna cum laude exornavit. Ut vir diffusæ fuit eruditionis, ita vix ullum est literaturæ genus, quod per ingenij sui ubertatem juvare scriptis publicis non potuerit. Testes sunt:
units.tr: Johannes Wirzius, a most deserving minister of the Church and school of Zürich. He was placed over the flock at Vitodurum as inspector of the Abbess's college, and afterwards, recalled home, he adorned the Carolinum college with great distinction: as lecturer in rhetoric from 1639, and as professor of theology from 1652 to 1659. As he was a man of wide learning, there is hardly any branch of literature that his talent, which was so fertile, could not help with his public writings. The witnesses to this are:

units.la: 1. Conciones ipsius in c.15. Lucæ & Festalex annexæ. 2. Scriptum Apologeticum, contra Iesuitam Forerum, quo & Bullingeri libellus, Expostulatio Dei cum Helvetijs, & ipsa Reformata religio docte vindicatur. 3. Disputationes variæ Synodales præsertim Theologicæ, cujusmodi sunt, Quæstiones miscellaneæ Theologicæ, Ennucleatio Ioh.14.6. Delineatio loci Paulini,1. Cor.4. de munere Ecclesiastico: De Ecclesia, ex 1.Tim. 3.15. Emblema Theologicum ex Apocalypsi: de invocatione religiosa: De juramento: Demonstratio, Iesum Christum unicum N.T. esse Pontificem: de Communione Sanctorum: An ex Oratione Dominica probari possit, hodiernam Religionem Pontificiam esse veram: De Apostolo Petro: De ementito in omnibus fidei dogmatibus Romanæ Ecclesiæ Doctorum consensu: De bonis operibus: Piæ conversi latronis preces, vindicatæ à figmento ignis purgatorii. Paulò antè obitum brevi disputatione, Salve Irenicum D. Danhavveri perstrinxit. Venæ poeticæ felicitatem & facilitatem varia ejus commenta carmina, edita multa, plura apud amicos deposita. Scripsit etiam rudimenta Prosodica: Systema Rhetoricæ Ecclesiasticæ accuratissimum, Metaphysicum: Gymnasium Logicum, Observationes Philosophicas, quæ etiamnum, etsi manu tantum descripta, Studiosorum teruntur manibus. Disputationes philosophicæ vel ab ipso conscriptæ, vel sub ejusdem præsidio habitæ adhuc in recenti sunt memoria, cujusmodi sunt Positiones de Natura Philosophiæ; de ejus Definitione, genere, objecto & fine: de Logica Theologiæ regno non proscribenda: de causis : de Prædicamentis, de Testimonio divino: ὁμολογία: Positiones Logicæ: Positiones de Propositione propria & impropria: De sensuum testimonio: de Circulo Logico: Positiones de Cælo. Sed & Orationes publicas & multas habuit, & doctas, quæ luce dignissimæ, meo judicio, essent.
units.tr: 1. His own sermons on chapter 15 of Luke, and the Festal Lexicon appended to them. 2. An apologetic writing against the Jesuit Forer, in which both Bullinger's little book, Expostulatio Dei cum Helvetiis, and the Reformed religion itself are learnedly vindicated. 3. Various disputations, chiefly synodal and theological, of which kinds are: Miscellaneous Theological Questions; an Unfolding of John 14:6; an Outline of the Pauline passage, 1 Cor. 4, on the ecclesiastical office; On the Church, from 1 Tim. 3:15; A Theological Emblem from the Apocalypse; On religious invocation; On the oath; A Demonstration that Jesus Christ alone is the High Priest of the New Testament; On the communion of the saints; Whether it can be proved from the Lord's Prayer that the present Papist religion is true; On the Apostle Peter; On the lie that the doctors of the Roman Church agree in all the dogmas of faith; On good works; The prayers of the pious converted thief, vindicated from the fiction of purgatorial fire. Shortly before his death, in a brief disputation, he took apart Salve Irenicum of Dannhauer. The happiness and facility of his poetic vein is shown by his various poems, many of which were published and more of which were deposited with friends. He also wrote elementary prosody, a most accurate Systema of ecclesiastical rhetoric, a Metaphysical Gymnasium, a Logical Gymnasium, and Philosophical Observations, which, though still only in manuscript, are handled by students. Philosophical disputations, either composed by himself or held under his presidency, are still fresh in memory, such as: Theses on the nature of philosophy; on its definition, genus, object and end; on logic, not to be banned from the realm of theology; on causes; on the predicaments; on divine testimony; [ὁμολογία] Confession; Logical Theses; Theses on the proper and improper proposition; On the testimony of the senses; On the logical circle; Theses on heaven. He also gave many public orations, and learned ones, which in my judgment would be most worthy of publication.

units.la: Wirzius Iob. Conradus Verbi Dei Minister, in agro primum Durgæo, Kessvilæ & Nuforæ; postea in Tigurino Birmenstorfij in urbe denique Ædis Petrinæ Diaconus ab an. Chr. 1645. ad 1648. quo, Templi ad Sp S Anstitium, ei demandatum est. Conciones aliquot, ut vir est facundissimus, edidit: anniversarias præsertim, id est, integri anni cursum exhibentes: Quæstiones item Catecheticas, majoribus per annum solennitatibus potissimum destinatas.
units.tr: Johann Conrad Wirzius, minister of the Word of God, first in the rural district of Thurgau, at Kessweil and Nussfort; afterwards in the Zürich territory at Birmensdorf; and finally, in the city, as deacon of St Peter's church, from 1645 to 1648, when the charge of the Temple of the Holy Spirit was committed to him. As he is a most eloquent man, he published several sermons, especially anniversary sermons, that is, those setting out the course of a whole year, and also catechetical questions, chiefly intended for the greater festivals of the year.

units.la: Wolfius Caspar, Medicus Tigurinus, Iohannis frater, Georgij Cellarij Collega: uterque in Professione Gesneri Physica successor 1566. postea Græcæ Linguæ, defuncto Collino, Interpres 1578. tum Gesneri plurima ἀνέκδοτα disposuit, & ad prælum paravit, tum vero ipse non pauca elaboravit. Nam ut hæres fuit non Professionis tantum, & laborum etiam Gesnerianorum, ita totum illud corollarium, quod Frisius appellat, in Bibliotheca Gesneriana, apud eundem fuit depositum. Inseremus illud, ceu mantissam eorum, quæ supra de Gesnero commemoravimus. Enchiridion, inquit, medicæ triplicis, illius primum quæ signa ex pulsibus & urinis dijudicat. Deinde Therapeuticæ de omni morborum genere curando sigillatim. Tertio Diæteticæ vel de ratione victus, præsertim in febribus. Hoc volumine continentur, De pulsibus libellus ex Galeni libris collectus, ac veluti in formulam redactus, authore quidem incerto, sed diligentissimo doctissimoque. De judicijs urinarum tractatus ex probatissimis collectus authoribus, & in tabulæ formam confectus, adjectis etiam causis, quæ hæc vel illam urinam reddant, Ioan. Vasseo Melden. authore. Morborum internorum prope omnium curatio, brevi methodo comprehensa ex Galeno præcipue & Mar. Gattinaria, per Iacobum Sylvium Medicum selecta. De ratione victus in febribus secundum Hippocratem, in genere & singillatim lib. 3. authore Brudo Lusitano medico. Præfatio Conr. Gesneri ad Achillem. P. Gassarum medicum. Liber impressus Tiguri per Andream Gesnerum F. & Iacobum Gesnerum fratres anno 1555. in 8. Chartis 59. semis. Conr. Gesneri de anima liber sententiosa brevitate, veluti per tabulas & Aphorismos ut plurimum conscriptus: Philosophiæ & Medicinæ Studiosis accommodatus. Impressus Tiguri apud Iac. Gesnerum 1563. in 8. Chartis 15. De omni rerum fossilium genere, gemmis, lapidibus, metallis & hujusmodi, libri aliquot, plerique nunc primum editi. Ioan. Kentmanni Dresdensis Medici Nomenclaturæ rerum fossilium, quæ in Misnia præcipue & aliis quoque regionibus inveniuntur. Ejusdem calculorum, qui in corpore ac membris hominum innascuntur, genera 12. depicta, descriptaque cum Historijs. De metallicis rebus ac nominibus, observationes variæ ex schedis Georgij Fabricij. Henrici Gesneri bellij medici de Succino lib. 2 prior Theologicus, posterior Physicus & medicus cum corollario C. Gesneri. Valerij Cordi de Halosantho, seu ipermate ceti cum corollario C. Gesneri S Epiphanij Episcopi Cypri, de 12. gemmis, quæ erant in veste Aronis liber Græcus & Latinus, cum corollario C. Gesneri. F. Ruel medici Insulani, de gemmis aliquot, ijs præsertim, quarum Ioan. in Apocalypsi meminit, & alijs, quarum usus hodie apud omnes percrebuit, lib. 2. Theologis nonminus utiles, quàm Philosophis. C. Gesneri de rerum fossilium, lapidum & gemmarum maximè, similitudinibus & figuris libris non solùm medicis, sed omnibus rerum naturæ & Philologiæ Studiosis utilis ac jucundus, omnia simul impressa Tiguri, apud Iacobum Gesnerum anno D. 1565. in 8. chartis 67. Ευπορίστα Ped. Dioscordis Anazarbæi ad Andromachum, h. e. de curationibus morborum per medicamenta paratu facilia lib. 2. Græcè & Latinè, partim à Ioanne Moibano Medico Augustano, partim vero post hujus mortem à C. Gesnero in Linguam Latinam conversi, adjectis, ab utroque interprete, Symphonijs Galeni, aliorumque Græcorum medicorum. Argentinæ excudit Iosias Richelius, anno 1565. in char: 62. Iod. VWillichii Magirica emendavit & edidit Tiguri. Moschionis de affectibus mulierum, liber impressus Basileæ apud Guarinum, à Gasparo VVolphio editus. Euonymi seu de remediis secretis pars secunda, edita à Gasparo VVolphio Tiguri apud Frosch-houerum 1569. Hic etiam in Germanicam Linguam translatus est per D. Ioan. Iacobum Nuschelerum medicum. Epistolarum medicinalium Gesneri editi sunt libri tres, per Gasparum VVolphium. Itemque Oxymelitis elleborati descriptio & usus: una cum ejusdem de Aconiti primi assertione, ab eodem. Præterea quàm plurimos Græcos & Latinos authores partim emendavit, partim Scholiis illustravit: Poëtas quidem Græcos, Nicandrum, Orpheum, Aratum, Sophoclem, Euripidem, Hesiodum, Musæum, Dionysium Q. Calabrum, Coluthum, Tryphiodorum, Sibyllina oracula. Medicos, Aretæum, cujus etiam capita quædam manuscripta asservantur in Bibliotheca Gesneri: Veterinariæ Medicinæ libros P. Ægenetam, Simeonem Sethi, Celsum Avicennam, Nicolaum Alexandrinum. Alios quoque authores emendavit, & quidem diligentissimè, Athenæi Dipnosophistas. Scriptores rei rusticæ. Stobæi sententias: Item Antonii & maximi Monachi, quos Stobæo conjunxit. Iulii Pollucis onomasticum. Servantur & in ejusdem Bibliotheca libri nondum editi Præterea Demetrij Constantinopolitani de nutritione & cura accipitrum, lib. 2. De canibus lib. 1, Græcè Epiphanij quædam Græca manuscripta. Petri de Musandinis de cibis & potibus præparandis pro infirmis. Alexander Seitz de Thermis & modo lavandi. Qua verò jam Methodo & serie ipse Wolphius vel suas, vel Gesneri meditationes luci publicæ exposuerit, videamus: Edidit ergo viaticum novum, de omnium ferè particularium morborum curatione, auctoris incerti. Id tamen postea quidam, Hollerij esse docuit, simul falsò & in humaniter VVolphium accusans, quasi ejus rei conscius, sibi alienum laborem vendicare voluisset, verum hic vicisim, Apologia publicata, calumnias hasce refutavit. Tiguri excudit Frofchouerus in 8. Harmoniam Gynaeceorum, ex Cleopatrae, Prisciani, Moschionis & incerti cujusdam muliebrium libris, concinnatam: superfluis ac repetitis omnibus recisis. Moschionis, Medici Graeci, recentioris, de passionibus mulierum librum Graecum, Gesneri opera emendatum. Librum, de aquis, oleis, salibus, & lapide Philosophorum, sub nomine ficto Diodori Euchyontis de Polychimia, ex Germanico libro innominati auctoris in Latinum sermonem convertit, addita praefatione, de chymicae artis praestantia & commendatione, Tiguri in 8. Edidit etiam Euonymi partem secundam Thesauri, a Gesnero concinnatam. Addita est huic Apologia, de viatici novi editione, ad titubantem Antonii Valerii Linguam. Tiguri apud Frofchouerum in 8. Hypolchefin, seu pollicitationem Historiae stirpium Conr. Gesneri. Impressam in 4. cum vita Gesneri. Epistolarum medicinalium, Conr. Gesneri lib. 3. in 4. Anno 77. Ejusdem Gesneri, Aconiti primi Dioscoridis asseveratio. De Oxymelit s Elleborati utriusque descriptione & usu, libellum. Emendationes novas in Sereni Poetae, & Medici librum, de morborum curatione una cum indice quintuplici, Epithetorum, & morborum, aliarumque rerum, quibus idem author est usus, Alphabethum Empiricum, sive Dioscoridis & Stephani Atheniensis Philosophorum & Medicorum, de remediis expertis librum e Graeco Latinum fecit. Anno 1581. Quin & in eundem authorem, qui Graece manuscriptus ab eo asservatur, annotationes scripsit, nondum editas. Editioni praeterea paravit, Dominici Vincentini Arcignanei, de ponderibus & mensuris medicinalibus lib. 3. Ex Graecis Arabicis, & Latinis rei medicae scriptoribus diligentissime conscriptos, non Medicis modo, sed omnibus literarum Linguarumque Studiosis perutiles futuros: Ante annos sexaginta in Italia primum editus, nunc vero ab innumeris mendis C. Gesneri opera, repurgatus. Huic & alia ejusdem argumenti opuscula variorum authorum sunt adjecta. Inprimis vero Iosiae Simleri Tigurini, vocabula rei nummariae, ponderum, & mensurarum, Graeca, Latina, Hebraica, Arabica, ex diversis authoribus collecta, & in ordinem Alphabethicum disposita. Item Conr. Gesneri de ponderibus & mensuris variaeque observationes, tabulae praesertim ita dispositae, ut quae sint majoris ponderis semper praecedant, tum liquidorum, tum aridorum, & alia prius ita non edita. Itemque Alphabethica Caspari VVolphij est enumeratio virorum illustrium, qui de ponderum & mensurarum doctrina, vel integros libros aut tractatus, vel obiter tantum in suis libris scripserunt. Aphorismorum Hippocratis methodum novam, partim Achillis P.Gasseri viri doctissimi opera, partim Conr. Gesneri emendationibus illustratam, praefixa omnium Aphorismorum tabula, propediem in lucem edendam, una cum Catalogo eorum omnium, qui tum in Aphorismos, tum caeteros omnes Hippocratis libros, aliquid laude dignum scripserunt, Casp. VVolphii opera collecta habet praeterea in manibus, quos jam pene absolvit Conr. Gessneri Physicarum meditationum lib. 4. vel 5. quorum primus est de principijs, natura, causis, motu, infinito, tempore &c. Secundus de cælo & meteoris: Tertius de anima. Quartus continet scholia & annotationes in aliquot Aristotelis libros quos de naturalibus rebus scripsit, ut in libros meteororum, de anima, & nonnullos parvorum naturalium. His accedet 5. variarum meditationum: in quo multa Theologicè, Ethicè, Dialecticè, Grammaticè &c. erudite & subtiliter proponuntur. Habet praeterea & alia, ut de experimentis paratu facilibus librum, partim ex nonnullis impressis, partim nunquam prius impressis, in unam methodum redactum. Partitiones Medicas maxima ex parte absolutas, quae paulatim, Domino sic adjuvante prodibunt. Haec ex ultima Bibliotheca Gessneriana editione. Hodie adhuc ab haeredibus ejus asservantur aliquot volumina, cujusmodi sunt: Onomasticii Medici Barbari ordine Alphabethico conscripti volumina duo in sol. quibus Arabica, Persica, Syriaca, Hebraica item Graeca aliaque Barbara vocabulari quae apud Arabes, aliosque Medicos occurrunt, diversorum authoritate, aut corriguntur explicantur. Antidotum practicum, omnes corporis morbos secundum locos & Genera, ad usum Medicum practicum accommodatum, voluminibus septem in sol. comprehensum & distinctum. Volumina tria in sol. quorum primum agit, de dolore capitis, oculorum, aurium &c. Secundum Pectoris remedia varia. Ventriculi item, Hepatis, Splenis &c. Tertium de Calculo renum, vesicae, genitalibus utriusque sexus. Συνοψις πραγματων practica in cepta an. 1559. Ejusdem practica ab an. 1592. Varia consilia Medica diligenter conscripta: Tomus in 4. In libros Aphorismorum Hippocratis, Excepta à Ludovico Dureto. Variarum lectionum liber scriptus Parisiis in 4. De simplicium Medicamentorum facultatibus, excepta manu propria Parisiis, ex ore Ioh. Montani. Alia quàm plurima Manuscripta ejusdem extant, quę partim incuria quadam perierunt, partim imperfecta. Sunt habeo & ego quaedam Επιτομαι ejus, tum in Academijs excepta, tum proprio Marte eompofita.
units.tr: Wolfius Caspar, Zurich physician, brother of Johannes and colleague of Georg Keller. Both succeeded Gesner in the professorship of natural philosophy in 1566. Afterwards, when Collinus died, Caspar became Greek lecturer in 1578. He then arranged and prepared for the press a great many of Gesner's unpublished works [ἀνέκδοτα], and he himself produced not a few works of his own. For he was heir not only to Gesner's professorship and his scholarly labours, but also to the whole appendix that Frisius calls the Corollary, which was deposited with him in the Gesner Library. I shall insert it here as a supplement to what we have already recorded above about Gesner. The Handbook of Medicine, he says, is threefold: first, the part that judges diseases by pulses and urine; second, the therapeutics, treating the cure of every kind of disease one by one; third, dietetics, or the regimen of diet, especially in fevers. This volume contains: a little book on pulses, gathered from the books of Galen and reduced to a kind of formula, by an author who is unknown but very diligent and learned; a treatise on the judgment of urine, compiled from the most approved authors and arranged in the form of a table, with the causes added that make this or that urine, by Johannes Vassaeus of Melun; a method, briefly summarised, for curing almost all internal diseases, chosen by Jacobus Sylvius, a physician, mainly from Galen and Marcus Gattinara; on the regimen of diet in fevers according to Hippocrates, in general and in particular, book 3, by Bruto the Lusitanian physician; and a preface by Konrad Gesner to Achilles Gasser, physician. The book was printed at Zurich by Andreas Gesner, son, and Jacob Gesner, brothers, in the year 1555, in octavo, with fifty-nine and a half leaves. Konrad Gesner's book On the Soul, written in pithy sentences and for the most part set out in tables and aphorisms, is suited to students of philosophy and medicine. It was printed at Zurich by Jacob Gesner in 1563, in octavo, with fifteen leaves. Several books On Every Kind of Fossil Thing, on gems, stones, metals and such like, most of them now published for the first time: Johannes Kentmann of Dresden, physician, Nomenclature of Fossils, which are found especially in Meissen and in other regions as well; by the same author, twelve kinds of stones that are born in the body and limbs of humans, depicted and described along with their histories; various observations on metallic things and names, from the notes of Georg Fabricius; Henrich Gesner's two books on amber by the physician Bellius, the first theological, the second physical and medical, with a corollary by C. Gesner; Valerius Cordus's On Halosanthus, or the sperm of the whale, with a corollary by C. Gesner; the Greek and Latin book of Saint Epiphanius, bishop of Cyprus, on the twelve gems that were in Aaron's vestment, with a corollary by C. Gesner; F. Ruel, physician of Insulae, two books on some gems, especially those which John mentions in the Apocalypse, and others whose use is now widespread among everyone, useful to theologians no less than to philosophers; C. Gesner's book on the similarities and figures of fossils, stones and especially gems, useful and pleasant not only to physicians but to all students of nature and philology. All these were printed together at Zurich by Jacob Gesner in the year of our Lord 1565, in octavo, with sixty-seven leaves. Euporista [Εὐπορίστα] of Pedanius Dioscorides of Anazarbus, to Andromachus, that is, on the cure of diseases by remedies easily prepared, two books, in Greek and Latin, partly translated into Latin by Johannes Moibanus, physician of Augsburg, and partly, after his death, by C. Gesner. To each translation have been added the Symphonies of Galen and of other Greek physicians, by both translators. Printed at Strasbourg by Josias Rihel in 1565, with sixty-two leaves. Johann Wilhelm's Magirica, corrected and published at Zurich. Moschion's book On the Diseases of Women, printed at Basel by Guarinus, edited by Caspar Wolf. The second part of Euonymus, or On Secret Remedies, edited by Caspar Wolf at Zurich by Frosch-hauer in 1569. This too was translated into German by Dr. Johann Jacob Nuschelerus, physician. Three books of Gesner's Medical Letters were edited by Caspar Wolf, and likewise the description and use of Oxymel of Hellebore, together with his own assertion concerning the first Aconite. Besides, he has emended, partly, and partly illustrated with scholia, very many Greek and Latin authors: among the Greek poets, Nicander, Orpheus, Aratus, Sophocles, Euripides, Hesiod, Musaeus, Dionysius Calaber, Coluthus, Tryphiodorus, and the Sibylline oracles. Among the medical writers, Aretaeus, some chapters of whom are also preserved in manuscript in the Gesner Library; the veterinary books of Paulus Aegineta, Simeon Seth, Celsus, Avicenna, and Nicolaus Alexandrinus. He has also emended, and that very diligently, other authors: the Deipnosophists of Athenaeus, the writers on agriculture, the Sayings of Stobaeus, likewise Antonius and Maximus the monk, whom he joined to Stobaeus, and the Onomasticon of Julius Pollux. In the same library are preserved books not yet published. Besides these, Demetrius of Constantinople, on the feeding and care of hawks, two books; on dogs, one book; some Greek writings of Epiphanius in manuscript; Peter of Musandinis on preparing foods and drinks for the sick; Alexander Seitz on baths and the manner of bathing. But let us see in what method and order Wolf himself has brought his own or Gesner's reflections to the public light. He therefore published a New Viaticum, on the cure of almost all particular diseases, by an unknown author. Yet afterwards a certain man showed that it was by Holler, falsely accusing Wolf at the same time and inhumanly, as if he, being aware of the matter, had wished to claim for himself another's labour. In turn, Wolf, having published an Apology, refuted these calumnies. Printed at Zurich by Frosch-hauer, in octavo. A Harmony of Gynaecology, compiled from the books on women by Cleopatra, Priscian, Moschion, and a certain unknown author, with all superfluous and repeated matter cut out. The Greek book on the diseases of women by Moschion, a more recent Greek physician, emended by the work of Gesner. A book on waters, oils, salts, and the stone of the philosophers, published under the fictitious name of Diodorus Euchyon, On Polychymia, he turned into Latin from a German book by an anonymous author, with a preface added on the excellence and commendation of the chymical art; at Zurich, in octavo. He also edited the second part of the Treasury of Euonymus, put together by Gesner. To this was added an Apology concerning the edition of the New Viaticum, directed against the wavering tongue of Antonius Valerius. At Zurich, by Frosch-hauer, in octavo. The Hypolchefin, or the promise of the History of Plants by Conrad Gesner, printed in quarto with the life of Gesner. Gesner's Medical Letters, three books, in quarto, in the year 1577. By the same Gesner, the assertion on the first Aconite of Dioscorides. A little book on the description and use of both kinds of Oxymel of Hellebore. New emendations to the book of the poet and physician Serenus On the Cure of Diseases, together with a fivefold index of epithets, diseases, and other things, which the same author uses. The Empirical Alphabet, that is, a book of Dioscorides and Stephanus of Athens, philosophers and physicians, On Tried Remedies, which he made into Latin from the Greek, in the year 1581. He also wrote annotations, not yet published, on the same author, which are preserved by him in manuscript in Greek. He has also prepared for publication three books of Domenico Vincentini Arcignano, On Medicinal Weights and Measures, most carefully compiled from Greek, Arabic, and Latin writers on medical matters, and useful not only to physicians but to all students of letters and languages. First published in Italy sixty years ago, but now cleansed of countless errors by the work of C. Gesner. To this have been added other little works of various authors on the same subject. Above all, the words of monetary matters, of weights and measures, in Greek, Latin, Hebrew, and Arabic, collected by Josias Simler of Zurich from various authors and arranged in alphabetical order. Likewise Konrad Gesner's On Weights and Measures and various observations, especially tables so arranged that those of greater weight always come first, both for liquids and for dry things, and other things not previously published in this way. Likewise the alphabetical list by Caspar Wolf of illustrious men who wrote on the doctrine of weights and measures, either whole books or treatises, or only in passing in their own books. He also has in hand, collected by his labour, a new method of the Aphorisms of Hippocrates, partly illustrated by the work of the most learned Achilles Gasser, partly by the emendations of Konrad Gesner, with a table of all the Aphorisms prefixed, to be published shortly, together with a catalogue of all those who have written anything praiseworthy either on the Aphorisms or on all the other books of Hippocrates. Konrad Gesner's Physical Meditations, four or five books, which are now almost finished, the first of which concerns principles, nature, causes, motion, the infinite, time, and so on; the second, on heaven and meteors; the third, on the soul; the fourth contains scholia and annotations on several books of Aristotle which he wrote on natural things, such as the books Meteorology, On the Soul, and some of the Parva Naturalia. To these will be added a fifth book of Various Meditations, in which many matters are set forth learnedly and subtly in theology, ethics, dialectic, grammar, and so on. He has besides other things, such as a book on experiments easily performed, partly drawn from printed sources, partly never printed before, reduced to one method. Medical Partitions, for the most part finished, which will gradually appear, the Lord so helping. These things are from the last edition of the Gesner Library. Today some volumes are still kept by his heirs, of which these are examples: two folio volumes of a Barbarian medical Onomasticon, written in alphabetical order, in which the Arabic, Persian, Syriac, Hebrew, likewise Greek and other barbarous words that occur among the Arabs and other physicians are corrected and explained by the authority of various writers. A Practical Antidotary, treating all diseases of the body according to their places and kinds, adapted for practical medical use, comprised and distributed in seven folio volumes. Three folio volumes, of which the first deals with pain of the head, the eyes, the ears, and so on; the second with various remedies for the chest, likewise the stomach, liver, spleen, and so on; the third with stone of the kidneys and bladder and the genitals of both sexes.
